W7220654752.title: Synthesis and characterization of Parthenium hysterophorus-derived biochar supported titanium dioxide-polyvinyl alcohol ternary composite hydrogel for efficient removal of textile dye

W7220667958.abstract: ABSTRACT Regulating polymer‐chain entanglement provides a powerful route to high‐performance sustainable bioplastics. However, achieving dense entanglement in ultrahigh‐molecular‐weight polymers remains difficult because long chain lengths and strong intramolecular interactions suppress interchain interpenetration, ultimately limiting mechanical performance. Here we introduce a gradual concentration‐regulation strategy that progressively amplifies trapped entanglements, followed by photochemical crosslinking to preserve the entangled state within a robust multinetwork architecture. The resulting bioplastics combine mechanical properties that surpass those of conventionally processed counterparts and approach those of commercial plastics, while maintaining high mechanical stability, environmental adaptability, and on‐demand degradability under mild conditions. As a proof of concept, we integrate these materials into soft electronic devices capable of emotion‐responsive sensing and remote actuation. These devices are fully transient, enabling programmed degradation via enzymatic or chemical pathways over timescales ranging from hours to months, thereby addressing end‐of‐life disposal challenges. This work establishes a scalable and broadly applicable strategy for engineering high‐performance sustainable polymer systems for advanced materials and bioelectronic applications.
W7220667958.title: Gradual Concentration‐Regulated Entanglement Enables Tough and Strong Sustainable Bioplastics

W7220680870.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable, biodegradable polymers are in increasing demand to address the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Here, bio‐based poly(butylene succinate‐co‐sebacate) (PBSSe) copolyesters are synthesized via two‐step melt polycondensation using succinic and sebacic acids as co‐monomers—with varying molar ratios (10:0, 8:2, 6:4, 4:6, 2:8, and 0:10)—with 1,4‐butanediol. Their chemical structure, thermal behavior, mechanical properties, and biodegradability are systematically investigated. Sebacic acid, a long‐chain aliphatic diacid, improves flexibility, thermal stability, and biodegradability. All PBSSe compositions exhibit a single melting transition and effective degradation under both home‐composting and soil conditions. PBSSe with 20 mol% of sebacic acid exhibits 37% higher tensile strength, 162% higher elongation at break, and superior degradability than commercial poly(butylene succinate‐co‐adipate) (PBSA), while maintaining favorable thermal properties, including a melting temperature of 93°C, T onset of 387°C, and crystallinity of 30%, which are comparable or superior to those of PBSA. Thus, 20 mol% sebacic acid incorporation provides an effective balance between mechanical performance, thermal stability, and biodegradation behavior in poly(butylene succinate)‐based copolyesters. These results highlight the potential of PBSSe 8:2 as a promising bio‐based alternative to petroleum‐derived PBSA for flexible packaging applications requiring superior mechanical performance, thermal resistance, and environmental compatibility.
W7220680870.title: Synthesis and Characterization of Bio‐Based Poly(Butylene Succinate‐Co‐Sebacate): A Sustainable Alternative to Petroleum‐Based Polyesters

W7220684316.title: Dual-parameter aeration control improves post-anoxic denitrification by limiting aerobic depletion of biomass-associated carbon pools

W7220710774.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates are biodegradable microbial polyesters considered promising alternatives to petroleum-based plastics. However, the development of sustainable end-of-life strategies for polyhydroxyalkanoates requires the identification of efficient depolymerising enzymes. Here, an extracellular short-chain-length PHA depolymerase, termed Cf PhaZ, was identified through metagenomic mining of polyester-enriched microbiomes. The enzyme was assigned to a Cellulosimicrobium funkei metagenome-assembled genome and expressed in Escherichia coli . Cf PhaZ shows the canonical architecture of extracellular PHA depolymerases. Biophysical analyses demonstrated that the enzyme adopts a monomeric α/β-fold structure with a melting temperature of 54 °C. The hydrolytic activity of Cf PhaZ toward poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) was validated by zymographic and spot-test assays and quantitatively characterised through direct HPLC-based quantification of 3-hydroxybutyrate release. Cf PhaZ displayed optimal activity at pH 6.5 and 40 °C, while maintaining prolonged thermostability under mesophilic conditions. Fluorescence-based adsorption assays demonstrated a strong interaction between the enzyme and the substrate surface. Kinetic analyses were performed using both conventional and inverse Michaelis-Menten approaches, and a surface-area-based kinetic framework was implemented to better describe the heterogeneous nature of polymer hydrolysis. Furthermore, Cf PhaZ efficiently degraded industrially relevant bioplastic films, reaching up to 40% conversion into soluble monomers. Overall, this study expands the current knowledge of extracellular PHA depolymerases from Gram-positive bacteria and highlights the potential of Cf PhaZ for enzymatic recycling and upcycling of biodegradable plastics.
W7220710774.title: A PHA depolymerase from Cellulosimicrobium funkei: Discovery, biochemical characterisation and plastic degradation

W7220716387.title: Sustainable polyhydroxybutyrate production and characterization from Chlorella vulgaris cultivated on waste-derived carbon sources

W7220723495.abstract: ABSTRACT Polylactic acid (PLA) is a bio‐based and biodegradable polymer, but its inherent brittleness limits its applications requiring high deformation capability. In this study, thermoplasticized bamboo flour was developed as a biomass‐derived deformable modifier for PLA through long‐chain fatty acid esterification. Among the modified products, decanoic acid‐modified delignified bamboo flour (DBF‐C10) showed the most favorable thermoplastic processability, with an elongation at break of approximately 160%. PLA/DBF‐C10 blends containing 10–50 wt% DBF‐C10 were prepared by melt processing, and their structure, thermal properties, mechanical properties, and fracture behavior were investigated. FTIR and 13 C‐NMR confirmed the coexistence of PLA and DBF‐C10 after processing without new covalent bond formation. Increasing DBF‐C10 content decreased the crystallinity and slightly reduced the glass transition temperature of the PLA phase, while the melting temperature remained nearly unchanged. Although tensile strength and storage modulus decreased, the elongation at break of TPLA‐50 was approximately twice that of neat PLA. DMA and SEM revealed that DBF‐C10 facilitated deformation and crack propagation through interfacial debonding, fibrous drawing, plastic deformation, and crack deflection. These results demonstrate the potential of thermoplasticized bamboo flour as a deformable biomass modifier for toughening PLA.
W7220723495.title: Fatty Acid Esterification of Bamboo Flour Toward Thermoplastic Biomass‐Based Toughening of Polylactic Acid

W7220732377.abstract: Introduction . A tissue-engineered vascular implant based on a biodegradable polymer scaffold may become an alternative to modern vascular prostheses, because it is free from such shortcomings as low patency rates in small-diameter vascular reconstructions, infection risks, and the absence of aged-related adaptive changes in the recipient’s body. Objective . Staged research and evaluation of the tissue-engineered vascular implant based on a combined polymer scaffold in a long-term chronic in vivo experiment. Materials and Methods . A two-layer bioresorbable scaffold was obtained by electrospinning from poly(Llactide) and poly(ε-caprolactone) fibers. The microstructure (scanning electron microscopy, Supra 55VP-32-49, Carl Zeiss), mechanical properties (Instron 5943 testing machine) and biocompatibility (MTT test) of the samples were studied. At the first stage, the scaffold was implanted into the abdominal aorta of Wistar rats (n=25); the follow-up periods were 1 month (n=3), 2 months (n=4), 3 months (n=6), 6 months (n=6), 12 months (n=2), 18 months (n=2), 24 months (n=2). At the second stage, the posterior vena cava of a Papio hamadryas primate (n=1) was reconstructed; the follow-up period was 29 months. Histology was performed on transverse and longitudinal sections of the implant, stained with hematoxylin and eosin; connective tissue was identified using the Mallory method. Results . The obtained bilayer biodegradable polymer scaffold possesses robust physical and mechanical properties and biocompatibility. In all in vivo experiments, the vascular reconstruction remained patent, with no signs of myointimal hyperplasia in the anastomotic area. The scaffold’s ability to integrate into the vascular bed, forming a new vascular wall, as well as adaptive age-related changes in the reconstruction area in response to recipient growth, was demonstrated. Conclusion . Long-term chronic in vivo experiments demonstrated the safety, biocompatibility, and efficacy of the developed scaffold. The resulting tissue-engineered vascular implant exhibits high patency rates and the ability to undergo adaptive age-related changes.
W7220732377.title: Staged Research and Evaluation of Tissue-Engineered Vascular Implant Based on Bioresorbable Polymer Scaffold for Human Vascular Reconstruction

W7220832745.abstract: Objective: This bibliometric study presents a detailed research trends of current state on next generation bioresorbable, biocompatible and conductive polymeric drug delivery systems have evolved.By evaluating global research scientific output, this paper tracks how research area evolved from fundamental core-shell drug delivery architectures that have passive drug-encapsulating mechanics towards complex polymer-based structures that are highly responsive to their local biological environment.Methods: Studies from 2008-2026 were collected from Scopus database and analysed using Microsoft Excel, VOSViewer 1.6.20 and BiblioShiny -Bibliometrix R 4.6.0 to evaluate patterns in publication and citation and various knowledge networks.Results: Upon analysis of 1283 papers, we find that research has steadily grown from 2008-2021.There have been two major milestones, one at 2013 and one between 2016 and 2019 as citations peaked in these years.Further, the top influential papers that caused these and what journals are most interested in this research area peaks have been shown.Demographic indexing also shows the leading females and their footprint and weight in the field.Localized mapping shows Indian institutions that have published most in this field and globalized mapping have identified distinct eastern and western hubs.Conclusion: The formulation of effective drug delivery techniques have gained steady traction over the globe and have given rise to cross disciplinary research in this field with significant results that are being applied in therapeutic procedures.
W7220832745.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
W7220832745.title: A Bibliometric Analysis on Next – Generation Polymers for Drug Delivery: Conductive, Bioresorbable, and Biodegradable Polymers

W7220833775.abstract: Polymers are large macromolecules formed by the repetition of smaller monomeric units, which may be arranged in linear, branched, or three-dimensional network structures. They may exist as homopolymers, composed of one type of repeating monomer, or heteropolymers, composed of different monomeric units. Since Staudinger introduced the concept of polymers as macromolecules in 1920, polymers have become an important field of scientific and industrial interest. Based on their origin, polymers are commonly classified into natural and synthetic polymers. Natural polymers such as proteins, cellulose, starch, silk, wool, cotton, and DNA are produced by living organisms, whereas synthetic polymers such as nylon, polyurethane, rubber, and plastics are produced through chemical processes. Polymers play an essential role in daily life and are widely used in clothing, packaging, furniture, electronics, automobiles, coatings, adhesives, and medical products. Among them, biopolymers have received increasing attention due to their renewable origin, biodegradability, biocompatibility, and environmental benefits. Biopolymers are naturally occurring or bio-based polymeric materials produced by plants, animals, microorganisms, or chemical processes using biological raw materials such as sugars, amino acids, and natural fats. They include proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, polyphenols, and polyhydroxyalkanoates. Because they contain peptide, glycosidic, or other biodegradable bonds, many biopolymers can be degraded by enzymatic action. Their strength, flexibility, and stability make them suitable for various industrial, medical, agricultural, and environmental applications, including bioremediation and pesticide degradation. Therefore, biopolymers represent a promising alternative to conventional synthetic polymers for sustainable development.
W7220833775.title: Production and Characterization of Gamma-Polyglutamic Acid Biopolymer: A Comprehensive Review

W7220834359.abstract: Testicular aging is characterized by progressive spermatogenic decline. Accumulating oxidative injury and insufficient metabolic support from Sertoli cells may contribute to this process. Although molecular hydrogen has shown antioxidant potential, its therapeutic application in reproductive aging is limited by rapid dissipation after administration. To overcome this barrier, we developed the localized hydrogen-releasing system S-H/B. This platform integrates hydrogenated silicon nanosheets (S-H) with a bioadhesive polymer, aldehyde-functionalized polylactic acid-hyperbranched polyglycerol (PLA-HPG-al). The resulting formulation adhered to peritesticular tissue following intrascrotal injection, showed prolonged local retention, and enabled sustained hydrogen release under physiological conditions. This sustained local hydrogen delivery reduced age-associated testicular degeneration and promoted spermatogenesis in aged mice. Notably, single-cell RNA sequencing revealed enhanced HIF-1 signaling and glycolysis-related transcriptional programs in aged Sertoli cells following S-H/B treatment. Further mechanistic analyses indicated that S-H/B reduced ONOO − levels and limited PHD1-dependent HIF-1α hydroxylation, thereby slowing HIF-1α degradation and promoting its nuclear localization. Consistently, S-H/B increased glycolytic enzyme expression, glucose uptake, glycolytic flux, and lactate production in Sertoli cells, whereas HIF-1α inhibition attenuated these metabolic changes. The increased lactate production may have contributed to improved seminiferous epithelial function. Overall, this work presents a bioadhesive hydrogen delivery strategy for age-associated male reproductive dysfunction and suggests that metabolic remodeling in Sertoli cells may contribute to its beneficial effects.
W7220834359.title: An intrascrotal bioadhesive nanoplatform for sustained hydrogen delivery ameliorates age-associated testicular dysfunction

W7220837226.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ultrathin-strut drug-eluting stents (DES) have been developed to enhance vascular healing and reduce restenosis following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Indigenous biodegradable-polymer ultrathin-strut DES are increasingly used in high-burden settings; however, comparative evidence against internationally established thin-strut DES remains limited. METHODS: This systematic review of randomized controlled trials was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to December 2025. Trials comparing indigenous ultrathin-strut DES with internationally manufactured thin-strut DES in adult PCI populations were included. Primary outcomes were major adverse cardiac events/trial-defined composite endpoints. Secondary outcomes included myocardial infarction, target lesion and vessel revascularization, stent thrombosis, cardiac death, and all-cause mortality. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB-2 tool, and a narrative synthesis was performed. RESULTS: Four randomized trials including 2,793 patients were analyzed. Indigenous stents demonstrated comparable rates of composite endpoints, myocardial infarction, repeat revascularization, and stent thrombosis across studies, with no consistent differences between groups. CONCLUSION: The available RCT evidence shows no consistent signal of superiority or inferiority between indigenous and international thin-strut DES. However, heterogeneity and limited trial numbers warrant larger studies with long-term follow-up and real-world materiovigilance. PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: CRD420251240469.
W7220837226.title: Safety and efficacy of indigenous ultrathin-strut versus international thin-strut drug-eluting coronary stents in percutaneous coronary intervention: a systematic review of randomized controlled trials

W7220838904.title: Integrated microbial and enzymatic strategies for waste valorization: From substrate depolymerization to bioproduct synthesis

W7220839094.abstract: Abstract The opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa can store carbon by polymerizing (R)-3-hydroxy fatty acids into polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) and forming large intracellular carbonosomes. These structures primarily function as stores of excess carbon that can be employed during nutrient imbalances, though they have been increasingly reported to have secondary functions in stress responses. A range of Proteobacteria can form carbonosomes, and they have been well characterised in strains used in bioplastic production and wastewater treatment. However, the occurrence, regulation and functions of carbonosomes in pathogenic bacteria remain poorly understood. Using flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy following staining of carbonosomes with BODIPY 493/503, we characterised carbonosome abundance and dynamics in growth-arrested P. aeruginosa starved of nitrogen but provided with excess carbon. We found that carbonosomes substantially impact the energetic and biosynthetic output of growth-arrested P. aeruginosa, affecting protein biosynthesis, flagellar motility, and ATP/NADPH pools. The production and use of carbonosomes was found to confer a strong fitness advantage to growth-arrested P. aeruginosa during fluctuating nutrient conditions. Small carbonosomes were observed during the lag phase of growth in rich media and the ability to produce these structures was conserved across several different laboratory and clinical strains, although with different dynamics and maximal amounts. For example, the Liverpool epidemic strain LESB58 showed very little BODIPY staining while the closely related LESB65 strain showed high levels of staining. Crucially, we found that growth-arrested cells depolymerize carbonosomes upon tobramycin exposure and that carbonosome depolymerization significantly increases P. aeruginosa tobramycin sensitivity. Together, our observations suggest that carbonosomes significantly impact the physiology, metabolism, and antibiotic susceptibility of P. aeruginosa .
W7220839094.title: Polyhydroxyalkanoate carbonosomes impact the activity and viability of growth-arrested Pseudomonas aeruginosa during nutrient fluctuations and tobramycin exposure

W7220846417.abstract: ABSTRACT The plastic pollution crisis highlights the urgent demand for bio‐based biodegradable polymers. Polyamide 4 (PA4) is a promising candidate, yet its application is severely limited by an extremely narrow thermal processing window (≈2°C). This work broadens this window through Lewis acid (LA) complexation modification and investigates the influence of CaCl 2 on the crystallization kinetics of PA4. Results show that specific LA, particularly CaCl 2 , acts as multifunctional modifiers. CaCl 2 interacts with the amide groups of PA4 and modifies the intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding network. This unique interaction significantly increases ductility (elongation at break rises from 99% to 211%) while maintaining tensile strength and approximately maintaining the thermal degradation temperature, and most critically, broadens the thermal processing window from 2°C to 24°C primarily by lowering the melting temperature. Advanced nonisothermal crystallization kinetics analysis reveals a novel concentration‐dependent dual mechanism of CaCl 2 : chain‐complexation dominates at low loadings, while heterogeneous nucleation prevails at 7 wt.%, substantially reducing the crystallization activation energy (Δ E = −23.36 KJ mol −1 ). This clarifies the precise pathway for regulating PA4 crystallization via additives. In summary, this study elucidates the precise pathway for regulating PA4 crystallization via additives, providing a reference for the thermal processing applications of materials with limited thermal processing windows.
W7220846417.title: Plasticizing Modification of Bio‐Based Polyamide 4 With Lewis Acids and Its Nonisothermal Crystallization Kinetics

W7220847509.abstract: The increasing environmental impact of synthetic plastics has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives, with bioplastics derived from renewable feedstock emerging as a promising option. Starch is a natural polymer widely distributed in plants, and it can be applied in diverse ways as a substitute for plastics, helping to reduce their environmental footprint. Conventional starch sources include corn, cassava, wheat, potato and rice, with starch contents of around 70%; however, their use in bioplastic production competes with the food supply chain. This review examines both conventional and alternative starch sources, particularly raw or waste materials with potential for valorisation, including chestnut, acorn, potato peel and sago pith waste. Although these materials generally contain lower starch levels (approximately 50%), they exhibit valuable functional properties. Various methods are available for starch extraction, and among the emerging technologies, enzymatic treatment, ultrasound- and microwave-assisted extraction, as well as pulsed electric fields, stand out as efficient and environmentally friendly options. The selection of the extraction method is critical, as it directly influences the physicochemical properties of starch and, consequently, its performance in final applications. While starch has certain limitations compared to synthetic polymers, its functionality can be improved for instance through blending with natural or synthetic polymers. Overall, starch obtained from alternative sources represents a viable and sustainable pathway to reduce dependence on conventional starch sources that compete for food supplies, as well as on petroleum-based plastics, while simultaneously promoting the valorisation of underutilised biomass and agro-industrial residues.
W7220847509.title: Characteristics of conventional and alternative starch sources, extraction techniques and applications: A review

W7220850361.abstract: Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) hybridized with nano-hydroxyapatite (nHA) and elemental magnesium (Mg) offers a route to tune load-bearing behavior while retaining a biodegradable polymer matrix. This study compares neat PLA, binary PLA-10Mg and PLA-10nHA controls, and three ternary hybrids containing a constant 10 wt.% total reinforcement at Mg:nHA ratios of 1:1, 3:1, and 1:3. Tensile, compressive, and three-point flexural responses were interpreted together with differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Ten specimens were tested per formulation in each mechanical assay (five initial specimens and five confirmatory specimens), and the mechanical data were consolidated across all ten specimens and are reported as an arithmetic mean ± standard deviation (SD). The recorded response was loading-mode-dependent: PLA-5Mg-5nHA combined a tensile stress of 52.0 ± 1.56 MPa with the largest tensile peak displacement ratio of 23.42 ± 0.70%; PLA-7.5Mg-2.5nHA showed the largest flexural peak load of 490.4 ± 14.71 N; and PLA-2.5Mg-7.5nHA combined 52.8 ± 1.58 MPa tensile stress, 93.7 ± 2.81 MPa compressive stress, and 431.5 ± 12.95 N flexural peak load. DSC showed a high-temperature heat-flow event at 365.6-372.6 °C under the stated mixed-purge conditions; this is treated as an operational thermal marker and not a melting or decomposition temperature. XRD remained matrix-dominated with reinforcement-sensitive features, while FTIR showed composition-dependent shifts in the C-O/C-O-C region. The results indicate that Mg:nHA partitioning alters the recorded loading-mode response within the tested 10 wt.% reinforcement window, while particle-scale mechanisms and biological performance require further validation.
W7220850361.title: Composition–Structure–Property Relationships in PLA-nHA-Mg Hybrid Biocomposites: Effect of Ceramic–Metallic Reinforcement Ratio on Mechanical and Physicochemical Performance

W7220858072.abstract: Chitosan-based films provide a biodegradable polymeric platform for the preparation of composite membranes through ionic crosslinking and the incorporation of inorganic materials. In this study, a chitosan–tripolyphosphate–zinc oxide (CTPP-ZnO) bionanocomposite film was prepared using chitosan dissolved in 2% acetic acid, followed by mixing with zinc oxide and crosslinking with sodium tripolyphosphate at approximately pH 5.0. The resulting mixture was cast and oven-dried to obtain a CTPP-ZnO membrane. The crosslinking mechanism is based on electrostatic interactions between protonated amino groups of chitosan and negatively charged phosphate groups of tripolyphosphate, while the β-1,4-glycosidic backbone of chitosan remains the principal structural framework of the polymer. Morphological characteristics of the prepared material were examined using scanning electron microscopy. A preliminary membrane-performance test was also conducted by passing a 4 ppm methylene blue solution through the membrane under a pressure of 10 bar. The observations support the formation of a cross-linked chitosan-based matrix containing zinc oxide and indicate morphological differences between chitosan and the composite film. However, the available measurements do not quantitatively distinguish dye adsorption, pressure-driven separation and photocatalytic degradation. Additional physicochemical, structural and membrane-performance characterisation is therefore required to establish the contribution of zinc oxide and tripolyphosphate to the functional properties of the composite. The study demonstrates a simple preparation approach for a chitosan-based composite film intended for further investigation as a functional membrane material.

W7220866024.abstract: The current research lacks insights into how consumers' utilitarian and hedonic attitudes may influence their sustainability value–behavior gap. We adopt the value–attitude–behavior (VAB) model to examine how utilitarian and hedonic attitudes toward products moderate the consumers' sustainability value–behavior relationship. We conduct three studies: the first tests the basic VAB model, the second examines differences between two time points, and the third compares three wood-based bioproducts: bioplastic bottle, T-shirt, and biofuels. The findings suggest that consumers with sustainable consumption values and hedonic attitudes toward sustainable products exhibit a reduced value–behavior gap and that this effect persists over time. This was most prominent in the case of the wood-based bioplastic bottle. Additionally, consumers with sustainable consumption values and utilitarian attitudes toward sustainable products tend to show a negative effect on the value–behavior gap, which is prominent with wood-based biofuels. These findings underscore the inherent nature of sustainability values and appeals as hedonic, hence the importance of aligning them with hedonic attitudes and related product attributes. Moreover, the importance of both hedonic and utilitarian attitudes is recognized in explaining the sustainability value–behavior gap, and the findings offer guidance for managers and policymakers promoting sustainable products while also highlighting the risks associated with greenwashing.
W7220866024.title: Consumers' hedonic and utilitarian attitudes toward sustainable products: Implications for the sustainability value–behavior gap and wood-based bioproducts

W7220897832.abstract: Abstract Graphene oxide (GO) exhibits strong adsorption capability for dye removal, but its practical utilization remains constrained by aggregation and poor recoverability in aqueous systems. In this study, GO was immobilized onto biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) through an interfacial engineering strategy. PLA substrates were first activated by alkaline etching to increase surface roughness and energy, followed by 3‑aminopropyltriethoxysilane (KH550) silanization to enhance interfacial adhesion. GO was then deposited onto the modified PLA via ultrasonic-assisted coating. The as-prepared composite was systematically characterized using SEM, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and XRD, confirming successful GO immobilization. Stability tests demonstrated that the composite retained 93.7% and 81.5% of its initial GO loading in aqueous and acidic environments after 13 days, respectively. Methylene blue (MB) adsorption experiments revealed kinetics following the pseudo-second-order model with adsorption equilibrium reached within approximately 60 min. The adsorption data were well described by the Langmuir isotherm model, yielding a maximum adsorption capacity of 197.21 mg·g −1 , indicative of monolayer adsorption. After six adsorption–desorption cycles, the composite retained 75.2% of its initial adsorption capacity, indicating satisfactory reusability. This work developed a surface-engineered GO–PLA composite through an effective surface modification strategy, generating a stable and reusable material whose functional performance was validated by the adsorption experiments.

Adsorption, diffusion, and thermodynamic properties of materials
W7220897832.title: Interfacial engineering of graphene oxide immobilization on polylactic acid substrates through surface modification

W7220900024.abstract: Application of biodegradable polylactic acid (PLA) is limited by its poor toughness and processability. This research focused on modifying PLA using butadiene rubber (BR) and epoxy butadiene rubber (EBR) as a toughening material. To enhance the compatibility between PLA and BR, and dicumyl peroxide (DCP) and acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) was introduced into the BR/PLA or EBR/PLA system to prepare BR/PLA-S or EBR/PLA-S by melt blending. The results showed that the optimal composition of modified-BR/PLA was that the mass ratio of PLA/BR/DCP/ATBC was 80/20/0.15/4. The impact strength and elongation at break of the BR/PLA-S and EBR/PLA-S were 8.73 kJ/m 2 and 105.6%; and 11.18 kJ/m 2 and 157.9% respectively. It improved the toughness of PLA, and the toughening effect of EBR was better than that of BR. The peak intensity of the C=C bond (3006 cm -1 ) in the FTIR spectra of the modified-BR/PLA weakened, and the peak area of the CH 2 bond (2918 cm −1 ) increased, occurring a cross-linking reaction between BR (or EBR) and PLA. Tg, Tc and Tm of the BR/PLA-S and EBR/PLA-S were 58.44°C, 92.53°C and 170.13°C; 55.0°C, 87.5°C and 167.66°C respectively, lower than Tg and Tc of PLA, and higher than Tm of PLA, suggesting that modified-BR improved processability and thermal stability of PLA composites. The successful preparation of BR-based toughening agent using an environmental-friendly system broadened the use of BR and PLA with the truly-sustainable developments.
W7220900024.journal: Progress in Rubber Plastics and Recycling Technology
W7220900024.title: Investigation of PLA composites modified by butadiene rubber using the compatibilization method

W7220901846.abstract: The accumulation of non-biodegradable, petroleum-based single-use packaging presents an urgent environmental crisis, particularly in dominant cocoa-exporting regions like West Africa, where millions of metric tons of Cocoa Pod Husk (CPH) are discarded annually as hazardous agricultural waste. This study presents a closed-loop valorization strategy by designing a purely theoretical, macro-scale industrial process simulation model to upcycle regional CPH side-streams into high-performance active and intelligent bio-based food packaging films. Operating under steady-state thermodynamic reference constraints (T₀ = 298.15 K, P₀ = 101.325 kPa), a multi-block refining flowsheet was computationally modeled across three interconnected operational tracks: Block 100 (First-order kinetic delignification and selective acid cleavage of amorphous matrix loops to isolate rigid, highly crystalline cellulose nanocrystals; CPH-CNCs); Block 200 (Supercritical fluid recovery using altered scCO₂ solvent matrices to isolate bioactive antioxidant polyphenols; CPH-Ext via broken-and-intact cell kinetics); and Block 300 (Continuous high-shear polyion blending and casting using a modified cationic cassava starch/chitosan hydrocolloid blend plasticized with 30 wt% glycerol). Materials performance simulations demonstrated that an optimal filler loading fraction of 5.0 wt% (Formulation M-5.0) generates an ideal interfacial hydrogen-bonding network across the polymer boundaries. This boundary alignment yielded a simulated peak Tensile Strength of 29.85 ± 0.95 MPa (representing a substantial 61.2% reinforcement over unreinforced controls) and a rigid Young's Modulus of 570.83 MPa. Mass transport modeling utilizing Maxwell-Barrer Fickian mechanics verified that this uniform nanoparticle dispersion maximized the matrix tortuosity factor (τ), reducing Water Vapor Permeability (WVP) by 56.5% to 2.11 × 10⁻¹¹ g⋅m⁻¹⋅s⁻¹⋅Pa⁻¹ and substantially minimizing the Oxygen Transmission Rate (OTR). Thermogravimetric specific heat capacity simulations (DSC) verified an enhanced structural ordering, shifting the simulated glass transition to 74.5°C and final thermal decomposition onset to 308.5°C. Active system kinetics demonstrated a stable DPPH radical scavenging efficiency of 84.2% over 48 hours, with a controlled migration velocity that successfully prevented early burst leaching. In antimicrobial boundary bioassays, the polyion network generated distinct inhibition zones against Staphylococcus aureus (18.4 mm) and Escherichia coli (13.8 mm). As an intelligent freshness indicator exposed to volatile total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N) spoilage metrics, the embedded CPH anthocyanins triggered an unambiguous, non-destructive colorimetric transformation (Δ E = 31.84), shifting visually from light pink to a vibrant green hue that far exceeds the human visual perception threshold (Δ E ≥ 3.5). Finally, environmental lifecycle tracking confirmed complete eco-compatibility, with the composite material achieving 88.5% cumulative biodegradation within 60 days under standard respirometric composting conditions (ISO 14855-1), while post-degradation soil matrix modeling (Lactuca sativa) verified zero phytotoxicity with a Germination Index of 101.2%, easily clearing the 80% OECD Guideline 208 safety baseline. These results establish a scalable, domestic engineering paradigm for transforming regional agricultural liabilities into advanced, eco-friendly functional resources for sustainable development.
W7220901846.title: Upcycling Side-Streams into Smart Bio-Based Packaging: A Purely Theoretical, Macro-Scale Industrial Process Design Simulation of Active, Intelligent Functional Films Derived from West African Cocoa Pod Husk (Theobroma cacao L.)

W7220906538.abstract: Excessive accumulation of plastic waste is an unresolved global environmental problem. A solution that can be applied and has the potential to overcome this issue is the use of natural polymer materials, such as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA). PHA has good physicochemical properties and characteristics similar to those of conventional plastics, making it a viable alternative plastic matrix. The application of PHA serves as a composite and can decompose plastic waste, a major problem today. The structure, synthesis, and applications of various PHA fields will be discussed in this review, which includes previous research reviews. PHA is biodegradable because it is processed by microorganisms. PHA can be synthesised from various microorganisms and carbon sources. The application of PHA also plays a role in the pharmaceutical and biofuel fields. This review makes a significant contribution to the development of polymer applications that support the global transition towards clean and environmentally friendly energy. This review employed a systematic literature review (SLR) approach following the PRISMA framework and PICOS criteria. Of 280 records identified in the Scopus database for the 2020-2024 period, nine experimental articles met the eligibility criteria and were analyzed using structured data extraction and narrative synthesis. The synthesis indicates that PHA properties are influenced by monomer chain length and composition, while production performance depends on the microorganism, carbon source, cultivation conditions, and polymer recovery method. The selected studies demonstrate potential applications in biodegradable packaging, pharmaceuticals, biofuels, and waste valorization; however, industrial implementation remains constrained by production costs, scale-up requirements, and limited life-cycle evidence. Thus, this review contributes an integrated assessment of the relationship between PHA structure, synthesis strategy, and application potential, while identifying process optimization and industrial-scale validation as key research priorities.
W7220906538.title: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) Polymers from Nature for Nature: Structure, Synthesis, and Applications

W7220919020.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to fabricate and assess the physical, mechanical, and in vitro biological properties of 3D printed single-layered scaffolds that simulate cartilage, calcified cartilage, and subchondral bone tissue. As well as a tri-layered osteochondral scaffold with a gradient composition and porosity. METHODS: Six groups were fabricated using a masked stereolithography-based 3D printer. The cartilage group consisted of polylactic acid (PLA)/ 2% hyaluronic acid (HA) with the smallest pores and percentage porosity. The calcified cartilage group comprised PLA/ 2% HA/10% nano-hydroxyapatite (nHAp). Subchondral bone scaffold was formed of PLA/ 25% nHAp with the largest pore size and % porosity. The three scaffold designs were assembled to create the tri-layered group. There were two control groups. A total of 683 scaffolds were 3D printed. Tensile strength, compressive strength, moduli, and interfacial adhesion strength were evaluated at 24 h and 30 days. The biodegradation % of different scaffolds was assessed after 7, 14, and 28 days. Cell viability was assessed through cell counting, cell adhesion, and H & E staining. Cell differentiation was assessed using fast green/safranin O, alizarin red staining, and immunofluorescence after coculturing with rat bone marrow mesenchymal stem at 7, 14, and 21 days. Data were statistically analyzed at p ≤ 0.05. RESULTS: The tensile strengths and moduli of the PLA/2%HA and PLA/25% nHAp scaffolds resembled those of normal cartilage and trabecular bone, respectively. The tri-layered scaffold exhibited strong interfacial adhesion strength and demonstrated 13.68% weight loss after 30 days. The tri-layered scaffold exhibited a stiffness gradient, supporting biological responses consistent with chondrogenic differentiation on the more flexible side of the scaffold and osteogenic differentiation on the stiffer side. It demonstrated evidence of both chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation. CONCLUSIONS: Incorporation of HA and nHAp, as well as variations in porosity, significantly impacted scaffolds' properties. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings suggested the potential of the fabricated scaffolds for medical and maxillofacial regenerative applications, particularly for repairing cartilage, bone, and osteochondral defects.
W7220919020.title: A biomimetic 3D printed gradient tri-layered scaffold stimulating osteochondral differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells for mandibular condyle regeneration

W7220927885.abstract: This study investigates how design-driven strategies enhance sustainability in food packaging within a circular economy framework. It identifies how design choices mediate environmental performance, usability and consumer behaviour, moving beyond material substitution as the sole sustainability strategy. A qualitative multi-case study using secondary data was adopted, supported by a design-based evaluation matrix applied to five packaging types (bioplastic tray, paper carton, glass jar, reusable modular container and compostable pouch). Thematic analysis compared cases across environmental, functional and behavioural dimensions using a transparent 0–3 scoring rubric. Design effectiveness depends less on material novelty and more on systemic compatibility with recovery infrastructures and user interaction. Packaging featuring intuitive functionality (resealability, clear disposal cues) and closed-loop integration achieved higher sustainability scores. Glass jars and reusable containers demonstrated superior circular-economy alignment; biobased and compostable materials underperformed due to infrastructural and behavioural constraints. The study introduces a design-based evaluation matrix integrating behavioural, functional and environmental criteria, offering a practical decision-support tool for designers, policymakers and waste managers. Reliance on secondary data and five cases limits generalisability. Future work should combine life-cycle metrics with primary consumer insights.
W7220927885.journal: International Journal of African Research Sustainability Studies
W7220927885.title: STRATEGIES FOR ACHIEVING SUSTAINABILITY IN DESIGN-DRIVEN FOOD PACKAGING: A MULTI-CASE EVALUATION WITHIN A CIRCULAR ECONOMY FRAMEWORK

W7220937903.abstract: Although the piezoresistive behavior of conductive polymer composites has been widely studied, the geometry-dependent piezoresistive response of MWCNT/PLA-based TPMS lattice structures produced by fused filament fabrication (FFF) remains insufficiently explored. The primary objective of this study is to comparatively investigate the mechanical, thermal, electrical, and piezoresistive behaviors of Gyroid (G), Diamond (D), and Schwarz Primitive (P) TPMS lattice structures produced using the same material system, constant relative density, and XY printing orientation. For this purpose, a 2 wt.% multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composite filament was fabricated via solvent mixing and used to produce the three TPMS topologies through FFF. Mechanical and electromechanical properties were assessed via Shore D hardness, monotonic compression tests, and in-situ electrical measurements using three independent replicate specimens for each topology (n = 3). The highest hardness was recorded for Diamond (75.6 Shore D) and the lowest for Schwarz Primitive (71.2 Shore D). At 50% compressive strain, compressive stresses were 14.164, 8.777, and 3.152 MPa for Diamond, Gyroid, and Schwarz Primitive, respectively. Specific energy absorption (SEA) values followed the same order at 9.161, 6.149, and 2.917 J g−1. Electrical conductivity and resistivity variations under loading were characterized using the four-probe method, with Diamond exhibiting the highest and Schwarz Primitive the lowest conductivity. Piezoresistive analysis showed that Diamond achieved the highest positive compressive gauge factor (GF) values of 4.74 and 2.74 at 10% and 25% strains, respectively. At 50% strain, Gyroid demonstrated superior sensitivity (GF = 1.66) over Diamond (1.57) and Schwarz Primitive (1.49). Electrical resistance exhibited a monotonic decrease with advancing compressive strain across all topologies, validating a coherent and continuous piezoresistive response under uniaxial compression. These results indicate that Diamond offers the best overall performance in mechanical strength, SEA, and low-to-medium strain sensitivity, while Gyroid is preferable for high-strain sensing. Overall, 2 wt.% MWCNT/PLA-based TPMS structures demonstrate considerable potential for piezoresistive sensor applications.
oa_topics: Advanced Sensor and Energy Harvesting Materials
W7220937903.title: Investigation of Piezoresistive Behaviors in TPMS Lattice Structures Produced with MWCNT-Reinforced PLA Filament

W7220948555.abstract: The transition toward sustainable manufacturing has accelerated the development of sustainable polymer composites reinforced with bio-based fillers such as biochar. This study investigates how the biochar carbonization route affects the thermal and mechanical properties of polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites. Bamboo-derived torrefied biomass (TBB) and pyrolyzed biochar (PBB) were incorporated into PLA at loadings of 1 wt.% and 2 wt.%. PLA–TBB composites exhibited improved tensile stiffness and flexural performance, achieving improvements of 4.28% in tensile modulus, 18.72% in flexural strength, and 12.30% in flexural modulus compared with neat PLA. In contrast, PLA–PBB composites showed the highest compressive strength, with a 29.53% increase. Thermal analysis further revealed that biochar, regardless of the carbonization route, induced cold crystallization and slightly improved PLA thermal stability, with PLA–PBB2 exhibiting the highest peak degradation temperature and PLA–PBB1 showing the lowest weight loss. These findings demonstrate that the carbonization route influences the reinforcing performance of bamboo biochar, with lower-temperature torrefied biomass favoring tensile and flexural performance, while higher-temperature pyrolyzed biochar provides superior compressive and thermal properties. The enhanced tensile stiffness and flexural performance of PLA–TBB suggest potential for rigid applications, whereas PLA–PBB is better suited to compression-loaded applications. The results provide valuable insights into tailoring the conditions for bamboo biochar production to support the development of PLA biocomposites.
W7220948555.title: From torrefaction to pyrolysis: Influence of bamboo biochar production route on biochar characteristics and the thermal and mechanical performance of polylactic acid biocomposites

W7220959468.abstract: ABSTRACT This work investigates the influence of fiber architecture on the fracture toughness and interfacial adhesion of polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites reinforced with coir, fique, and sisal fibers. Composites containing 1, 3, and 5 wt.% fiber were prepared under identical processing conditions using untreated and alkali‐conditioned fibers, enabling a comparative assessment of the structure–interphase–property relationship. Thermal behavior was evaluated by differential scanning calorimetry and thermogravimetric analysis, tensile properties were determined under uniaxial loading, and fracture response was analyzed using double‐deeply edge‐notched tensile specimens to determine the critical J ‐integral under quasi‐static conditions. Results indicate that fiber architecture is the primary factor governing energy dissipation; coir and fique systems demonstrated a superior capacity for increasing fracture resistance and ductility compared to neat PLA. Coir‐ and fique‐reinforced systems showed the most significant increase in fracture toughness, accompanied by higher ductility and improved interfacial features in scanning electron microscope observations, whereas sisal composites exhibited a more limited response. Thermal analysis revealed only moderate changes in glass transition, crystallization, and degradation behavior, indicating that the main effects of conditioning are associated with interfacial efficiency rather than bulk thermal transitions. The results support a structure–interphase–property framework in which fiber architecture governs the effectiveness of alkali treatment and the activation of toughening mechanisms in PLA‐based biocomposites.
W7220959468.title: The Role of Fiber Architecture in Interfacial Adhesion and Fracture Toughness of Polylactic Acid/Lignocellulosic Fiber Biocomposites

W7220987087.abstract: This work presents the development of engineering-grade bio-based polymers derived exclusively from second-generation agri-food residues within the European project POLYMERS-5B (CBE-JU, Grant Agreement No. 101157840). Tomato pomace and olive pomace were processed through a cascaded biorefinery integrating enzymatic depolymerisation, green chemistry fractionation and immobilised-lipase polycondensation. Pilot-scale validation on batches of up to 15 kg demonstrated the reproducible synthesis of polyesters with an elastic modulus of approximately 2 GPa and a glass transition temperature of at least 80 degrees Celsius, enabling conventional industrial melt processing. Cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment indicates a reduction of about 50 per cent of CO2 emissions with respect to fossil-based PET and polycarbonate grades. Using the AI-driven C-Tech Navigator platform developed by NSBproject, the materials were benchmarked against poly(ethylene furanoate) and polyhydroxyalkanoates, identifying a market gap in automotive interiors, technical textiles and functional coatings, where waste-derived and thermally stable polymers can outperform the existing bio-based alternatives. The results confirm the industrial relevance and the scalability of the POLYMERS-5B platform, validated at Technology Readiness Level 5, and position it as a competitive circular polymer pathway for the European bioeconomy.
W7220987087.title: From Agri-food Residues to High-performance Sustainable Polymers: The POLYMERS-5B Pathway Toward Circular Bioplastics

W7220992700.abstract: This study presents a comparative acoustic analysis of drone propellers manufactured using different materials and additive manufacturing methods. A total of twelve propellers were produced with FFF (Fused filament fabrication) and MSLA (Masked Stereolithography) techniques, employing six different material types, including ABS (Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene), ASA (Acrylonitrile Styrene Acrylate), PETG (Polyethylene Terephthalate Glycol), PLA (Polylactic Acid), Tough Resin and Water Wash Resin. All propellers were tested individually under the same conditions specific to the experimental setup and acoustic data were recorded using a microphone. Subsequently, various sound characteristics such as A-weighted sound pressure level (dB(A)), fluctuation strength, roughness and sharpness were analyzed using MATLAB. The results demonstrate that both the material and the printing method have a substantial influence on acoustic behavior. While FFF-printed propellers generally produced higher sound pressure levels, MSLA-printed ones tended to exhibit higher values in temporal modulation metrics such as fluctuation and roughness. Furthermore, materials with higher stiffness generally tended to exhibit lower overall loudness, fluctuation and roughness, whereas higher sharpness values were observed. The findings contribute to the understanding of how material selection and additive manufacturing methods influence noise emissions in drones, providing a perspective for future design optimizations.

W7220992700.title: A comparative acoustic analysis of 3D-printed drone propellers with different materials and manufacturing methods

W7221009309.abstract: ABSTRACT Zein is an insoluble prolamin protein extracted from different by‐products of the corn industry. More recently, the thermoplastic behavior and ability to melt when heated displayed by zein/glycerol blends (zein/Glycerol) have highlighted its use in versatile plastic thermal processing techniques. In this study, the effect of additives that may reinforce the resulting materials is examined. A water‐soluble chitosan derivative, carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCH), was included in zein/CMCH/Glycerol systems to assess the feasibility of complexation between zein and CMCH as a way to tune the hydrophilicity and mechanical properties of the material. Additionally, genipin (GNP), a natural cross‐linker, was added either to zein/Glycerol or zein/CMCH/Glycerol systems to reinforce the mechanical properties. In this context, Young's modulus ( E ) increased from around 16 to 40 MPa when GNP was added at 0.5 mM, while maintaining its water uptake (WUC) around 170%. The joint role of CMCH and GNP was only synergistic at low GNP concentrations (0.01 mM). However, at high GNP concentrations (0.5 mM), no enhancement of the mechanical properties was observed, despite the greater thermal resistance. Thus, the properties of zein‐based materials can be improved by selecting a suitable GNP concentration, which facilitates the development of bioplastics with specific applications.
W7221009309.title: Effect of Carboxymethyl Chitosan and Genipin on the Structural, Water Uptake, and Thermomechanical Properties of Zein‐Based Biodegradable Materials

W7221013205.abstract: The environmental impact of non-biodegradable plastic waste has intensified the demand for sustainable, bio-based food packaging. This study examines the effects of citric acid (CA) crosslinking concentrations of 1.7% and 3.4% on the mechanical, structural, and biodegradation properties of pectin-chitosan (PC) bioplastic films integrated with Moringa oleifera leaf powder as a functional filler, prepared via the solvent casting method. Research results revealed that an increase in CA concentration led to a mechanical trade-off, where Tensile strength and Young’s modulus decreased from 1.73 to 0.89 MPa and 2.04–0.31 MPa, respectively. Conversely, the elongation at break significantly increased from 86.48% to 288.55%, validated by real-time IoT monitoring over 3000 s to precisely capture the fracture point of the films. FTIR analysis confirmed crosslinked network formation via ester linkages (C O ∼1728 cm −1 ), while XRD analysis confirmed that the lower CA concentration resulted in a more crystalline fraction (~23.36%), thereby providing enhanced stiffness. In contrast, the higher concentration increased the amorphous fraction (~88.46%), which enhanced flexibility. We found that the higher amorphous fraction in PCC 3.4 led to a significantly faster degradation rate (63.53% mass loss by Day 7), as SEM results showed accelerated crack and void formation. Despite kinetic differences, both formulations demonstrated promising environmental compatibility, achieving a total mass loss of ≥ 89.17% within 21 days.
W7221013205.title: Structural and biodegradation properties of pectin-chitosan/moringa oleifera as bioplastic: IoT-based mechanical testing implemented

W7221018387.abstract: This study presents a continuous biochemical process for producing 3-hydroxypropionic acid (3-HP), an important platform chemical for bioplastics, using two renewable feedstocks including corn stover and brewer's spent grains. An integrated ionic liquid recovery unit allows catalyst recycling and reuse, enabling continuous operation. Biomass-to-3-HP conversion efficiencies of 25-27% were achieved for both feedstocks. A detailed techno-economic evaluation was carried out to assess the economic viability of the process. At an annual production capacity of 50,000 tonnes of 3-HP, the break-even selling price was estimated at $2,472 per tonne for corn stover and $2,643 per tonne for brewer’s spent grains-based plants. These findings demonstrate the economic feasibility of waste biomass-derived 3-HP as a sustainable alternative to petrochemical-based plastics.
W7221018387.title: Techno-economic Assessment of Biomass-derived 3-HP for Bio-based Chemicals

W7221019191.abstract: Traditional Design for Assembly seeks to simplify manufacturing processes by reducing complexity, cost, and assembly time. This study presents the integration of traditional Japanese joinery techniques with advanced manufacturing technology, specifically focusing on the Design for Assembly principles in 3D printed parts, the opportunities to overcome limitations inherent to traditional manufacturing methods. Three specific joinery configurations are selected for evaluation: the Dovetail joint, T joint, and C joint. For each configuration, three critical geometric parameters were designed and the corresponding specimens were 3D printed using Polylactic acid. Each joint configuration underwent tensile testing to determine their mechanical strength. Digital Image Correlation analysis was employed during the tensile tests to provide real-time visualisation of strain distribution and damage development. The C joint configuration, with a 5 mm neck thickness, showed a high ultimate tensile strength of 7 MPa, as well as optimal load distribution, and predictable failure behaviour in comparison to all other joints tested. Conversely, the Dovetail joint with a 10mm thickness exhibited the lowest mechanical strength equal to 2.2 MPa. Relative to the sound reference sample, which showed the ultimate tensile strength of 44.4MPa, the sample with the optimal C joint configuration achieved about 15.8% of the ultimate tensile strength of the reference specimen. The results showed that the C joint has the most favourable tensile performance among the tested configurations and demonstrated the feasibility of using joinery-inspired interlocking joints as a basis for further design investigation.
W7221019191.title: Design for assembly of 3D-printed structures using joinery-inspired interlocking joints

W7221034040.title: Structure-performance relationship of MOF-derived cu/N-doped biochar composites for efficient H2S removal: Insights into adsorption and regeneration mechanisms

W7221040452.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(lactic‐co‐glycolic acid) (PLGA) is a biodegradable polymer widely used in biomedical research owing to its biocompatibility, tunable degradation, and compatibility with a broad range of therapeutic agents. This review examines recent advances in PLGA‐based systems across established and emerging areas, including cancer nanomedicine, wound healing, tissue regeneration, phytoconstituent delivery, immunomodulation, imaging and diagnostics, three‐dimensional (3D) printing, antimicrobial therapy, and surgical adjuncts. It also considers clinical translation and recent patent activity, providing a broader perspective on how PLGA‐based technologies are evolving beyond conventional drug delivery. Recent studies show that PLGA‐based micro‐ and nanosystems can support controlled release, improve drug loading and cellular uptake, and enable targeted or multifunctional delivery. Despite this progress, translation remains constrained by formulation stability, hydrophilic drug encapsulation, batch‐to‐batch variability, sterilization, scale‐up, and regulatory requirements. PLGA therefore remains a highly versatile platform for biomedical use, but its broader clinical impact will depend on reproducible manufacturing, stronger translational evidence, and formulation strategies that adequately address safety, stability, and scalability.
W7221040452.title: Emerging Frontiers of Biomedical Applications of PLGA : Where Do We Stand?

W7221043531.abstract: The global reliance on petroleum-based plastics has intensified the demand for biodegradable alternatives such as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs). In this study, PHA production by Bacillus sp. was investigated under nitrogen-limited conditions with glucose, fructose, and sucrose as carbon sources at varying C:N ratios (19:1, 38:1, 76:1). Batch experiments were performed to evaluate biomass growth and intracellular polymer accumulation. Glucose proved to be the most effective substrate, supporting a maximum PHA content of 82.9% of cell dry weight at a C:N ratio of 38:1 after 48 h. Fructose yielded moderate accumulation (54%) but showed degradation at extended incubation, while sucrose supported only limited storage (35%). Excessive nitrogen limitation reduced both biomass and polymer yields, whereas moderate limitation optimized accumulation. These findings highlight the decisive role of nutrient balance and substrate choice in PHA biosynthesis and demonstrate the potential of Bacillus sp. for sustainable bioplastic production.
W7221043531.title: Optimization for Polyhydroxyalkanoate Production from Various Carbon Sources and C:N Ratios by Bacillus sp. under Nitrogen Limitation

W7221049954.abstract: Bio-composites are emerging as viable alternatives to conventional building materials owing to their renewable origin, environmental benefits, and potential to reduce the carbon footprint of the construction sector. Comprising natural fibers embedded within polymer matrices, these materials have attracted considerable attention within the building industry for their capacity to mitigate environmental impact while offering functional alternatives to conventional synthetic materials. This review provides a comprehensive examination of the various classes of bio-composites, their applications in building construction, mechanical properties, manufacturing processes, associated advantages and limitations, and prospects for future development. Natural and agricultural fibers such as jute, hemp, flax, sisal, bamboo, rice husk, wheat straw, and coconut coir, combined with matrices including corn starch, arrowroot, polyethylene, polypropylene, polylactic acid, and bio-based epoxy resin, are evaluated in terms of their structural and functional performance. Particular attention is given to recent advances in bio-composite fabrication, including the incorporation of novel binder systems, hybrid fiber reinforcements, and chemical surface treatments aimed at enhancing mechanical and thermal performance. The environmental benefits of bio-composites are also discussed, including reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved energy efficiency, and minimized construction waste, all of which align with the objectives of green building standards and sustainable construction practices. Nevertheless, several challenges continue to impede widespread adoption, including moisture sensitivity, variability in raw material properties, insufficient long-term performance data, and the absence of standardized testing protocols. The significant potential of bio-composites to advance sustainable construction practices, offering a practical pathway toward reducing the environmental footprint of the built environment.
W7221049954.title: A review of natural fiber and agricultural waste fiber-based bio-composites used in building construction

W7221056230.abstract: A biodegradable polymer coating on a permanent metallic vascular stent must combine mechanical stability during deployment, hemocompatibility, and controlled resorption without a pronounced local inflammatory response. The aim of this study was to compare the physicochemical characteristics and physiologically relevant biological responses of six commercial polymers based on polylactide and its copolymers with glycolide, differing in stereoregularity (L- and DL-lactide), monomer ratio (50/50, 75/25, 90/10), and end-group type (ester or acid), in order to select a material for further development of a biodegradable stent coating. Equilibrium swelling and tensile properties were examined using model free-standing films; for five materials that could be prepared as intact films, hemolysis, platelet activation in vitro, biodegradation, and local tissue response after 30-day subcutaneous implantation in Wistar rats were assessed. Crystalline poly(L-lactide) and the copolymer containing 10% glycolide exhibited high stiffness and low elongation at break; the latter was excluded from biological testing because of film brittleness. Copolymers containing 50% glycolide were highly ductile. None of the biologically tested materials caused pronounced hemolysis or platelet activation. On day 30, the faster-degrading PLGA(50/50)-E, PDLLG(50/50)-A, and PLGA(75/25)-E showed pronounced resorption with minimal local inflammation, whereas slowly degrading PDLLA-E and PLLA-A persisted in the tissues and were associated with a more pronounced chronic foreign body response. PLGA(75/25)-E showed the most balanced combination of mechanical properties, degradation behavior, and biological response profile. These data support its selection as a candidate for the next stage, namely deposition on a metallic stent platform and evaluation as an actual stent coating.
W7221056230.journal: Journal of Evolutionary Biochemistry and Physiology
W7221056230.title: Comparative Evaluation of Physicochemical and Biological Characteristics of Polylactides and Lactide–Glycolide Copolymers for Biodegradable Vascular Stent Coatings

W7221059711.title: In situ thermal welding for constructing PBAT/rGO porous structures for shape-stable composite phase-change materials

W7221060448.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) profoundly impact the storage and stability of soil organic matter (SOM), yet the mechanisms by which phages mediate the transformation of plant- and microbially derived SOM under biodegradable MP perturbation remain poorly understood. This study integrated multiomics, stable isotope techniques, and phage inoculation experiments to investigate how phages mediate SOM transformation following biodegradable MP addition in agricultural soil. The results revealed that lytic phage-bacteria interactions were central to MP-dependent SOM transformation. Polylactic acid (PLA) reduced plant-derived organic molecules by 15% without affecting microbially derived carbon. PLA increased phage lysis and enriched auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) such as queC (2.2-fold increase), which supports phage replication and reduces microbial biomass. Pure culture experiments supported that PLA increased phage lytic infectivity. Phage inoculation further revealed that lytic phages accelerated bacteria to shift toward catabolism (e.g., lignocellulose degradation, citrate cycle) in PLA-amended soil, reducing carbon use efficiency (CUE) and accelerating decomposition of plant- and microbially derived carbon through viral shunt. In comparison, polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) increased microbially derived molecules by 37%, particularly amino nitrogen compounds. The higher degradability of PHA stimulated lytic phage bloom with their hosts and enriched biosynthesis-related AMGs (e.g., cysH, glmS). Phage inoculation experiments showed that surviving bacteria assimilated phage lysate products into anabolism (e.g., amino acid and amino sugar biosynthesis), enriching metabolites such as l-isoleucine and MurNAc after PHA addition. This increased CUE and accumulation of microbial organics through viral shuttle. These findings uncover phage-mediated mechanisms linking microplastic perturbation to soil carbon cycling.
W7221060448.title: Phage Lysis Associated with Biodegradable Microplastics Mediates Microbial Physiological Adaptation to Transform Organic Matter in Soil

W7221073020.abstract: Abstract This work examines the influence of an inorganic chalk-based additive on the quality and mechanical properties of products produced by 3D printing using the fused filament fabrication (FFF) method from polylactic acid (PLA). The use of inorganic additives is common mainly to reduce material costs and modify mechanical properties. Regarding the potential for material savings, the effects of different infill patterns (strain and octagonal) and densities (0, 50, and 100 %) were also tested in the study. The test specimens were evaluated using mechanical tests, qualitative surface morphology analysis with a digital optical microscope featuring a large depth of field, and thermal analysis. The work also included a finite element method (FEM) simulation to analyse the mechanical behaviour of the specimens under study. The FFF process is influenced by several parameters, such as printing temperature, substrate temperature, printing speed, and printing orientation, which have a fundamental impact on the resulting product quality. The results show that the amount and choice of additive significantly affect the mechanical properties and overall quality of printed parts, which emphasises the need to optimise both material composition and printing parameters.
oa_topics: Innovations in Concrete and Construction Materials
W7221073020.title: Effect of inorganic chalk additive on 3D-printed polylactic acid specimens

W7221075642.abstract: ABSTRACT This work demonstrates successful grafting of N ‐hydroxyethyl acrylamide (HEAA) onto poly[( R )‐3‐hydroxybutyrate] (P[( R )‐3HB]), up to 156 wt.% using 60 Co gamma irradiation (10.1 kGy) and a 1:4 P[( R )‐3HB]:HEAA molar ratio in ethyl acetate. The resulting N ‐hydroxyethyl acrylamide‐grafted poly[( R )‐3‐hydroxybutyrate] (P3HB‐HEAA) was comprehensively characterized using FTIR, NMR, SEM, DSC, TGA/DTG, tensile testing, and water uptake, and exhibited striking property changes relative to the native polymer. The modified material showed a T g of 124°C, reduced melting enthalpy ( ΔH m = 12 J/g), increased T d,10 and T d,50 of 260°C and 340°C, respectively, increased elongation at break (ɛ = 65%), increased toughness (by 378%), exceptional water absorption capacity (610 wt.%), a markedly less ordered surface structure compared to the starting materials. These changes indicate formation of a less crystalline, highly hygroscopic, hydrogel‐like system. HEAA grafting generated a biphasic architecture comprising a semicrystalline, structurally robust, P[( R )‐3HB] backbone coupled with an amorphous, hydrogel‐like HEAA surface layer, yielding a potentially biodegradable polymer with enhanced hydration capacity. The structure retains structural integrity while enabling substantial water uptake properties not accessible with either component alone. Combining mechanical strength with tuneable hydration behavior, HEAA‐grafted P[( R )‐3HB] expands the functional and commercial potential of P[( R )‐3HB] into applications requiring simultaneous structural integrity, controlled swelling, and potential biocompatibility.
W7221075642.title: Gamma Irradiation‐Based Free Radical Grafting of N ‐Hydroxyethyl Acrylamide onto Poly[( R )‐3‐hydroxybutyrate]

W7221079503.abstract: The environmental burden of conventional plastic packaging has increased interest in sustainable alternatives. This study evaluates the environmental performance of polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites reinforced with brewer’s spent grain (BSG), an agro-industrial by-product, using life cycle assessment (LCA). PLA, PLA/BSG biocomposites containing 10 wt% and 20 wt% BSG, and conventional plastics (polypropylene and polyethylene terephthalate) were compared. BSG was modeled using a cut-off approach as a waste-derived material, with preparation impacts attributed to energy consumption. Cradle-to-gate results showed environmental benefits from BSG incorporation, but also relevant trade-offs. Compared with neat PLA, 10 wt% and 20 wt% BSG reduced global warming potential by 4.10% and 8.20%, respectively, and fossil depletion by 5.40% and 10.70%. In contrast, freshwater eutrophication increased with BSG content, reaching +32.2% at 20 wt% BSG, mainly due to electricity consumption associated with drying and milling. Compared with conventional plastics, PLA/BSG biocomposites showed substantially lower fossil depletion, although polypropylene had a lower global warming potential. Composting and recycling performed better than incineration. Overall, BSG incorporation can reduce fossil-resource dependence and support circular resource utilization, while optimization of BSG processing is needed to minimize environmental trade-offs.
W7221079503.title: Life Cycle Assessment of Polylactic Acid/Brewer’s Spent Grain Biocomposites: Environmental Impact of Lignocellulosic Waste Incorporation

W7221085471.abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the efficiency of biodegradable bilayer packaging materials based on thermoplastic starch (TPS) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) containing ferulic acid (F) or beer bagasse extract (E) obtained by subcritical water extraction as active agents (60 g/kg) for refrigerated pork meat preservation. Bilayers (Bilayer-F, Bilayer-E) were characterized and the physicochemical and microbiological quality of the meat packaged in these active biodegradable materials along with a free-active film and a commercial polyethylene bag, was analyzed. The results showed that the incorporation of both active agents did not significantly alter the water barrier capacity of the films but acted as plasticizers, increasing the elongation at break up to 55%. In preservation trials, all bilayers significantly inhibited microbial growth compared to commercial bags, likely due to their superior oxygen barrier capacity. Specifically, Bilayer-F exhibited the highest antimicrobial and antioxidant efficacy, achieving a 2-log reduction in total viable counts and extending pork microbiological shelf life by approximately 7 days. Conversely, Bilayer-E showed limited effectiveness due to lower bioactivity compared to pure ferulic acid. While bilayers resulted in higher weight loss than commercial bags due to their inherent water vapor permeability, Bilayer-F represents a promising sustainable alternative for maintaining fresh meat quality. Overall, these results demonstrate that TPS-PHA bilayers incorporating ferulic acid represent a highly effective active packaging system to extend the shelf life of fresh pork meat, whereas the complex beer bagasse extract was not effective in preservation
