W7221085471.title: Efficiency of biodegradable active starch-polyhydroxyalkanoate bilayers containing beer bagasse extract or ferulic acid on refrigerated pork meat preservation

W7221085952.title: Synthesis of Boron Composite Biochar and Its Evaluation for Growth Effectiveness in Rice

W7221089665.abstract: Diverse contaminants in urban non-point source pollution increase the difficulty of remediation, and developing low-cost and eco-friendly materials for simultaneous multi-pollutant removal is a promising mitigation strategy. Using waterworks sludge and rice husk as raw materials, a zero-valent iron-zeolite-biochar (ZVI-ZL-BC) composite was successfully synthesized via carbothermal reduction followed by hydrothermal treatment. The as-prepared ZVI-ZL-BC efficiently adsorbed typical urban non-point source pollutants including sulfamethoxazole (SMX), NO3 −, PO4 3 − and Cu2+ with high Langmuir capacities of 18.39, 20.63, 30.81 and 101.45 mg·g−1, respectively. The effects of environmental factors such as pH and humic acid (HA) on the removal of pollutants by ZVI-ZL-BC were explored. Additionally, the competitive removal behaviors and underlying mechanisms of the four target pollutants were also explored. This work demonstrates the feasibility for resource utilization of waterworks sludge and low-cost ZVI fabrication, which can effectively remove urban non-point source pollutants and bring potential environmental and economic benefits.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7221089665.title: Zero-valent iron-zeolite-biochar composites derived from waterworks sludge and rice husk for removal of typical pollutants in urban non-point source wastewater

W7221096057.abstract: The growing demand for environmentally sustainable materials has encouraged the development of biodegradable polymer nanocomposites with improved functional properties. In the present study, ZnO/tapioca starch nanocomposite films were fabricated by combining hydrothermally synthesized ZnO nanoparticles with a tapioca starch matrix through a solution-casting process. The influence of ZnO incorporation on the structural, morphological, chemical, and optical characteristics of the films was investigated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV-Visible spectroscopy, and photoluminescence (PL) analysis. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of crystalline hexagonal ZnO in the nanocomposite films. The average crystallite size decreased from 60 nm for pristine ZnO to 39 nm and 33 nm for ZnTp1 and ZnTp2, respectively, suggesting that the starch matrix restricted crystal growth during film formation. FESEM images revealed a corresponding reduction in particle size and a more uniform particle distribution with increasing tapioca content. FTIR spectra showed the characteristic absorption bands of both ZnO and tapioca starch without the appearance of new chemical bonds, indicating that the interaction between the inorganic nanoparticles and the polymer matrix was predominantly physical and governed by hydrogen bonding. The optical behaviour of the nanocomposite films was influenced by the incorporation of ZnO nanoparticles. UV-Visible measurements showed enhanced absorption in the ultraviolet region together with a slight decrease in the optical band gap from 3.56 to 3.49 eV. Photoluminescence spectra exhibited characteristic near-band-edge emission along with visible defect-related emission associated with intrinsic ZnO defects, indicating changes in the defect structure after incorporation into the starch matrix. Overall, the results demonstrate that hydrothermal synthesis combined with solution casting provides an effective route for preparing biodegradable ZnO/tapioca nanocomposites films with improved structural and optical characteristics.
W7221096057.journal: American Journal of Polymer Science and Technology
W7221096057.title: Hydrothermal-Assisted Fabrication of Eco-Friendly ZnO/Tapioca Nanocomposite Films with Enhanced Structural and Optical Properties

W7221097625.abstract: Nanocrystalline cellulose/zein (NCC/zein) bioplastic films coupled with maleic anhydride (MAH) were prepared from sugar-palm solid waste and corn waste to valorize agricultural biomass into biodegradable film materials. NCC was isolated from sugar-palm solid waste, whereas zein was extracted from corn waste with aqueous ethanol. Films containing 0-5 wt.% NCC were produced by melt intercalation using MAH and characterized by FTIR, 1H NMR, XRD, tensile testing, TG/DTA, soil burial and SEM. FTIR bands at 3431.51, 2879.85, 1635.71 and 1074.40 cm–1 confirmed hydrogen-bonded OH/NH, C-H, carbonyl and C-O groups in the coupled matrix. After correction of stress units, the highest tensile strength and elongation at break were 3.535 MPa and 10.954% in NCC/zein 0%, while the highest apparent secant modulus at break was 60.02 MPa at 1 wt.% NCC. The maximum biodegradation occurred at 5 wt.% NCC with 2.7287% weight loss day–1. The results support further development of biomass-derived biodegradable films; however, the packaging suitability cannot be concluded without dedicated barrier, water-uptake and surface-wettability measurements.
W7221097625.title: Mechanical, Thermal and Biodegradation Properties of Maleic Anhydride-Coupled Nanocrystalline Cellulose/Zein Bioplastics Derived from Agricultural Biomass

W7221100829.title: Hydrolytic degradation of fused filament–fabricated polylactic acid: Architecture-dependent evolution of anisotropic tensile failure

W7221106550.abstract: Globally, large amounts of fruit peel waste from food processing remain underutilized. Therefore, in this study, an active packaging layer was manufactured from discarded pomelo peels using a simple, one-step thermocompression process. This active packaging layer (PPF) was then fabricated into a biodegradable multilayer film via a multilayer thermocompression process with polylactic acid (PLA) and a PLA/polybutylene adipate-co-terephthalate (PBAT) blend (PT) as the outer layer. The introduction of a polyester layer significantly increased the film density, resulting in markedly improved mechanical and barrier properties. Among all the biodegradable film structures tested, the PT/PPF/PT trilayer film exhibited the best overall mechanical and barrier performance. Although the PT/PPF/PT film had lower tensile strength and elongation at break, as well as slightly higher water vapor permeability than commercial PE film, it exhibited a lower oxygen transmission-related value and stronger antioxidant activity and retained substantial functional activity after 30 days of storage. This functional stability may be attributed to the protective sandwich structure, which helped retain bioactive compounds within the PPF layer. When applied for raspberry preservation, the PT/PPF/PT film could delay raspberry spoilage and prolong the postharvest life by at least 8 days. The multilayer polyester shell delays the degradation rate without compromising the system's overall degradability.
oa_topics: Postharvest Quality and Shelf Life Management
W7221106550.title: Development of a PLA/PBAT/pomelo peel-based antibacterial and antioxidant multilayer film for fresh raspberry preservation

W7221116355.abstract: This study presents a multimaterial robotic end-effector that combines compliant gripping structures with deformation sensing using thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) and conductive polylactic acid (PLA). Four lattice geometries—diamond, hexagonal, triangular, and square—were evaluated through robotic pick-and-place experiments, electrical-response measurements, and cyclic durability tests. Each geometry was tested until visible structural damage, permanent deformation, or loss of functionality was observed; consequently, the accumulated number of cycles depended on the durability of each lattice. The triangular lattice exhibited localized fractures and limited cyclic durability, completing 1200 pick-and-place repetitions and approximately 900 sensor cycles. The hexagonal lattice provided an intermediate balance between functional durability and electrical response, completing 4350 pick-and-place repetitions and approximately 4984 sensor cycles. The square lattice completed 2850 pick-and-place repetitions but exhibited permanent deformation and did not complete the conductive-sensor durability test. The diamond lattice achieved the most favorable overall performance, completing 5700 accumulated pick-and-place repetitions without visible defects and approximately 9969 sensor cycles over 72 h while maintaining a periodic ADC response. These findings demonstrate that lattice geometry considerably influences grasping performance, structural integrity, electrical responsiveness, and cyclic durability. Therefore, an integrated assessment of these characteristics is required when selecting a lattice geometry for sensorized compliant gripping. Under the evaluated experimental conditions, the diamond lattice is recommended for the repetitive manipulation of delicate or irregular objects, whereas the hexagonal lattice represents an alternative when a balance between functional durability and electrical response is required.
W7221116355.title: Experimental Evaluation of Lattice Geometries for a Soft Robotic End-Effector

W7221117782.title: Effect of raster angle and layer thickness on fracture behavior of 3D printed Wood/PLA composites under different loading rates: statistical validation using ANOVA

W7221119763.abstract: Abstract Light-driven self-propelled microrobots offer opportunities for active environmental remediation by enabling controllable interactions with dispersed pollutants in aqueous environments. Here, we report biohybrid microrobots, composed of enzyme-functionalized, Au-decorated cubic hematite, that reversibly switch between clustered and dispersed states to enhance microrobot-substrate interactions and photoenzymatic degradation. In the dark, microrobots spontaneously assemble into interconnected filamentous clusters. Under blue-light irradiation, these clusters disassemble into self-propelled microrobots, increasing catalyst exposure and promoting broader microrobot-substrate interactions. Applied to polylactic acid (PLA) plastics, this collective-to-individual transition increases repeated microrobot-substrate contacts and promotes ester-bond hydrolysis at the polymer-water interface. Mass spectrometry identifies soluble PLA-derived oligomers, while electron microscopy reveals localized surface erosion after photoenzymatic treatment. By dynamically redistributing enzyme-functionalized microrobots across the polymer surface, reversible light-controlled switching enhances transient catalytic interactions and surface exploration. This strategy provides a general approach for optimizing photoenzymatic degradation by coupling collective organization, active motion, and catalyst accessibility in aqueous environments, while preserving reversible control over their spatial organization and activity.
W7221119763.title: Light-driven biohybrid microrobots for contact-enhanced photoenzymatic degradation of plastic debris

W7221128776.abstract: Background: Isosorbide dinitrate (ISDN) and hydralazine hydrochloride (HDZ) are dual cardiovascular drugs used to treat heart failure. However, the drugs have limitations such as short plasma half-life, low bioavailability, and potential for tolerance of the nitrate component. To address the need for prolonged drug release, a floating dual-compartment drug delivery system was developed to provide controlled drug release under simulated gastric dissolution conditions. Objectives: This study aimed to develop floating dual-compartment devices (FDCDs) to contain ISDN and HDZ gel and modify drug release under simulated gastric conditions. Methods: The FDCD was designed in a cylindrical shape consisting of an air chamber on the upper part for floating ability, and two compartments for loaded drug gel and controlling the drug release rate. Fused deposition modeling (FDM) was selected to fabricate FDCDs using polylactic acid (PLA) filament. The ISDN formulation varied the ratio of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) to achieve drug release for 12 h. The HDZ formulation was optimized by varying the ratio of PVP and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) to extend drug release at 24 h. Results: The shape dimension and weight variation in the FDCDs showed low standard deviation (SD). FDCDs exhibited immediate floating, resisted overturning, and demonstrated in vitro floating ability for more than 24 h. The formulation ISDN3 at a PVP: drug: water ratio of 5:2:3 exhibited complete release at 12 h, while the formulation of HDZ1 at an HPMC: PVP: drug: water ratio of 0.3:2.5:2:5.2 showed complete release within 24 h. The ISDN3- and HDZ1-loaded FDCDs demonstrated prolonged release behavior, with ISDN and HDZ release profiles showing the best fit to the zero-order and Higuchi models, respectively, based primarily on the coefficient of determination (R2), while root mean square error (RMSE) was used as a complementary measure of fitting error. Conclusions: These findings suggest that the developed dual-drug-loaded FDCD has potential as a dual-drug oral delivery platform for simultaneous delivery of ISDN and HDZ with prolonged drug release characteristics and further development of oral combination drug delivery systems.
W7221128776.title: 3D-Printed Gastroretentive Floating Modified-Release Device for Dual Cardiovascular Drug Delivery: Isosorbide Dinitrate and Hydralazine

W7221128921.abstract: The transition toward sustainable polymer systems is frequently framed as a material substitution challenge. However, the environmental performance of bio-based, biodegradable, and recyclable polymers is not an intrinsic property of feedstock origin but a system-dependent outcome shaped by energy inputs, infrastructure compatibility, economic feasibility, and governance alignment. This review provides a critical engineering assessment of sustainable polymer technologies based on systematic evidence screening (n = 193), bibliometric analysis, life cycle assessment (LCA) synthesis, techno-economic indicators, end-of-life scenario interpretation, and a multi-criteria evidence synthesis based on source-linked quantitative indicators and categorical evidence. To avoid treating these components as parallel but disconnected analyses, the synthesis explicitly links bibliometric clusters with LCA, TEA, and infrastructure evidence categories through an evidence-gap mapping matrix and confidence grading scheme. The findings indicate that bio-based polymers, such as PLA, PHA, and PBS, may achieve reduced greenhouse gas emissions under optimized production conditions; however, these advantages are highly sensitive to electricity carbon intensity, land-use assumptions, and end-of-life infrastructure. Quantitative LCA evidence indicates that polylactic acid (PLA) may achieve greenhouse gas emission reductions in the range of approximately 25–55% compared to conventional PET under low-carbon energy scenarios (1.3–3.0 vs. 2.0–3.5 kg CO2e/kg), while polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) show reductions of 10–40%, depending on fermentation efficiency and feedstock selection. However, these benefits can diminish or reverse under fossil-intensive energy mixes or when land-use change impacts are included, reinforcing the system-dependent nature of sustainability performance. Recyclability within established material streams frequently provides more stable long-term performance than biodegradable alternatives deployed without controlled composting systems. Evidence-strength analysis reveals moderate confidence in carbon footprint comparisons, weak-to-moderate confidence in techno-economic scalability claims, and conditional confidence in infrastructure-dependent outcomes. The results demonstrate that sustainable polymers are system-dependent technologies rather than inherently sustainable materials. Future engineering research must prioritize integrated LCA–TEA modeling, infrastructure-aligned material design, scenario-based end-of-life assessment, and harmonized sustainability reporting standards to enable scalable and verifiable circular polymer systems.
W7221128921.title: Sustainable Polymers as System-Dependent Technologies: A Critical Engineering Assessment of LCA Evidence, Circular Compatibility, and Scalability Constraints

W7221135868.abstract: Additively manufactured implants may be vulnerable to localized corrosion within narrow gaps, yet the critical crevice geometry and the effectiveness of multilayer coatings under such conditions remain insufficiently understood. This study compares the crevice-corrosion behavior of direct metal laser sintering (DMLS) and conventionally wrought mill-annealed Ti-6Al-4V alloys and evaluates a hierarchical coating comprising a plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) layer, a polycaprolactone (PCL) seal, and a porous polylactic acid (PLA) breath-figure topcoat. Electrochemical testing was conducted in simulated body fluid (SBF, pH 7.4, 37 °C) using a tapered crevice cell, followed by microscopic, compositional, and topographical analyses. Both uncoated alloys exhibited passive film breakdown; however, the wrought alloy subsequently repassivated, whereas the DMLS alloy underwent sustained localized attack within the critical crevice gap of ~11.4 µm. The transpassive potentials for DMLS and wrought Ti-6Al-4V with PEO/PCL/PLA coating system were 1.32 V and 1.45 V, respectively. Despite the intrinsic porosity and interfacial gaps of the coating, no crevice-type damage was detected in DMLS Ti-6Al-4V. PCL/PLA hierarchy increased the PEO pore resistance to ~3.5 kΩ cm2, reduced the passive current density by ~2 times, and increased the PEO barrier layer resistance to 107 Ω cm2.
W7221135868.title: Crevice Corrosion Mitigation in Ti-6Al-4V DMLS Alloy via Hybrid PEO/PCL/PLA Hierarchical Coatings for Biomedical Implants

W7221136377.abstract: Abstract In freshwater environments, microplastics (MPs) have emerged as important organic contaminants vectors. This study investigates the individual and combined toxicity of microparticles of polystyrene (PS) and polylactic acid (PLA) with two contaminants of major concern in Spanish waters─pyrene (PYR) and methyl chlorpyrifos (CPF). Adsorption behavior was assessed using adsorption isotherms fitted to mathematical models such as Henry, Langmuir, Freundlich, and Temkin. PYR adsorption on both polymers followed monolayer behavior (Langmuir model), while CPF adsorption was best described by the Freundlich model, indicating heterogeneous multilayer adsorption. Toxicity of these particles was assessed in Daphnia magna using acute and chronic toxicity assays. Acute toxicity tests showed that coexposure to MPs and contaminants increased immobilization, suggesting that adsorption onto MPs may influence contaminant partitioning and exposure. When organisms were exposed only to the contaminant remaining in the aqueous phase of CPF and PYR (after adsorption), EC50 values increased due to this reduced concentration. Regarding chronic exposure, significant effects were observed on Daphnia survival and reproduction, particularly when PS contained adsorbed contaminants on its surface. Therefore, this study indicates that MPs modify contaminant behavior and provides mechanistic insight relevant for understanding contaminant exposure and hazard processes in aquatic systems.
W7221136377.title: Toxicity Evaluation of Microplastics Exposure in Water Contaminated with Pyrene and Methyl Chlorpyrifos Using Daphnia magna

W7221147116.title: Insights into the polymorphic photoaging of microplastics: physical aspects and molecular level

W7221147798.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrospun nanofibers based on advanced polymers have emerged as versatile materials with significant promise in environmental and biomedical domains. With an emphasis on catalytic wastewater treatment and biomedical systems, this study provides a thorough analysis of the design concepts, functionalization techniques, and real‐world uses of bio‐polymer‐based electrospun nanofibers. The use of biodegradable and sustainable polymers, such as chitosan, gelatin, cellulose, and polylactic acid (PLA), which have special physicochemical qualities including biocompatibility and high surface area, is emphasized. Their catalytic and therapeutic activity is improved when functional nanomaterials, such as metal nanoparticles, metal oxides, and enzymes, are incorporated into a nanofibrous matrix. These functionalized nanofibers show excellent efficacy in microbial inactivation, biofouling resistance, and pollutant degradation in wastewater treatment. Because of their advantageous biological interactions and adaptable architectures, they are used in biomedical applications for antibacterial activity, wound healing, medication delivery, and tissue engineering. The review also discusses surface modification methods, fabrication difficulties, and the requirement for environmentally sustainable, scalable production. The subject of multifunctional nanofibrous systems for sustainable and health‐oriented applications is further advanced by highlighting current limitations and offering insights into potential future advancements that could bridge lab research and practical implementation.
W7221147798.title: Engineering Multifunctional Polymer‐Based Electrospun Nanofibers for Sustainable Environmental Remediation and Biomedical Technologies

W7221158401.abstract: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. Despite their potential, several challenges impede their widespread adoption. Key challenges include the inherent hydrophilicity of cellulose, which affects the mechanical and barrier properties of the bioplastics, and the complex, energy-intensive extraction and processing methods required to convert cellulose into usable forms. Additionally, achieving the desired thermal and mechanical properties for various applications often necessitates the use of additives or blending with other biopolymers, which can complicate the production process and affect biodegradability. Future prospects for cellulose-based bioplastics hinge on advancements in materials science and processing technologies. Innovative approaches such as chemical modifications, nanocellulose reinforcement, and the development of novel cellulose derivatives are being explored to enhance the performance characteristics of cellulose bioplastics. Furthermore, integrating green chemistry principles and improving the scalability of production processes are critical for reducing costs and environmental footprint. Research into the lifecycle assessment and end-of-life scenarios of these bioplastics is essential to ensure their sustainability credentials. Incentivizing research and development, coupled with supportive regulatory frameworks, can accelerate the transition towards cellulose-based bioplastics. Ultimately, these materials hold significant potential to contribute to a circular economy by reducing reliance on fossil fuels, lowering greenhouse gas emissions, and minimizing plastic pollution. The journey towards fully realizing this potential is ongoing, necessitating continuous innovation and commitment to sustainable practices.
W7221158401.title: Cellulose-based bioplastics for a circular bioeconomy: Properties, applications, market potential, consumer acceptance, and future perspectives

W7221159029.abstract: Glycolic acid (GA) is an important platform chemical with applications in biodegradable polymers, cosmetics, and pharmaceutical synthesis; however, traditional petrochemical routes raise environmental concerns, and current microbial production platforms remain constrained by acid toxicity. In this study, systematic metabolic engineering combined with fermentation optimization was implemented to construct an efficient GA biosynthetic pathway in the acid-tolerant non-conventional yeast Issatchenkia orientalis. To redirect the metabolic flux of the glyoxylate cycle, the Arabidopsis thaliana glyoxylate reductase (AtGLYR), with a catalytic efficiency approximately 74-fold higher than that of the native yeast enzyme, was heterologously expressed, coupled with the overexpression of endogenous isocitrate lyase (ICL) and the knockout of the competing malate synthase (MLS) gene. Furthermore, a heterologous xylose assimilation pathway was integrated into the engineered strain to rescue the growth deficiency caused by mls deletion. Subsequent fermentation optimization via an ethanol–xylose co-feeding strategy and calcium carbonate supplementation effectively further improved GA accumulation. Ultimately, the optimized engineered strain yielded a maximum GA titer of 712.42 mg/L in shake-flask fermentation. This work validates the potential of I. orientalis as a robust chassis microbe for sustainable GA biosynthesis and broadens the product portfolio of metabolic engineering applications for this yeast strain.
W7221159029.title: Xylose-Assisted Glycolic Acid Overproduction in Engineered Issatchenkia orientalis

W7221198683.title: Hybrid GA–ANFIS Optimization of Fused Deposition Modeling Processing Parameters for Enhanced Mechanical Performance of Polylactic Acid Components

W7221215212.abstract: Η αυξανόμενη συσσώρευση πλαστικών αποβλήτων έχει ενισχύσει το ενδιαφέρον για την ανάπτυξη βιοαποικοδομήσιμων πολυμερών, όπως οι πολυ(υδροξυαλκανοϊκοί) εστέρες (PHAs), ως εναλλακτική λύση στα συμβατικά πλαστικά πετροχημικής προέλευσης. Στην παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία διερευνήθηκε η παραγωγή του συμπολυμερούς πολυ(3-υδροξυβουτυρικό-co-3-υδροξυβαλερικό) (PHBV) από το κυανοβακτήριο Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, με αξιοποίηση αναερόβιας απορροής (Anaerobic Digestion Effluent, ADE) ως εναλλακτικού υποστρώματος καλλιέργειας. Αρχικά, μελετήθηκε η επίδραση του περιορισμού αζώτου και φωσφόρου, καθώς και της προσθήκης οξικού, στη συσσώρευση PHBV. Η παρουσία οξικού ενίσχυσε σημαντικά την παραγωγή του βιοπολυμερούς, με εντονότερη επίδραση υπό συνθήκες έλλειψης αζώτου. Σε fed-batch καλλιέργεια με 7,5% v/v ADE, η συγκέντρωση της βιομάζας έφτασε περίπου 1,1 g L⁻¹, ενώ επιτεύχθηκε απομάκρυνση 99% του αμμωνιακού αζώτου και 90% του ολικού φωσφόρου. Κατά τη φάση χλώρωσης, η υψηλότερη περιεκτικότητα σε PHBV, περίπου 21% w/w, επιτεύχθηκε με αρχική προσθήκη 2 g L⁻¹ οξικού. Παράλληλα, η προσθήκη οξικού ήδη κατά τη φάση ανάπτυξης επέτρεψε την ταυτόχρονη παραγωγή βιομάζας και PHBV σε μικρότερο χρόνο, με μέγιστη περιεκτικότητα περίπου 13% w/w. Τέλος, διερευνήθηκε η αξιοποίηση του PHB ως πολυμερικού φορέα για την ενθυλάκωση αμοξικιλλίνης με τη μέθοδο διπλού γαλακτώματος (W1/O/W2). Η υψηλότερη απόδοση ενθυλάκωσης, 56%, επιτεύχθηκε για θεωρητική φόρτωση φαρμάκου 5%, ενώ υψηλότερες φορτίσεις οδήγησαν σε μειωμένη απόδοση. Συνολικά, τα αποτελέσματα αναδεικνύουν τη δυνατότητα αξιοποίησης της ADE για την καλλιέργεια κυανοβακτηρίων και την παραγωγή PHAs προστιθέμενης αξίας, καθώς και την προοπτική αξιοποίησης των βιοπολυμερών αυτών σε εφαρμογές ελεγχόμενης χορήγησης φαρμάκων.
W7221215212.title: Production of polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) through the cultivation of Synechocystis sp. in anaerobic digestion effluent : effect of acetate and application in amoxicillin encapsulation

W7221269272.abstract: Lignin is a complex natural polymer within the plant cell wall that provides rigidity, mechanical strength, and pathogen defense. Historically dismissed as a mere byproduct of the pulp and paper industry, it is now recognized as a strategic feedstock for the global bioeconomy. This review examines its molecular architecture, structural diversity, and current extraction methods. Furthermore, it analyzes emerging applications in bioplastics, composite materials, carbon fibers, adhesives, and high-value platform chemicals. Finally, the main technical and economic challenges hindering its industrial-scale valorization are discussed, highlighting lignin’s pivotal role in the transition toward a sustainable and circular economy.
W7221269272.title: Lignina: El tesoro para una industria sostenible

W7221307612.abstract: Worldwide, 10 to 40 million tons of microplastics (MPs) are emitted annually into the environment, redistributing across environmental compartments and affecting organisms. Current life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) methods partially account for their impacts on ecosystem quality by considering a limited number of compartments and particles. This study advances the work of the MarILCA group by introducing the PEBBLE method which integrates physical effects of MPs, tire and road wear particles (TRWPs), and cellulosic microfibers across environmental compartments into life cycle assessment (LCA). Characterization factors (CFs) are developed for 10 conventional polymers, 6 biodegradable polymers, 6 cellulosic materials, and TRWPs, for multiple shapes and sizes. Particle fate is modelled using the SimpleBox object-oriented (SBoo) model for microparticles, computing fate factors (FFs) in air, terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments at continental and global scales, following USEtox regionalization. SBoo was improved to account for size and shape effects, refined degradation data, regional marine currents, and biofouling. FFs are combined with exposure and effect factors in water, sediments, and terrestrial environments to obtain updated CFs. Uncertainty is quantified using Monte Carlo simulation, and time-horizon-dependent CFs are computed. Results are provided for different LCIA methods: for IMPACT World+ and ReCiPe, CFs representing regional species loss are derived, while for GLAM, the Global Extinction Probability is applied to derive CFs representing global species loss. The results support environmental decision-making for plastics and their alternatives, and aim to be the consolidated version of MarILCA CFs for microparticles, ready for implementation in LCA tools and methods.
W7221307612.title: MarILCA characterization factors for microplastics, tire particles and cellulosic fibers in life cycle assessment: the PEBBLE method for regionalized physical impacts in marine, freshwater and terrestrial ecosystems

W7221308931.journal: Composites Part A Applied Science and Manufacturing
W7221308931.title: Soft-Hard interfacial engineering for optimized mechanical properties of magnesium alloy/polylactic acid films

W7221312710.abstract: In recent years, bioplastics have been developed as a biodegradable alternative to conventional plastics. Commonly used for single-use packaging, it is expected that bioplastics will follow a similar trajectory and enter the aquatic environment, yet in comparison to conventional plastics, little is known about the effect on aquatic species. Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), a popular bioplastic, has been reported to have similar effects to conventional plastics at an acute and chronic level. The objective of this study was to determine if PHB microplastics (micro-PHBs) (10–80 µm) alter cellular viability and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in Poeciliopsis lucida hepatocellular carcinoma (PLHC-1) cells, while using nano-polystyrene (nano-PS) (100 nm) as a control particle throughout. After 24 h exposure, micro-PHB (100–400 mg/L) and nano-PS (20–80 mg/L) had no effect on cellular viability in the alamarBlue (AB) assay, but a significant difference to the negative control was demonstrated with the Neutral Red (NR) assay. To date, limited data on the toxicological mixture effects of micro-PHB and environmental contaminants have been documented. Copper (II) chloride (CuCl2) was chosen as a traditional contaminant to investigate mixture effects. Although an essential element, copper can be toxic and an oxidative stress inducer at elevated concentration levels. The half maximal effective concentration (EC50) for CuCl2 (AB = 104.5 mg/L; NR = 90.5 mg/L) was higher when mixed with nano-PS with the AB assay (EC50 = 120.2 mg/L) and NR assay (EC50 = 115.7 mg/L), although the overlapping confidence intervals indicate that these differences should be interpreted cautiously. Micro-PHB had no effect on CuCl2 cellular viability toxic units. It was determined that micro-PHB (>100 mg/L) and nano-PS (20–80 mg/L) significantly increased oxidative stress with a dose-dependent response. While exposure to CuCl2 significantly induced ROS, a dose–response relationship was not found. Co-exposure of CuCl2 and each particle produced variable ROS responses across trials, dependent on polymer type and CuCl2 concentration. These results suggest that specific conventional and bioplastics may have the capacity to alter the toxicological effects of a contaminant such as copper, although this effect requires further investigation. Before bioplastics are adopted as an “environmentally friendly” alternative to conventional plastics, further toxicological evaluations are warranted.
W7221312710.title: Evaluation of the Cytotoxic and Oxidative Stress Effects of Polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) Microplastics Mixed with Copper on PLHC-1 (Poeciliopsis lucida) Cells

W7221321612.abstract: Unlocking the full economic and environmental potential of lignocellulosic biorefineries hinges on overcoming the critical bottleneck of residual lignin valorization. This study introduces an integrated, solvent-free paradigm to directly transform enzymatic hydrolysis lignin (EHL) from corn stover into high-strength polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites. By modulating the severity of an upstream green oxalic acid pretreatment (140, 180, and 220 °C), structure-property relationships dictating composite performance were elucidated. Comprehensive FTIR, GPC, TG, XPS, and the 13 C CPMAS solid-state NMR analyses unveiled temperature-dependent evolution of EHL, with pronounced depolymerization at 180 °C yielded a highly mobile lignin matrix characterized by lower T g (92 °C) and T m (177 °C), whereas 220 °C triggered profound structural re-polymerization. Direct thermal blending of raw EHL with PLA, without prior chemical modification or solvents, increased the tensile strength. The optimal formulation containing 10 wt% EHL derived at 220 °C increased the tensile strength to above 60 MPa, while the stiffness remained comparable to that of neat PLA. Concurrently, the 180 °C pretreatment delivered an unparalleled operational balance between macroscopic property enhancement and holistic process sustainability. Under the stated model assumptions, the techno-economic analysis indicated potential economic competitiveness, with minimum selling prices of USD 2.65/kg (10 wt% loading) and USD 2.38/kg (20 wt% loading). Sensitivity analysis identified the PLA purchase price and EHL-PLA annual production rate as the principal economic drivers. This work demonstrates the potential of raw EHL as a biopolymer additive and provides a basis for integrating biochemical fractionation with thermoplastic engineering toward more sustainable plastics.
W7221321612.title: Direct utilization of enzymatic hydrolysis lignin in high-strength polylactic acid biocomposites: Performance and techno-economic assessment

W7221322965.title: Rapid bisphenol A removal from contaminated sediment by plant-assisted bioelectro-Fenton through interfacial enrichment and Fe/Cu-mediated H2O2 activation

W7221329349.abstract: The construction sector is seeking sustainable alternatives to conventional building materials to reduce carbon emissions and promote circular economy practices. This study developed gypsum–biochar composites using date-palm-waste biochar at a fixed 20:80 biochar:gypsum mass ratio and evaluated water content, polymeric additives (SBR, RDP, and BT), and drying conditions. FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDS, FESEM, and BET characterized the raw materials. Optimum water contents were 55 wt% relative to gypsum and 70 wt% relative to biochar. Excess water reduced strength, whereas insufficient water impaired workability. SBR gave the best room-temperature performance among the additives. Oven drying at 60 °C for 24 h increased the strengths of SBR-, RDP-, and BT-modified composites from 3.60, 2.43, and 2.97 MPa to 6.35, 5.89, and 6.63 MPa, respectively; the unmodified composite reached 8.25 MPa. The results support the use of waste-derived biochar in lightweight, non-load-bearing interior components, although other biochar replacement levels and durability properties require evaluation.
W7221329349.journal: Proceedings of International Structural Engineering and Construction
oa_topics: Recycling and utilization of industrial and municipal waste in materials production
W7221329349.title: ASSESSMENT OF ADDITIVES AND WATER CONTENT EFFECTS ON THE COMPRESSIVE STRENGTH OF GYPSUM-BIOCHAR COMPOSITES

W7221339501.abstract: Tendons are highly elastic connective tissues that transfer mechanical loads from muscle to bone, and their healing is often slow and incomplete because of limited vascularization. Tissue engineering approaches are therefore emerging as promising alternatives to support tendon repair. In this study, polylactic acid (PLA)-based nanofibers containing hyaluronic acid (HA) and collagen (COL), intrinsic components of the extracellular matrix, were fabricated by blend and coaxial electrospinning. Matrices of identical overall composition were produced by both configurations, so that the contribution of nanofiber architecture could be isolated from that of chemical composition; the coaxial nanofibers comprised a load-bearing PLA/COL core and a PLA/HA shell, reproducing the collagen-rich tendon proper and the hyaluronic acid-rich gliding surface of native tendon. Mean fiber diameters ranged from 319 ± 82 nm for neat PLA to 854 ± 220 nm for the coaxial nanofibers, approximately twice that of the compositionally identical blend nanofibers (454 ± 110 nm). Tensile strength increased from 2.108 MPa for neat PLA to 4.94 MPa for PLA/COL, and the coaxial nanofibers retained a comparable value (4.651 MPa, p > 0.05) despite the incorporation of HA. In human mesenchymal stem cells, viability was maintained or increased over 7 days on the coaxial scaffolds but declined markedly on the blend scaffolds, indicating that the core–shell architecture is more favorable for tendon tissue regeneration.
W7221339501.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Polylactic Acid/Hyaluronic Acid/Collagen Nanofibers for Tendon Tissue Engineering

W7221341845.abstract: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a promising biodegradable polymer, but its inherent brittleness and limited thermal stability restrict broader applications. Bamboo charcoal (BC), possessing porous structure and large specific surface area, can be incorporated as a filler into PLA to improve the performance of PLA-based composites. Nevertheless, the structure-property relationship in BC/PLA composites with varying loadings of BC remains unclear. In this study, BC/PLA composites containing 0-50 wt% BC were prepared by melt blending, and the effects of BC loading on mechanical properties, crystallization behavior, thermal stability, morphology, and wettability were systematically investigated. When 10 wt% BC was mixed with PLA, the tensile strength of BC/PLA composites increased to 45.40 MPa, enhancing by 21.55% in comparison with pure PLA (37.35 MPa). Further increasing BC loading led to a gradual decline in strength and ductility because of BC aggregation and interfacial defects. Meanwhile, BC promoted crystallization of the PLA phase, increasing the PLA-content-normalized crystallinity from 6.20% to 56.97%, while the POM images showed qualitative changes in birefringent morphology. Thermogravimetric analysis showed that initial degradation temperature was reduced after adding BC, but the char residue was increased, reaching 44.55% at 500°C for PBC-50. Furthermore, the results suggested that the property evolution of BC/PLA composites is governed by a transition from reinforcement-dominated behavior at low BC loadings, followed by a competitive regime at intermediate loadings and an aggregation-dominated regime at high loadings.
W7221341845.title: Effects of bamboo charcoal (BC) loading on the properties of BC/PLA composites

W7221347986.abstract: Deep skin wounds are responsible for severe trauma and raise quite a concern in the healthcare sector. Compared to traditional dressings, polymeric hydrogels are considered effective in treating wounds and are considered functional wound healing material. Natural polymers, like chitosan, alginate, gelatin, dextran, cellulose, collagen, etc., possess excellent biodegradability, cellular compatibility, and bioactivity, making them effective in promoting tissue regeneration and cellular adhesion. However, they have certain limitations, including relatively poor mechanical properties, high chances of microbial contamination, and batch-to-batch variability. Whereas synthetic polymers such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), polylactic acid (PLA), polyvinyl alcohol (PVA), etc. provide appreciable mechanical strength and controlled degradation rates. However, there remains concern regarding their biocompatibility and effective biological functionality. To maximize the benefit, natural and synthetic polymers can be combined to provide synergistic efficacy by associating the biological activity with improved physicochemical and mechanical properties. This review focuses on the types, characteristics, modifications, advantages, limitations, current research progress, and wound-healing properties of several natural and synthetic polymers, with a focus on their applications in advanced wound dressings. Finally, the review outlines the current perspective and future challenges of developing polymer-based hydrogels for wound healing.
W7221347986.title: Polymeric hydrogels in wound management: Recent progress and translational potential

W7221365183.abstract: This study intends to experimentally investigate the temperature-difference response in three-dimensional (3D)-printed polylactic acid (PLA) components filled with bio-based walnut shell/epoxy composites. A fixed 35 wt.% walnut shell particles are used with epoxy as a composite to fill the voids in the PLA-manufactured frames. The Taguchi L9 array modified the print angle (45°, 50°, and 55°), infill percentage (10%, 15%, and 20%), and number of walls (1, 2, and 3). Four thermocouples are used at fixed locations in the same laboratory enclosure, with a nominal electrical input of 100 W as the heating source. The response is specifically defined as the stable temperature difference (Δ T = T 2 − T 1 ), rather than thermal resistance or thermal conductivity. The mean and temporal standard deviation are calculated from the final five quasi-steady readings. Configuration L3 (45°, 20% infill, and three walls) produces the highest stable Δ T of 21.50 ± 0.14 K, which is 61.7% greater than that of the pure-PLA reference under identical test conditions. The larger-is-better Taguchi analysis ranked infill first (69% of the summed factor ranges), followed by print angle (20%) and number of walls (11%). As a result, this strategy may screen the temperature-difference response of samples containing agricultural waste fillers in additively manufactured hybrid polymer systems, depending on sample geometry. This in turn would offer a cost-effective, environmentally friendly, and efficient solution for cutting-edge thermal management in electronic insulation applications.
W7221365183.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part E Journal of Process Mechanical Engineering
W7221365183.title: Experimental investigation of temperature-difference response in 3D-printed PLA structures filled with bio-based walnut shell/epoxy composites

W7221461028.abstract: Abstract Paraquat (PQ) is a widely used herbicide categorized as an environmental contaminant due to its high toxicity and risk to aquatic ecosystems and human health. In this study, we developed a Screen-printed Disposable Polyethylene Terephthalate (SD-PET) sensor using a green sodium alginate/graphite conductive ink. To maximize performance, the electrode surface was modified with a bamboo biochar composite incorporating copper nanoparticles (BC-CuNPs). Under optimized differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) conditions, the BC-CuNPs sensor outperformed the other configurations, displaying excellent linearity for PQ detection from 10 to 250 µmol L −1 (R 2 = 0.988), a sensitivity of 0.0234 µA µmol −1 L, and limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) of 7.65 µmol L −1 and 25.48 µmol L −1 , respectively. Selectivity studies against common aquatic interferents (chloroquine, levofloxacin, and sulfamethoxazole) and tap water assays indicated mild matrix effects, though the device successfully quantified the analyte under competitive conditions. UV–Vis spectrophotometry validated the accuracy of the proposed method as an independent reference technique. Furthermore, the environmental sustainability of the device was quantitatively confirmed by green chemistry metrics, achieving a high AGREE score of 0.71 and a favorable ComplexGAPI profile. Despite presenting a limited shelf life over 21 days, the developed SD-PET/BC-CuNPs sensor stands out as a highly efficient, eco-friendly, and viable alternative for on-site environmental monitoring of paraquat.
W7221461028.title: Biochar copper nanocomposite modified sensor for the green electroanalytical sensing of paraquat

W7221461327.abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable polymer processing requires the replacement of conventional toxic solvents. However, limited information is available on how environmentally friendly solvents, particularly ethyl acetate (EA) as a sustainable alternative to chloroform (H), influence the structural, morphological, surface, and optical properties of spincoated poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) thin films. In this study, the effect of solvent selection on the properties of PCL thin films prepared by spin coating was investigated, highlighting the potential of EA as a more environmentally friendly alternative for PCL film fabrication. The films were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), contact angle measurements, and UV–Vis spectroscopy. XRD analysis confirmed the preservation of the orthorhombic crystalline structure of PCL, with similar crystallite size values indicating that the choice of solvent had no significant effect on the crystallization process or the size of the crystalline domains. SEM analysis showed that both films have a characteristic spherulite morphology, with the PCL-EA film forming larger spherulites than the PCL-H film. At the same time, the PCLEA film exhibited a higher surface free energy and a more pronounced polar component, with a measured surface free energy of 54.70 mN/m compared with 41.62 mN/m for the PCL-H film, indicating better wettability and more favorable interfacial interactions. UV–Vis analysis showed higher optical band gap values for both direct and indirect electronic transitions in the PCL-EA film compared to the PCL-H film, with direct and indirect band gap values of 5.0 eV and 4.8 eV for PCL-EA, and 4.8 eV and 4.1 eV for PCL-H, respectively, which may indicate a reduced number of localized energy states and greater structural order, with both films retaining the optical properties characteristic of PCL as an electrically insulating polymer. The results confirm that ethyl acetate is a suitable, more sustainable alternative to chloroform for preparing PCL thin films, thereby improving surface and optical properties while preserving the structural characteristics of the biodegradable polymer. Such thin films have potential applications in sustainable polymer coatings, packaging materials, and other environmentally friendly technologies, contributing to the development of greener polymer fabrication approaches.
W7221461327.title: Structure–Property Relationships of Eco-friendly Spincoated Poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) Thin Films

W7221467676.abstract: ABSTRACT Polyhydroxyalkanoates are biodegradable plastics that offer a sustainable alternative to petroleum‐based plastics, which are associated with environmental persistence and microplastic‐related health risks. However, because polyhydroxyalkanoates are stored intracellularly, their recovery requires cell disruption and extraction processes that are often costly and traditionally rely on toxic solvents such as chloroform. This study evaluated the impacts of biomass loading and incubation time on the use of 1:1 thymol–decanoic acid natural deep eutectic solvent for poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate) extraction from Cupriavidus necator KCTC 2649. Results showed that lower biomass loading resulted in higher poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate) recovery, while incubation time had no significant effect. The best condition from the factorial experiment was obtained at 1% w/v biomass loading and 1 h incubation time, yielding a recovery of 17.41% w/w and a purity of 93.97% w/w. The application of 45 kHz power ultrasound at 100% during the first 30 min of incubation further increased the recovery to 68.42% w/w under the selected extraction conditions. A more stringent washing was also applied to improve purity from 60.80% to 93.4% w/w. Response surface methodology experiment revealed that the optimum region is located near 3% w/v biomass loading and 5 h incubation time. Overall, the 1:1 thymol–decanoic acid natural deep eutectic solvent‐based extraction protocol produced a high‐quality poly(3‐hydroxybutyrate) powder with physicochemical characteristics comparable to those already available commercially.
W7221467676.title: Ultrasound‐Assisted Poly(3‐Hydroxybutyrate) Extraction from Cupriavidus necator KCTC 2649 Using Thymol–Decanoic Acid Natural Deep Eutectic Solvent

W7221481258.abstract: Darier disease (DD) is a rare autosomal dominant inherited keratinizing skin disorder caused by mutations in the ATP2A2 gene, which encodes the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca²⁺-ATPase 2 (SERCA2). The disease is characterized by abnormal keratinization, acantholysis, hyperkeratotic papules, nail abnormalities, and mucosal involvement. Although topical and systemic retinoids are commonly used for management, conventional topical therapy may be limited by poor drug solubility, inadequate skin penetration, and irritation. Therefore, advanced drug delivery systems may provide an effective approach for improving topical therapy. Lipid–polymer hybrid nanoparticles (LPHNPs) are innovative nanocarriers that combine the advantages of polymeric nanoparticles and lipid-based delivery systems. They generally consist of a biodegradable polymeric core surrounded by a lipid shell, providing improved drug encapsulation, enhanced stability, controlled drug release, and improved interaction with the skin. These characteristics make LPHNPs particularly promising for the delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs such as retinoids. This review summarizes the pathophysiology and therapeutic challenges of Darier disease, the principles of topical and nanotechnology-based drug delivery, and the structure, components, preparation methods, advantages, and applications of LPHNPs. The potential use of LPHNPs as a novel platform for improving topical drug delivery in Darier disease is also discussed. Overall, LPHNP-based delivery represents a promising strategy for enhancing drug localization, penetration, and controlled release, and may provide a potential approach for improving the management of Darier disease.
W7221481258.journal: International Journal of Pharmacology and Clinical Research (IJPCR)
W7221481258.title: A Review of Lipid Polymer Hybrid Nanoparticle in Skin Disease of Darier Disease

W7221503846.abstract: The coffee-making process generates substantial quantities of organic residues. Spent Coffee Grounds (SCG) represents a major waste stream produced after beverage preparation. Its rich composition in lipids, lignocellulosic fractions, proteins, phenolics and other bioactive compounds makes it a promising feedstock for integrated biorefineries. This review critically evaluates SCG valorisation routes for biofuels and value-added products, with particular attention to oil extraction, biodiesel production, defatted SCG (DSCG) utilisation and biorefinery development. Literature indicates that SCG generally contains approximately 10–20wt.% oil, with a biodiesel conversion efficiency of ∼95%. Nevertheless, biodiesel scalability remains constrained by high acidity, moisture removal, solvent recovery and feedstock logistics. Anaerobic digestion is promising, as DSCG can generate higher methane yields than SCG, with reported values of 336±7 mLCH4/gVS and 310±2 mLCH4/gVS, respectively. Pellet, biochar and activated carbon pathways appear more scalable because they require fewer high-purity separation steps, whereas bioethanol, nutraceutical, bioactive compound and bioplastic routes require more intensive pretreatment, extraction, purification and product validation. Technology Readiness Level, techno-economic feasibility, environmental benefit and scalability indicate that integrated biorefineries are more realistic than single-product valorisation. Coupling Techno-Economic Analysis with Life Cycle Assessment is essential for identifying SCG valorisation pathways that are technically feasible, environmentally beneficial and commercially viable.
W7221503846.title: Valorisation of Spent Coffee Grounds in integrated biorefineries: a comprehensive review of biofuels and value-added products potential

W7221505068.abstract: Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) lattices are attractive cellular architectures owing to their smooth, curvature-continuous geometry, high surface-to-volume ratio, and efficient load-bearing behavior. TPMS structures are widely investigated for lightweight and energy-absorption applications, including impact-resistant protection systems and medical scaffolds. In this work, dual-nozzle fused deposition modeling (FDM) is employed to fabricate single-phase TPMS specimens from polylactic acid (PLA), while a complementary phase structure (CPS) is fabricated from polyethylene terephthalate glycol (PETG). The combination of these phases results in an interpenetrating phase composite (IPC). Four sheet-based TPMS topologies, namely Primitive, Gyroid, Diamond, and I-graph-wrapped package (IWP), are investigated. Quasi-static compression experiments are conducted to characterize and compare the compressive performance of the interpenetrating architectures and their constituent-phase counterparts. The results demonstrate that IPC architectures outperform the TPMS and CPS phases, revealing a strong synergistic effect induced by phase interpenetration. This structural synergy promotes more uniform deformation and mitigates strain localization. The IWP, Gyroid, and Primitive topologies exhibit the greatest improvements in stiffness, whereas the Primitive and Gyroid architectures achieve the highest yield stress and energy absorption capacity.
W7221505068.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part L Journal of Materials Design and Applications
W7221505068.title: Quasi-static compression performance of multiphase 3D-printed PLA–PETG interpenetrating TPMS structures

W7221508388.abstract: ABSTRACT Biochar‐supported zero‐valent iron (ZVI‐biochar) is a promising material for groundwater remediation, and carbothermal reduction offers a simple, potentially scalable route for its production. However, this method requires high temperatures and typically results in low Fe(0) formation. This study demonstrates that introducing CO 2 during pyrolysis markedly enhances in situ Fe(0) formation at lower temperatures while simultaneously improving material reactivity and stability. Beech wood‐derived ZVI‐biochar prepared under a CO 2 :N 2 (1:9, v/v) atmosphere at 900°C exhibited a 1.7‐fold higher trichloroethylene (TCE) removal rate and a sixfold higher Fe‐normalized TCE dechlorination rate compared to that produced without CO 2 addition. The improved TCE reactivity (removal extent and rate) was primarily attributed to enhanced reductive transformation, driven by both increased Fe(0) formation and CO 2 ‐induced changes in the biochar matrix. The resulting ZVI‐biochar exhibited lower corrosion rates than other reported ZVI reactants and maintained high TCE reactivity even after prolonged exposure to air or water. It also achieved complete removal of other chlorinated ethylenes, including cis‐dichloroethylene and vinyl chloride, from contaminated groundwater. These findings demonstrate that CO 2 ‐assisted carbothermal treatment offers a simple and potentially scalable route for producing stable and reactive ZVI‐biochar composites for groundwater remediation, while avoiding the need for multi‐step syntheses using chemical reductants.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7221508388.title: CO 2 ‐Enhanced Carbothermal Production of Biochar‐Supported Zero‐Valent Iron for Efficient Chlorinated Ethylene Remediation

W7221515633.title: Sustainable All-PLA MEM nonwovens with hierarchical porous-wrinkled structure for high-performance air filtration

W7221516045.abstract: This study investigates the structural and thermal responses of maleic anhydride-modified polylactic acid (PLA) prepared through peroxide-initiated reactive melt processing using integrated Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA). The objective was to determine how MA content is associated with the local spectral environment, thermal-transition and crystallization behavior, and thermal stability of PLA. FTIR analysis revealed progressive variations in band intensity, broadening, asymmetry, and localized spectral distribution with increasing MA content, particularly in the carbonyl and fingerprint regions, while the characteristic PLA absorption framework remained identifiable. A weak shoulder at approximately 1630–1650 cm -1 was interpreted cautiously as a localized spectral variation rather than definitive evidence of a newly formed chemical structure. DSC showed lower glass transition temperatures (T g ) of 53.4–56.2 °C for the modified formulations compared with 64.8 °C for neat PLA and distinct cold-crystallization peaks (T cc ) at 95.3–97.5 °C, while melting temperatures (T m ) remained within 174.5–176.7 °C. TGA showed that the temperature at 5% mass loss (T 5 %) decreased from 342.1 °C for neat PLA to 320.1–339.2 °C for the modified formulations, whereas the maximum degradation temperature (T max ) remained comparatively stable at 368.8–372.5 °C. Collectively, the integrated FTIR–DSC–TGA results demonstrate that MA-containing reactive melt processing is associated with distinct changes in spectral, thermal-transition, crystallization, and early-stage thermal responses, while key PLA characteristics remain identifiable. This integrated interpretation provides a basis for understanding how formulation changes are reflected across complementary spectral and thermal responses, supporting future studies on modified PLA materials.
W7221516045.title: Integrated FTIR, DSC, and TGA analyses of structural evolution and thermal behavior in maleic anhydride-modified polylactic acid prepared by reactive melt processing

W7221521052.abstract: This study reports the statistically optimized production of long-chain polyhydroxyalkanoate PHA-JO (LCL-PHA; with C16–C18 monomer units) by Paenibacillus lutimineralis JP-30 using non-edible Jatropha curcus oil (JO) as a low-cost, renewable carbon source. The key media component was identified and optimized by combining the Plackett-Burman design (PBD) approach with the response surface methodology (RSM). Jatropha oil, ammonium sulfate, and potassium dihydrogen phosphate were used to maximize the accumulation of PHA. The resulting optimized medium (37.0 g L-1 JO, 0.5 g L-1 (NH4)2SO4, 1.5 g L-1 KH2PO4, 0.5 g L-1 MgSO4, 1.0 mg L-1 NaCl) increased the polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) yield by 1.4-fold in shake-flask conditions (1.78 ± 0.05 g L-1) and by 88 % under bioreactor conditions (3.36 ± 0.04 g L-1) compared with the unoptimized media (1.30 ± 0.07 g L-1). The fitted quadratic model displayed strong predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.9019; adj R2 = 0.8137) and validated the statistical design. Further agitation optimization in a 3.2 L bioreactor (400 rpm, 36 h) enhanced biomass (3.77 ± 0.06 g L-1) and PHA-JO yield (Yp/x = 0.931), with highest mean volumetric productivity (Qp): 0.0837 ± 0.0137 g L-1/h at 36 h while highest mean specific productivity (qp): 0.0384 ± 0.0030 g/g/h at 12 h, These findings suggest that P. lutimineralis JP-30 has potential for converting non-edible Jatropha curcas oil into long-chain PHA under optimized laboratory conditions and may support further research on lipid valorisation.
W7221521052.title: Optimization of long-chain polyhydroxyalkanoate (LCL-PHA) biosynthesis from non-edible

W7221539132.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.
W7221539132.title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters

W7221541392.abstract: One of Egypt's biggest obstacles to sustainable agriculture is the lack of water. By assessing the effects of applying biochar composite (BC) which consists of biochar made from a mixture of wood (produced from woody ornamental nursery wastes) and biochar made from banana waste at a 2:1 (w/w) ratio either alone or in conjunction with tripartite microbial consortium comprising pure, active strains of Azotobacter chroococcum, Azospirillum lipoferum, and Bacillus polymyxa as plant growth promoters (PGPR), this study investigated sustainable methods to reduce water stress in Calendula (Calendula officinalis L.). During the growing seasons of 2023/2024 and 2024/2025, two factorial field experiments with a split-plot design were carried out at the Medicinal Plant Farm, Faculty of Pharmacy, Cairo University, Giza, Egypt. Three irrigation schedules were applied to calendula plants: normal (14-day intervals; I1), moderate water deficit (21-day intervals; I2), and severe water deficit (28-day intervals; I3). The most effective regime, according to the results, was the 21-day irrigation interval, which saved 16% to 21% of irrigation water without affecting the calendula plants' vegetative development, flowering, or chemical analysis. Co-application of Biochar composite (BC) and Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria PGPR demonstrated the best biological synergy under this mild stress. When compared to the untreated control, this combined treatment greatly improved vegetative growth, flowering characteristics, total carotenoids and total flavonoids, total chlorophyll (a and b), total carbohydrates, and nutritional levels (N, P, and K). Additionally, it maintained relative water content (RWC%), accumulated proline and phenolic contents, and increased phytohormones, antioxidant enzymes, and water productivity all of which substantially mitigated yield losses caused by drought. The co-application of Biochar composite (BC) and PGPR treatment under moderate water shortage (21-day intervals) might be suggested as a sustainable agronomic strategy to enhance vegetative growth, essential oil composition, and nutritional quality of Calendula plants based on the obtained results.
W7221541392.title: Physiological and Quality Responses of Calendula (Calendula officinalis L.) to Co-application of Biochar composite and PGPR under Water Deficit Conditions

W7221543651.abstract: Kazakhstan combines a large agricultural-residue base with an expanding grain-processing sector, creating a credible platform for biodegradable polymers if feedstock availability is matched to polymer chemistry, pretreatment intensity, and realistic end-of-life routes. This critical review integrates Kazakhstan-specific production data with the chemistry of starch, cellulose, hemicelluloses, lignin, and rice-husk silica and evaluates the conversion pathways most relevant to domestic implementation. Collectible dry residues from wheat, barley, maize, and rice are estimated at about 15.1 Mt yr−1, while potato and cereal starch streams provide directly processable carbohydrates. Near-term options are thermoplastic starch (TPS), cellulose/nanocellulose reinforcement, lignin-containing functional composites, and hybrid materials using rice-husk-derived silica. PLA and PHA offer higher-value routes but require fermentation, purification, polymerization or recovery, and dedicated end-of-life infrastructure. The review emphasizes molecular limitations—hydrogen-bonded polysaccharide networks, retrogradation, interfacial polarity mismatch, lignocellulosic recalcitrance, filler agglomeration, and environment-dependent biodegradation—and links them to processing and performance tests. A staged strategy is proposed: compound and reinforce existing starch streams first, build regional fractionation and standardized intermediate platforms next, and develop PLA/PHA fermentation only after low-cost carbon streams, product markets, and life-cycle advantages are demonstrated.
W7221543651.title: Renewable Lignocellulosic and Starch Feedstocks for Biodegradable Polymers in Kazakhstan: Resource Chemistry, Conversion Routes, and Implementation Priorities

W7221545837.title: Heat-resistant, high-strength, and thermally insulating biodegradable polyglycolic acid foams fabricated via supercritical CO2 foaming

W7221547805.abstract: Many studies have been carried out on pure polylactic acid (PLA) material to provide good roadmaps to additively manufacture this material when using Fused Filament Fabrication (FFF), which is considered one of the most used additive manufacturing (AM) techniques. Many recommendations can be found in the literature to address its mechanical properties and fabrication. However, there are few studies that provide recommendations and roadmaps for Wood-reinforced PLA (WrPLA) materials fabricated using the FFF technique. In addition, FFF machine manufacturers cannot guarantee the effectiveness of their produced machines in fabricating WrPLA materials, especially in terms of repeatability. In this review, the objective is to address the different challenges and issues representing the main obstacles, especially uncertainty issues, with the aim of industrializing this material, which paves the way to elaborate an Industrialization Standard for AM (IS4AM). Furthermore, since material properties represent a key point for this industrialization, several works are reviewed to help in identifying different issues and obstacles. After that, several suggestions and recommendations are provided considering our industrial experiences and the different existing works in the literature. These propositions and recommendations are provided to industrialize WrPLA materials when using the FFF technique. The most important recommendation is to develop advanced reliability strategies to reduce uncertainty cases. So, this review combines academic and industrial standpoints to reduce defect/defective cases in order to improve the mechanical properties of the resulting products, where a reciprocal validation between our industrial examples and the previous works in the literature is presented to help a large audience manage the different challenges in this area. This can then provide readers with ideas to handle WrPLA materials at the macromolecular level to reduce several certainty and uncertainty issues and to extend the use of WrPLA for several vital applications as well.
W7221547805.title: A Review of Different Challenges Related to Industrializing Additively Manufactured Wood-Reinforced Polylactic Acid Materials Using the Fused Filament Fabrication Technique

W7221549859.abstract: Vascular stents, serving as a cornerstone in the interventional treatment of cardiovascular diseases, had undergone rapid technological evolution and accumulation of clinical evidence. To systematically deconstruct the global research landscape, collaborative networks, and knowledge development pathways, we conducted a bibliometric and visual analysis of 5322 relevant articles (2015-2025) from the Web of Science Core Collection using VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The results showed that the annual publication growth had entered a plateau phase characterized by deepening integration, with the paradigm transitioning from discrete technological iteration toward system integration. Besides, keyword clustering identified four major research pillars including precision decision-making in revascularization, material innovation, personalized antiplatelet therapy, and evaluation based on clinical evidence. Notably, the intersection of materials science and biology (e.g., biodegradable polymers, immunomodulatory coatings) was the key driver of cutting-edge advancements. We further pointed out that future breakthroughs would depend on the deep integration of biodegradable smart materials, artificial intelligence-empowered precision intervention, and dynamic management based on real-world data. Therefore, we believe that the constructed knowledge graph and the proposed paradigm transition framework clarify the developmental trajectory and provide an evidence-based roadmap for future innovation.

W7221559148.abstract: Abstract The growing environmental concern over petroleum-based plastics has intensified the demand for sustainable alternatives with high performance and reliable processability. Bio-based plastics have attracted considerable attention as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-derived plastics. However, despite their environmental advantages, their development and application are severely constrained by the necessity for tedious chemical modification and complex processing. Herein, we propose a covalent adaptable network strategy to transform chitosan (CS) into a thermally processable bioplastic through simple and efficient dynamic covalent enamine cross-linking. The enamine bonds enable network rearrangement upon heating, imparting hot-press processability, thermal repairability, and closed-loop recyclability to the material. The resulting bioplastic exhibits a high flexural strength of 189.8 MPa, excellent moisture and solvent resistance, favorable recyclability, high thermal stability, a low thermal expansion coefficient of 1.05 ppm k−1, superior quantitative green chemistry metrics, and rapid soil-burial disintegration. With these advantageous features, the developed bioplastic represents a promising sustainable substitute for conventional petroleum-based plastics.
W7221559148.title: Facile Fabrication of Sustainable Chitosan Bioplastics Integrating High Strength, Water Resistance, and Closed-Loop Recyclability

W7221564256.abstract: Transdermal drug delivery is an effective and, for some substances, the only feasible method. The most effective and advanced method for its implementation is the use of microneedles made of bi-odegradable polymeric materials. This study proposes a method for producing transdermal delivery patches containing microneedles on their surface. The method involves developing a 3D model of the patch master mold, 3D printing it, filling the intermediate mold with polydimethylsiloxane, and then filling the patch with a biopolymer. The biopolymers studied were PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)), PLA (polylactic acid), and PDLLA (poly-d,l-lactic acid). PLGA showed the best results. Two microneedle array topology variants were used. In the first case, the needles were arranged in a 34 × 34 array with a tip-to-tip spacing of 500 µm and a height of 800 µm. The base thickness was 5 mm, and the side dimensions were 20 mm. A second design variant featuring larger needles was pro-posed; this array consisted of 21 × 21 needles with a height of 1.6 mm.
W7221564256.title: Transdermal Drug Delivery Using Biodegradable Microneedles
