W7222903619.abstract: Porous titanium scaffolds for bone repair require coordinated control of pore architecture, mechanical behavior, and surface bioactivity. Here, we report a sacrificial-template route based on polymer 3D printing that produces orientation-controlled porous titanium scaffolds with hierarchical macro- and microporosity without direct metal additive manufacturing. Polylactic acid lattices printed by fused deposition modeling are infiltrated with a titanium powder slurry and then subjected to template removal and sintering. The process yields ortho-grid, tri-lattice, and quad-lattice structures with approximately 26% isotropic linear shrinkage, 65%-67% porosity, preserved geometric fidelity, and a relative density of approximately 95% in the sintered strut walls. Uniaxial compression tests reveal architecture-dependent behavior along the tested loading direction, whereas finite element simulations predict lower directional sensitivity under off-axis loading as strut-orientation diversity increases. Micro-arc oxidation forms a Ca-P-containing microporous oxide layer and improves cell spreading, proliferation, and alkaline phosphatase activity relative to untreated titanium scaffolds in vitro. In a rat calvarial defect model, uncoated titanium scaffolds achieve bone regeneration comparable to commercial porous tantalum, while micro-arc oxidation further enhances bone formation. Fabrication of cone augments and other non-prismatic geometries further demonstrates the adaptability of the approach to complex implant-relevant structures.
W7222903619.title: Sacrificial‐Template Fabrication of Orientation‐Controlled Porous Titanium Lattices With Bioactive Surfaces

W7222916975.abstract: To support the national dual-carbon strategy, this study developed low-carbon solid-waste-based concretes, in which carbide slag or steel slag, together with ground granulated blast-furnace slag and desulfurization gypsum, fully replaced ordinary Portland cement, and compared the mechanical properties and microstructures of the two systems. The carbide slag binder was modified with chopped basalt fiber (0–0.30% by mass) for added toughness, with a 1% or 3% biochar as a basal component, whereas the steel slag binder was modified with corn-stalk biochar (1–7% by mass) as a partial fine-aggregate replacement for carbon sequestration. Compressive strength tests, together with XRD, SEM, TG/DTG and MIP, characterized both concretes. When tested at 7 days, the carbide slag concrete showed a first-rising-then-declining strength response to basalt fiber, strength increased from 3.24 MPa at 0.10% fiber to a maximum of 4.91 MPa at 0.25%, then dropped to 4.68 MPa at 0.30%, while the no-fiber baseline reached 3.17 MPa. The steel slag concrete was markedly stronger, the 1%-biochar fiber-free mix reaching 11.0 MPa at 7 days, larger than the 3.17 MPa recorded for the carbide slag binder under the matched condition, and climbing to 38.7 MPa after 28 days. Increasing biochar dosage penalized strength, the 3% mix reaching only 8.5 MPa at 7 days and the 5% and 7% mixes being too weak for valid testing; with further curing, however, all four steel slag mixes developed measurable strengths by 28 days, at 38.7, 32.6, 22.5 and 18.2 MPa for 1%, 3%, 5% and 7% biochar, respectively. Microstructurally, the steel slag system hydrated more fully, Ca(OH)2 being largely consumed to form C-S-H and calcite (CaCO3); TG/DTG gave a calcium carbonate content of about 24.8%, higher than the 16.6% measured for the carbide slag binder, and MIP revealed a markedly refined pore network, with the dominant pore size shifting from about 40 nm to about 10 nm and the sub-10 nm pore fraction rising from 2.2% to 4.0%, even though its total porosity was slightly higher, at 27.7% compared with 24.9% in the carbide slag binder. Both solid-waste concretes delivered adequate mechanical performance, with the steel slag system outperforming; basalt fiber and biochar acted as auxiliary modifiers that improved toughness and sequestered carbon, respectively, and their dosages, therefore, require careful control.
W7222916975.title: Compressive Strength and Microstructure of All-Solid-Waste Concretes Modified with Basalt Fiber or Biochar: A Comparative Study of Carbide Slag-Based and Steel Slag-Based Systems

W7222919189.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to report the implementation and initial experimental evaluation of an adaptive infill method for fused deposition modeling that combines cross-section-driven variable-density assignment with an explicit transition-layer branch triggered at detected geometric discontinuities, all operating at the slicing stage without external geometry modification or load-path input. Design/methodology/approach A continuous exponential mapping converts the slice-wise cross-sectional area sequence into a layer-specific infill density bounded by user-defined limits. A dual-criterion detection module identifies abrupt geometric transitions using area-change rate and centroid displacement; a sliding-window slope-exclusion rule prevents false detection on continuous gradients; densified reinforcement layers are inserted only at flagged abrupt interfaces. The two algorithmic branches were exercised separately on two test geometries – compression specimens with circular necked profiles and tensile specimens with rectangular stepped profiles – printed in polylactic acid (PLA) at 20\% baseline infill density with five specimens per group. Findings The adaptive group showed a marginal trend toward higher first peak force on compression specimens (5.6∼kN to 5.9∼kN, +5.4\%; Welch’s t-test, p = 0.054) and a statistically significant 15.4\% higher peak load on tensile specimens (803.2∼N to 926.8∼N; p = 0.043), with mass increases of 0.5\% and printing time increases below 7\%. A directional check with glycol-modified polyethylene terephthalate (PETG) at three specimens per group gave +14.2\% tensile peak-load difference (p = 0.0045), consistent in direction with the PLA result. Sparse-infill toolpath length differed from the uniform baseline by less than 1.5\%. The algorithm transferred without modification to three geometries of greater complexity. Originality/value This work presents an integrated implementation that combines an existing class of cross-section-driven variable-density assignment with an explicit transition-layer detection and reinforcement branch within a single slicing-level pipeline, together with per-layer diagnostic data that make the algorithm’s geometric decisions inspectable.
W7222919189.title: Adaptive infill method for FDM based on cross-section features and transition layers

W7222920298.abstract: The shortage and high cost of autologous bone grafts have created an urgent need to the development of biocompatible materials for bone defect repair. Bone is a natural piezoelectric tissue that generates electrical stimulation to induce osteogenic differentiation. However, most biodegradable polymers lack inherent piezoelectric properties, making the design of controllably degradable piezoelectric biomaterials particularly significant. In this work, poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) was used as a raw material to synthesize a polyurethane (PU)-based bio-ink consisting of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and hydroxyapatite (HA) via a one-step method. Personalized composite scaffolds (PU/PVDF/HA) were then fabricated by extrusion-based 3D printing. Characterization results from FTIR, XRD, water contact angle, and degradation tests confirmed the successful formation of PU/PVDF/HA composite scaffolds and demonstrated that the incorporation of HA effectively enhanced the bioactivity of the composite material with pronounced piezoelectric properties, suggesting potential relevance for osteogenic applications. Further, the PU/PVDF/HA15 group (containing 15 wt% HA and 5 wt% PVDF) had a good biocompatibility, which was clearly reflected by CCK-8 detection and live/death fluorescence imaging compared with the other groups. Overall, the synergistic action of piezoelectricity and bioactivity in PU/PVDF/HA scaffolds improved the physicochemical characteristics of the material-tissue interface, and then promoted the osteogenic activity. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the feasibility of integrating piezoelectric functionality and bioactivity into polymer-based scaffolds for bone tissue engineering.
W7222920298.journal: Journal of Biomaterials Science Polymer Edition
W7222920298.title: Piezoelectric-bioactive coupling of PVDF and hydroxyapatite for enhancing the interfacial bioactivity and osteogenic potential of the 3D-printed polyurethane scaffolds

W7222922119.abstract: The development of sustainable electrode materials for electrochemical nitrate removal from water has attracted increasing interest due to the need for efficient and environmentally friendly nitrate removal technologies. This paper presents the development and electrochemical evaluation of electrodes for nitrate-associated electrocatalytic activity using sustainable materials. Algal biomass and mineral hematite, which are abundant and low-cost resources, were employed alongside hydrothermal treatment and pyrolysis, resulting in the formation of an iron-enriched hybrid aerogel with distinct structural configurations. The physicochemical properties of the prepared materials were investigated by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and electrical conductivity measurements. Their electrochemical performance was evaluated by cyclic voltammetry in sodium sulfate electrolyte containing different nitrate concentrations (0–25 mM NO3−). Electrochemical measurements demonstrated that the combination of biochar with hematene nanosheets is a promising approach for developing fully sustainable electrodes with the potential for electrochemical nitrate treatment in polluted water. Linear sweep voltammetry and scan-rate-dependent cyclic voltammetry measurements further revealed significant differences in background current and hydrogen-evolution behavior among the electrodes. These findings demonstrate that iron-doped algal biochar aerogels are promising sustainable electrodes for electrochemical nitrate treatment and support the development of low-cost, environmentally friendly water denitrification technologies.
W7222922119.title: Development and Electrochemical Evaluation of Sustainable Algal Biochar/Hematene Aerogel Electrodes for Nitrate Conversion in Water

W7222924175.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains the world's leading infectious cause of death, with an estimated 10.8 million people falling ill and about 1.25 million dying in 2023. Isoniazid has anchored first-line therapy for seventy years, yet it is given orally for months, distributes throughout the body, and reaches the infected lung only after a long detour through the gut and liver. Objective: This review examines whether biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles delivered directly to the lung can improve the therapeutic index of isoniazid, and sets out what the formulation, aerosol and preclinical evidence actually supports. Methods: Published work on pulmonary barriers, isoniazid pharmacology, polymer selection, nanoparticle fabrication, aerosol engineering, controlled release, characterization and preclinical testing was surveyed from PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus and Google Scholar, then synthesized into comparative tables. Key Findings: PLGA, PLA, chitosan, alginate, gelatin and albumin have all been used to encapsulate isoniazid, though its high water solubility keeps encapsulation efficiency low in hydrophobic polyesters and pushes formulators toward polyelectrolyte systems or modified emulsion methods. Nanoparticles alone aerosolize poorly; nanoparticle-in-microparticle powders solve the aerodynamic problem while preserving nanoscale behaviour after deposition. Animal studies report prolonged lung and plasma drug levels and reduced dosing frequency, but most used drug combinations rather than isoniazid alone, and none has reached clinical trial. Conclusion: Inhaled polymeric isoniazid nanoparticles are pharmaceutically feasible and preclinically promising. Translation now depends on raising drug loading, controlling burst release, proving aerosol and storage stability, and generating long-term pulmonary safety data. Keywords: Isoniazid; Tuberculosis; Polymeric nanoparticles; Pulmonary drug delivery; PLGA; Chitosan; Dry powder inhaler; Alveolar macrophages; Controlled release
W7222924175.journal: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
W7222924175.title: Polymeric Nanoparticle-Based Pulmonary Delivery of Isoniazid: Advances in Formulation Design, Controlled Release, and Tuberculosis Therapy

W7222927468.abstract: Postbiotics and paraprobiotics are emerging microbial-derived bioactive agents for sustainable food packaging, offering alternatives to plant extracts and essential oils, which face limitations from resource-intensive extraction, variability, and sensory drawbacks. Postbiotics comprise non-viable microbial preparations and functional metabolites, including organic acids, bacteriocins, exopolysaccharides, enzymes, and peptides. In contrast, paraprobiotics are inactivated cells that retain structural and biological functionality without requiring viability. This review examines their biological activity, incorporation methods, and food applications in active and biodegradable packaging. Both agents exhibit antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-biofilm effects against pathogens such as Listeria monocytogenes, Escherichia coli, Salmonella, and Staphylococcus aureus, primarily via membrane disruption, intracellular acidification, competitive exclusion, and radical scavenging. However, their antimicrobial efficacy is highly variable and strongly context-dependent, being governed by the microbial strain inactivation method. These processing variables and matrix interactions must be systematically optimized when integrating these non-viable bioactives into functional packaging systems. Incorporation into biopolymeric matrices such as chitosan (CH), alginate, starch, bacterial nanocellulose (BNC), gelatin, and polylactic acid via solvent casting, dip coating, electrospinning, and encapsulation enhances antimicrobial performance, barrier properties, and oxidative stability. However, mechanical effects depend on the microbial source, inactivation method, and formulation. Real-food trials in meat, seafood, dairy, and produce demonstrate reduced pathogen loads, delayed lipid oxidation, and shelf-life extensions from several days to over two weeks. Key challenges include food-matrix interference, inconsistent terminology and preparation protocols, unclear dose–response and migration behavior, sensory changes, regulatory uncertainty, and scale-up feasibility. Interestingly, postbiotics and paraprobiotics represent a clean-label, sustainable platform for multifunctional packaging. Progress requires standardized production, strain-specific optimization, controlled-release design, migration and safety testing, empirical life-cycle assessments, and regulatory harmonization to enable safer, more sustainable packaging systems that valorize fermentation byproducts and support circular food-system innovation.
oa_topics: Postharvest Quality and Shelf Life Management
W7222927468.title: Postbiotics and Paraprobiotics as Clean-Label Bioactive Agents for Sustainable Food Packaging: A Review

W7222933525.abstract: Nanoparticles improve protective characteristics of biodegradable packaging. The aim of this study was to investigate physicomechanical characteristics of polylactic acid film containing 1, 2 and 3% silver nanoparticles synthesized using photo-assisted and ultrasound-assisted methods and aqueous extract of nettle ( Urtica dioica ). Formation of silver nanoparticles was verified using UV-vis spectroscopy. Photochemical and sonochemical synthesized silver nanoparticles were monodisperse with particle sizes of 91.28 and 68.06 nm and polydispersity indices of 0.382 and 0.371, respectively. Solubility and water absorption decreased with silver nanoparticles, especially ultrasound-assisted synthesized ones, into polylactic acid films ( p < 0.05). Nanocomposites containing 2 and 3% of ultrasound-assisted synthesized silver nanoparticles showed the highest tensile strength and elongation at break. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy verified the role of nettle extract as a decreasing, stabilizing and capping agent of silver nanoparticles. In fingerprint region of the spectra, presence of Ag-O bonding and synthesis of silver nanoparticles were verified. Silver nanoparticles improved the thermal stability of polylactic acid nanocomposite films. Therefore, use of silver nanoparticles is recommended to improve physicomechanical and thermal characteristics of polylactic acid films.
W7222933525.title: PLA nanocomposites reinforced with green synthesized AgNPs: its physico-mechanical investigation

W7222936622.title: Development and Characterization of 3D Printed PLA Composites Using Palm Oil Fuel Ash and Garlic Skin Fibers

W7222937275.title: Effect of biochar, yeast, silica and mineral fertilisers on cacao productivity and profitability in Piura, Peru

W7222938229.abstract: The long-term effects of straw and biochar amendments on soil aggregation, C:N:P stoichiometry of soil aggregates, and rice phosphorus (P) uptake in double-rice systems remain unclear. We conducted a seven-year double-rice field experiment comparing mineral fertilization only (NPK), low and high rice straw incorporation (LS and HS; 3 and 6 t ha−1 per season, respectively), and two wheat straw-derived biochar applications (LB and HB; 24 and 48 t ha−1, respectively). Biochar was applied once at the beginning of the experiment, whereas straw was incorporated after each rice season. HS increased mean weight diameter (MWD), whereas both HS and HB increased the proportion of >2 mm aggregates, with the increase under HB not accompanied by higher MWD. Biochar, particularly HB, increased C:P and C:N ratios, whereas N:P ratios differed among aggregate size fractions depending on the amendments. LS and HS increased late-rice straw P uptake relative to NPK, whereas HB decreased it. The N:P ratio in the 1–2 mm aggregate fraction was positively associated with straw, grain P concentrations, and straw P uptake, whereas the N:P ratio in the 0.053–<0.25 mm fraction was negatively associated with straw P uptake and MWD. Forward selection in Redundancy analysis (RDA) identified degree of P saturation (DPS) and average aggregate N:P ratio as significant explanatory variables for rice P concentrations and uptake. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of aggregate-size-specific N:P ratios for understanding rice P uptake responses to straw and biochar amendments.
W7222938229.title: Contrasting Effects of Straw and Straw-Derived Biochar Amendments on Soil Aggregates and Phosphorus Uptake in a Rice–Rice Cropping System

W7222941242.abstract: The purpose of the work was to identify innovative principles in packaging design that integrate functionality, aesthetics and environmental responsibility, contributing to the spread of a culture of sustainable consumption. The work used a systematic approach to the design of eco-friendly packaging, which is based on the integration of analytical-comparative, functional and morphological analysis methods and covers interdisciplinary research in the fields of design, ecology, materials science, marketing, consumer psychology, etc. A systematic analysis of eco-packaging has led to the development of three principles for its design: the use of biodegradable materials, multifunctionality, and the visualisation of natural aesthetics. It has been proven that the key area of innovation is the creation of packaging from biodegradable materials (paper, fabric, wood, plant raw materials, bioplastics, combined raw materials) that are capable of decomposing naturally without leaving environmentally harmful waste. The essence of the principle of multifunctionality has been substantiated, demonstrating the possibilities of eco-packaging design to form new ways of interacting with people and products (edible packaging, transformer packaging, organiser packaging, scented packaging). It has been found that the principle of visualising natural aesthetics emphasises the ecological orientation of the product and shapes the eco-conscious behaviour of the consumer through design. The principles considered ensure systematic design aimed at sustainable development of the natural environment, minimisation of negative impact on the environment, and improvement of aesthetic appeal. The results of the study outline the prospects for the implementation of innovative strategies in the practice of enterprises that seek to combine economic efficiency with care for the environment. The practical results of the research open up opportunities for creating conceptual models of eco-packaging that demonstrate a synthesis of functionality, aesthetics and environmental responsibility. This can be used in the design, educational and manufacturing activities of designers
W7222941242.title: Innovative principles of designing eco-friendly packaging

W7222945685.title: Production of tailored bio-oils and biochars via catalytic co-pyrolysis of barley spent grains–spent coffee grounds waste cooking for prospective application in bio-asphalt formulations

W7222948691.abstract: Diatomite is useful in soil remediation and water purification. However, its impacts on methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions in paddy soils and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. A pot experiment was set up with four treatments, including a non-amended control (CK), sole biochar (B), sole diatomite (D), and combined biochar–diatomite (BD) amendments, to compare their effects on CH4 and N2O emissions from paddy soil. Compared to CK, D and BD treatments reduced global warming potential (GWP) by 32.40% and 34.41%, respectively, significantly outperforming B treatment. All amendments reduced cumulative N2O emissions by 50.0−62.3%, with no significant variations observed among the amended treatments. CH4 was the primary contributor to GWP, and its emissions were most effectively reduced by diatomite. A random forest analysis found that the DOC/NO3−-N ratio had a high relative influence on CH4 emissions. B, D, and BD treatments significantly increased pmoA gene abundances by increasing redox potential and lowering the DOC/NO3−-N ratio. B treatment significantly reduced mcrA gene abundances, whereas D treatment exhibited no significant effect. All amended treatments altered the methanogenic community; only D and BD affected the methanotrophic community. Overall, diatomite outcompetes biochar for reducing the GWP of rice cultivation because it more potently suppresses CH4 emissions by improving soil aeration, favorably shifting microbial community structure and altering resource stoichiometry.
W7222948691.title: Diatomite Outcompetes Biochar for Reducing Methane Emissions in Rice Paddy Soil Through Shifts in Microbial Communities and Resource Stoichiometry

W7222949055.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) havae strong potential to replace fossil-based plastics in applications where sustainability and end-of-life management are critical, such as biomedical applications. Haloferax mediterranei is a robust halophilic archaeon able to produce PHBV under high salinity conditions, which reduces contamination risks and simplifies process operation.
W7222949055.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
W7222949055.title: Fermentation strategies for enhanced PHBV production by Haloferax mediterranei using sugar-rich waste streams

W7222949971.title: Environmental effects of biodegradable microplastics in cadmium-contaminated soil and their regulation on cadmium bioavailability

W7222950269.abstract: Banana peels account for 30 to 40 percent of the fresh weight of the banana fruit and are generated in quantities large enough to constitute a serious solid waste management problem in producing regions. At the same time, the peels are rich in potassium and other mineral and organic constituents that make them a promising raw material for organic fertilizer. This review synthesizes the peer-reviewed literature on the use of banana peel as an organic fertilizer, covering the composition of the peel, the principal preparation methods (composting, dried and powdered peel, liquid organic fertilizer, biochar, nano-fertilizer, and blended formulations), the documented effects on soil physical and chemical properties, and the reported responses of horticultural and field crops. Across the studies reviewed, banana peel-based fertilizers generally improved soil organic carbon, porosity, and nutrient availability, and supported plant growth and yield at levels comparable to inorganic fertilizer in several trials, although nutrient concentration in the finished product varies widely and some treatments produced no significant advantage over mineral fertilizer. The review concludes that banana peel fertilizer is a viable component of sustainable nutrient management, and identifies standardization of production protocols, field scale validation beyond the seedling stage, and economic evaluation as priority areas for future research.
W7222950269.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
W7222950269.title: From Peel to Product: A Review of Banana Peel Waste Valorization as Organic Fertilizer for Sustainable Crop Production and Soil Health

W7222953519.abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Herpes zoster (HZ) results from reactivation of latent varicella-zoster virus and disproportionately affects older adults. Antiviral therapy and systemic analgesia are well established, but local wound care of the eroded skin remains largely empirical: no dressing has been validated in controlled trials for this indication, and denuded HZ lesions are frequently mismanaged with dry gauze that adheres to the wound bed and aggravates pain. Case Presentation: An 85-year-old man with no known chronic disease presented with a one-week history of thoracic HZ unresponsive to outpatient antiviral therapy, requiring admission for uncontrolled pain (9/10 on the Numeric Rating Scale, NRS), vomiting, asthenia, and hyporexia. Examination revealed confluent, superficial-partial-thickness erosions across the T6–T8 dermatomes (12.5 × 24 cm). After a negative wound culture, a single polylactic-acid-based membrane (Suprathel®250) was applied over the entire denuded area. Pain decreased from 9/10 to 2/10 on the NRS within seven days and complete re-epithelialization was observed by day 12, under concurrent antiviral and systemic analgesic therapy and the patient resumed independent daily activities by the third week without scarring. Conclusions: In this single uncontrolled case, pain reduction and wound closure followed one application of a polylactic acid membrane to an extensive HZ lesion. Because antiviral and analgesic therapy were given concurrently and HZ improves spontaneously over time, no causal or comparative inference is possible; the observation is hypothesis-generating and supports further controlled investigation. Suprathel® is CE-marked and FDA-cleared for burn and wound care, so its use for HZ erosions extends an established burn indication.
W7222953519.journal: Reports — Medical Cases Images and Videos
W7222953519.title: Use of a Polylactic Acid Membrane for Wound Care After Severe Herpes Zoster (Shingles): A Case Report

W7222953696.abstract: Present research was conducted to investigate the interactions between deficit irrigation and biochar application in pepper (Capsicum annuum L. cv. Demre Sivrisi) grown under greenhouse conditions in a sandy-loam soil with low water-holding capacity. The experiment was arranged in a 4×4 factorial design with three replications, comprising all combinations of four irrigation levels (100%, 75%, 50% and 25% of field capacity) and four biochar doses (0, 50, 150 and 250 g/5 kg). The amount of irrigation water was determined using a gravimetric method. Plant height, fresh biomass, yield and crop water consumption (ET) were measured, and water use efficiency (WUE), biomass water use efficiency (BWUE), harvest index (HI) and yield response factor (Ky) were calculated. Water deficit markedly reduced all growth and yield parameters; mean yield decreased from 1058 g per pot under full irrigation to 108 g per pot under the most severe deficit. Biochar application increased growth and yield at all irrigation levels, providing about a 35% yield increase at the highest dose relative to the control. Biochar raised the field capacity of the sandy-loam soil by 30% at the highest dose. WUE reached its maximum not under full irrigation but at the 75% irrigation level (15.9 g/L), with the highest WUE (17.0 g/L) obtained at the 75% irrigation–250 g biochar combination. Increasing biochar dose lowered the yield response factor (Ky), reducing the crop's sensitivity to water deficit. Present findings indicated that, in water-scarce regions, combining 75% irrigation with a high biochar dose was an effective strategy to maximize yield per unit water.
W7222953696.journal: Türk Tarım ve Doğa Bilimleri Dergisi
W7222953696.title: Optimizing Yield and Water Use Efficiency of Pepper Under Deficit Irrigation Using Biochar

W7222954418.abstract: Fused deposition modelling (FDM) is a widely adopted additive manufacturing technique to fabricate three-dimensional components from thermoplastic feedstock. The investigation is carried out for the effect of layer thickness, nozzle temperature, infill density, and sisal fibre weight fraction on the tensile and flexural properties of sisal fibre-reinforced polylactic acid (PLA) composites fabricated through FDM. A Box-Behnken Design (BBD) within the Response Surface Methodology (RSM) framework was employed to investigate and optimize these four experimental factors. The parameter ranges considered were 0.1–0.3 mm for layer thickness, 190–210°C for nozzle temperature, 60–100% for infill density, and 3–9 wt% for sisal fibre content. ANOVA indicated that fibre weight fraction was the most influential factor for tensile strength, while infill density was the dominant factor affecting flexural strength. The regression models established R 2 values of 98.81% and 92.04% for tensile and flexural strength, respectively. Among the experimental design points, 6 wt% sisal fibre produced the highest tensile strength of 46.50 MPa and flexural strength of 78.38 MPa. The RSM-based multi-response optimization identified an optimum combination of 0.2357 mm layer thickness, 209.61°C nozzle temperature, 78.89% infill density, and 6.41 wt% fibre content, with predicted tensile and flexural strengths of 43.50 MPa and 53.55 MPa, respectively. Confirmatory experiments at the optimized condition yielded tensile and flexural strengths of 40.68 MPa and 50.09 MPa, respectively. The results demonstrate the applicability of RSM for identifying a balanced combination of material composition and FDM processing parameters for sisal fibre-reinforced PLA composites.
W7222954418.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part L Journal of Materials Design and Applications
W7222954418.title: Mechanical property optimization of sisal fiber-reinforced PLA composites fabricated by fused deposition modelling using response surface methodology

W7222955386.title: Treatment efficiency of magnesium-modified magnetic sludge-based biochar in pharmaceutical wastewater: Adsorption, biodegradation, and enhancement mechanisms

W7222955620.abstract: Marine algae sustain primary productivity, nutrient cycling, and coastal carbon regulation, yet warming, salinity fluctuations, acidification, and nutrient/metal loading increasingly challenge their physiology, and evidence linking adaptation to biotechnological value remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes physiological, biochemical, and transcriptomic studies (2016–2026) on marine micro- and macroalgae exposed to thermal, saline, light/oxidative, nutrient, heavy-metal, and acidification stress; a few non-marine extremophile taxa are included and flagged as mechanistic comparators. Across taxa, algae rely on recurrent strategies—osmolyte accumulation, antioxidant/photoprotective pigments, fatty-acid desaturation, metal chelation, and phytohormone-mediated (ABA, SA, MeJA) signalling coupled to ribosome-biogenesis upregulation—that appear to restore redox and osmotic homeostasis. These phenotypes underpin biofuel, bioremediation, blue-carbon, and bioplastic applications, ranked on a Technology Readiness Level scale from wastewater bioremediation and aquaculture co-culture (TRL 6–7) to biodiesel and blue-carbon crediting (TRL 3) and photoprotection-trait transfer (TRL 2). We propose a reaction-level conceptual framework in which ribosome-biogenesis control and ABA/SA/MeJA signalling act as a testable stress-integration hub, presented explicitly as a hypothesis rather than an established mechanism. Stress tolerance and circular-economy value may be mechanistically linked, but most evidence derives from short-term, single-species laboratory exposures, remains taxonomically narrow, and macroalga-specific comparative laboratory data are scarce.
W7222955620.journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
W7222955620.title: Physiological and Biochemical Mechanisms of Marine Algae in Response to Environmental Stress: Adaptive Strategies and Applications in Circular Bioeconomy—A Narrative Review and Conceptual Synthesis

W7222959415.abstract: The development of cost-effective and durable anode materials derived from renewable biomass is essential for practical lithium- and sodium-ion batteries (LIBs/SIBs). However, conventional strategies for integrating high-capacity metal oxides with biomass carbon often suffer from weak oxide–carbon adhesion, nanoparticle aggregation, and large volume changes during cycling. To overcome these limitations, we present an interfacial engineering approach in which carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) serves as a molecular bridge to anchor Fe3O4 nanoparticles in situ onto ginkgo branch-derived biochar (GBC). The abundant hydroxyl and carboxyl groups of CMC simultaneously guide uniform Fe3O4 nucleation and create a molecular bridge that mediates interfacial chemical interactions that facilitate charge transfer while accommodating volume strain. Structural and compositional analyses confirm the formation of CMC/Fe3O4/GBC with well-dispersed nanocrystals, a hierarchically porous architecture, and magnetic responsiveness. As an anode, CMC/Fe3O4/GBC delivers 256 mAh/g at 2000 mA/g in SIBs, substantially higher than that of bare GBC and unmodified Fe3O4/GBC. Comparable durability is observed in LIBs, where the composite retains 297 mAh/g after 2000 cycles at the same rate. Kinetic studies using cyclic voltammetry, galvanostatic intermittent titration technique, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveal that CMC bridging enhances pseudocapacitive contribution and accelerates ion diffusion. Post-cycling X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and transmission electron microscopy further confirm the preserved electrode integrity. These results establish a scalable interfacial modification strategy for biomass-derived magnetic composites toward durable alkali-ion storage.
W7222959415.title: Interfacial Engineering of Fe3O4/Biochar via CMC Bridging for Durable Lithium/Sodium-Ion Storage

W7222960484.abstract: Long-term monoculture degrades soil ecological conditions and is associated with severe wilt disease in Chrysanthemum morifolium. The effects of combining rapeseed biofumigation and biochar to alleviate these continuous cropping obstacles remain poorly understood. A field experiment compared a control (CK), rapeseed biofumigation alone (R), and biofumigation combined with corn-straw biochar (RB) in soil under eight years of continuous chrysanthemum cultivation. Soil properties, enzyme activities, wilt disease severity, chrysanthemum yield, and rhizosphere microbial communities were assessed. Compared with CK, RB significantly increased available phosphorus (+40.7%), available potassium (+16.4%), total nitrogen (+4.9%), cation exchange capacity (+8.6%), selected enzyme activities, plant height, and flower yield (p < 0.05). The disease index decreased from 8.67 in CK to 2.67 under R and 2.33 under RB, with both reductions significant but no significant difference between R and RB. Both treatments altered microbial community composition, reduced bacterial richness, and enriched MND1; RB additionally reduced bacterial diversity, enriched Acidobacteriota, and decreased the abundances of Firmicutes and Bacteroidota relative to CK. Exploratory Mantel tests indicated that available phosphorus and cation exchange capacity were associated with variation in rhizosphere microbial community structure. Overall, RB improved selected soil fertility parameters and flower yield, accompanied by microbial community changes and lower wilt severity. Broader application requires multi-site and multi-season validation.
W7222960484.title: Rapeseed Biofumigation Combined with Biochar Mitigates Continuous-Cropping Obstacles in Chrysanthemum via Soil Improvement, Rhizosphere Microbial-Community Modification, and Wilt Disease Reduction

W7222961147.abstract: N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) is a widely used industrial solvent that can enter industrial wastewater, creating a need for efficient and low-cost treatment methods. In this study, biochar prepared from waste Procambarus clarkii shells was used as an auxiliary material to evaluate its promotion of NMP biodegradation by Paracoccus sp. strain NH1 under anoxic conditions. Among the materials tested, biochar prepared at 300 °C showed the highest mean NMP degradation efficiency after 24 h, increasing from 85.9% in the no-material control to 98.0% (p < 0.05). Mean ETSA was also significantly higher in the SSB 300 group than in the no-material control (p < 0.05). Abiotic controls with 500 mg/L NMP showed that NMP loss within 24 h was below 5% in the presence of raw crayfish shell material, SSB 300-SSB 600, or activated carbon, indicating that adsorption or other abiotic losses were insufficient to explain the observed enhancement. Surface characterization showed that low-temperature biochar retained more nitrogen-containing and oxygen-containing surface chemical structures than high-temperature biochar; at the same time, SSB 300 was also associated with higher N-methylhydantoin amidohydrolase (NMA) activity, higher extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) polysaccharide production, and more favorable cell attachment. Because the mineral salts medium contained nitrate, this study interprets ETSA as an indicator of enhanced microbial respiratory/redox activity rather than evidence of direct electron transfer through biochar to NMP. Therefore, the results support a multifactorial enhancement mechanism, including metabolic stimulation, surface-associated colonization, and potentially redox-active biochar surface chemistry. These findings provide a route with practical application potential for integrating crayfish shell waste valorization with NMP biological removal. The novelty of this work lies in linking the properties of shell waste-derived biochar to the biological removal of NMP, while distinguishing abiotic NMP loss from microbially mediated enhancement.
W7222961147.title: Crayfish Shell-Derived Biochar Enhances Paracoccus-Mediated NMP Biodegradation Under Anoxic Conditions: A Waste-to-Wealth Strategy

W7222961533.abstract: Phosphate enrichment of surface waters is a major cause of eutrophication, creating demand for low-cost materials that support phosphorus removal and recovery. In this study, Conocarpus waste biochar (CBC) was modified with iron (Fe-CBC), magnesium (Mg-CBC), and both metals (FeMg-CBC) to improve phosphate adsorption. FTIR, XRD, SEM, and elemental analyses confirmed clear changes in surface chemistry and mineral composition after modification. FeMg-CBC showed the strongest overall performance, with higher surface area, faster uptake, and greater adsorption capacity than the mono-metallic materials. Phosphate removal was strongly influenced by pH, adsorbent dosage, and contact time, with optimum performance near pH 6. Adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model (R2 = 0.997), while equilibrium data were best described by the Langmuir–Freundlich model. FeMg-CBC achieved Langmuir and Sips capacities of 86.2 and 106.5 mg g−1, respectively. Its enhanced performance was attributed to combined electrostatic attraction, ligand exchange, Mg-phosphate precipitation, and possible interlayer anion exchange within the Fe-Mg layered phase. These findings highlight its potential for wastewater treatment and nutrient recycling.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7222961533.title: Iron–Magnesium Bimetallic Biochar Composites Derived from Conocarpus Waste for Enhanced Phosphate Removal: Insights into the Underlying Adsorption Mechanisms in Aqueous Solution

W7222963605.abstract: Adsorption remains one of the most practical and widely adopted strategies for removing pollutants from wastewater, yet conventional powder and granular adsorbents suffer from persistent limitations: poor recyclability, difficult solid–liquid separation, and limited control over selectivity in complex, multi-contaminant streams. Three-dimensional (3D) printing has emerged as a compelling alternative, offering precise control over geometry, porosity, and macrostructure that conventional shaping methods simply cannot achieve. However, the base polymers and inks most commonly used in additive manufacturing, such as PLA, ABS, PETG, and alginate, are chemically inert and lack inherent affinity for specific pollutants. Achieving meaningful adsorption capacity therefore depends critically on how and when the active functional component is introduced into the printed structure. This review examines the full spectrum of modification strategies applied to 3D-printed adsorbents for wastewater treatment, organized by the timing of modification relative to printing. Pre-printing approaches, including composite filament fabrication, functional ink formulation, and resin doping with active materials such as MOFs, biochar, zeolites, and metal oxides, are critically evaluated alongside post-printing strategies, including surface coating, nanoparticle decoration, chemical grafting, plasma treatment, and in situ growth of porous frameworks. For each approach, the implications for pollutant selectivity are assessed across the main contaminant classes: heavy metals, synthetic dyes, and organic micropollutants such as pharmaceuticals and Bisphenol A, which are considered according to their charge, hydrophobicity, and adsorption mechanism. Finally, key structure–modification relationships are identified, gaps in regeneration, competitive-adsorption, and real-wastewater testing are highlighted, and directions for rational, pollutant-targeted adsorbent design using additive manufacturing are outlined.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7222963605.title: Modifications of 3D-Printed Adsorbent Materials for Pollutant Removal from Wastewaters

W7222967078.abstract: The use of polylactic acid (PLA) and polycaprolactone (PCL) as film-forming components in composites with thermoplastic starch (TPS) was investigated. An optimal composition of the functional additive in TPS was developed using chitosan and lactic acid (chitosan lactate, LC). The physical and mechanical properties of the PLA/TPS and PCL/TPS composites were determined. The structure of the composites and its changes following thermomechanical treatment were studied using FT-IR spectroscopy. Mass spectrometric analysis was performed, and the characteristic mass spectra of ion fragments resulting from the thermal decomposition of PLA, LC, and PLA/TPS were analyzed; their intensities at the peak region were measured. Structural changes in the compositions were studied using DSC and TGA methods, and the mass loss and rate of mass loss during thermal decomposition were quantitatively determined.
W7222967078.title: Analysis of structural transformations in biodegradable polymer composites as a function of film-forming components and functional additives

W7222968137.abstract: Subarachnoid hemorrhage after cerebral aneurysm rupture has a 50% first-month fatality rate. Endovascular flow diversion is the primary treatment modality. However, no prior study has compared stents, coils, and the Woven Endo-Bridge hemodynamically integrating hemodynamic results with structural device behavior in one framework. An aneurysm model was reconstructed from computed tomography imaging of a patient, and computational fluid dynamics evaluated multiple hemodynamic metrics across three flow-diversion strategies. Finite element analysis assessed stent geometries with 50%, 55%, and 60% porosity in 316L stainless steel, poly-L-lactic acid, and nitinol. Universal testing machine tests validated the models with printed polylactic acid and thermoplastic polyurethane analogues. Dimensional and elastic-tube analyses tested scale equivalence between the FEA and UTM geometries and the rigid-wall CFD assumption. Patient-specific CFD confirmed a high-risk hemodynamic profile. The stent yielded the lowest peak intra-sac velocity, greatest pressure reduction, near-zero wall shear stress, the only reduction in time-averaged wall shear stress, cycle-averaged TAWSS, and the largest peak-systolic reductions in velocity, WSS, and vorticity. OSI and RRT rose for all three treated configurations, consistent with the hemodynamic signature of flow diversion. FEA reproduced the expected stiffness hierarchy (Steel > Nitinol > PLLA), and TPU was the closest surrogate for Nitinol's elastic recovery. Scaled specimens matched native-scale stiffness within 2.3%. Predicted radial distension was orders of magnitude below native wall values, supporting rigid-wall CFD. Stent-assisted diversion demonstrated the most favorable hemodynamic profile. A 50%-porosity Nitinol stent best matched target elastic mechanics, while 316L stainless steel provided the greatest resistance to radial compression.
W7222968137.title: Hemodynamic-Structural Multi-Fidelity Assessment of Endovascular Flow Diversion Strategies for Cerebral Aneurysm Treatment: An Integrated Computational and Experimental Framework

W7222968699.abstract: The aging of marine microplastics (MPs) and their release of plastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) have raised growing concern, yet comparative assessments of conventional polyolefins versus biodegradable polyesters under synergistic UV-salinity stress remain limited. Here, we systematically compared the surface alteration and DOM release of polyethylene (PE), polypropylene (PP), and polylactic acid (PLA) across a salinity gradient (0, 15, and 30 PSU; Practical Salinity Unit) under UV-exposed and dark conditions over 60 days. UV irradiation markedly accelerated aging in all three MP types, as evidenced by progressive enrichment of oxygen-containing functional groups. For PE and PP, increased salinity further intensified photo-oxidative degradation, and released DOM exhibited optical shifts from protein-like toward humic-like fluorescence signatures characterized by elevated SUVA 254 and HIX values. In contrast, PLA degradation was consistent with ester bond hydrolysis, producing 2–6 times greater DOM yields than PE and PP, with released DOM dominated by protein-like fluorescence components. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) indicated that UV exposure exerted stronger effects than salinity on the surface oxidation of PE and PP ( β = 0.39–0.41 vs. 0.20–0.31), while salinity showed no significant effect on PLA aging. These findings reveal contrasting pathways by which conventional and biodegradable MPs contribute to marine dissolved organic carbon pools, providing a basis for assessing their differential environmental behaviors under variable salinity regimes.
W7222968699.title: Aging dynamics and subsequent dissolved organic matter evolution of microplastics regulated by UV–salinity conditions

W7222969562.abstract: Sugarcane vinasse is a high-strength industrial wastewater that presents treatment challenges due to its high organic load and instability of anaerobic digestion (AD) caused by volatile fatty acid (VFA) accumulation. This study explored biochar (BC)-assisted thermophilic AD as an engineering strategy to enhance process stability, treatment performance, and energy recovery from vinasse. Batch experiments were conducted using BC dosages of 5, 10, and 15 g L −1 , followed by consequential life cycle assessment (CLCA). The optimal BC dosage (10 g L −1 ) significantly improved AD performance, increasing biogas and methane yields by 36% (568 mL g −1 VS) and 43% (362 mL g −1 VS), respectively, while enhancing COD removal to 81% and reducing residual total VFAs from 7.1 to 4.1 g L −1 relative to the control. Kinetic analysis further showed increased methane production potential and a shorter lag phase, indicating improved digestion stability. The CLCA showed that BC-assisted AD achieved a greater net global warming (GW) benefit than conventional AD (−62.72 vs. −44.10 kg CO 2 -eq), but the benefits were impact-category dependent, with water consumption shifting from a net saving to a net burden. Sensitivity analysis further showed that the comparative results were strongly influenced by avoided electricity and fertilizer substitution and by the geographical configuration of the BC supply chain. Localizing BC production reduced transportation-related burdens but did not proportionally improve the overall GW result. These findings demonstrate that BC can enhance vinasse AD, while its life-cycle implications depend on consequential substitutions and regional supply-chain conditions.
W7222969562.title: Biochar-assisted anaerobic digestion of sugarcane vinasse for enhanced energy recovery: Experimental evaluation and environmental assessment

W7222970223.abstract: To investigate the combined effects of a reduced nitrogen application rate and biochar amendment on fruit yield and quality, photosynthetic carbon allocation, and soil carbon retention in apple orchards, a two-year field experiment was conducted using Malus domestica Borkh. cv. ‘Red Fuji’/M9T337. Six treatments were established: three nitrogen levels (conventional nitrogen [TN], 20% nitrogen reduction [TN80%], 40% nitrogen reduction [TN60%]) with and without biochar amendment (+B). The TN80%+B treatment led to the highest anthocyanin, soluble solid, and soluble sugar values and sugar/acid ratio. The yield and economic benefits of TN80%+B were not significantly different from those of TN, while its agronomic efficiency was the highest among all treatments. Moderate nitrogen reduction combined with biochar increased 13C accumulation in fruits and roots, enhanced the 13C distribution rate in fruits (41% in TN80%+B), and promoted the transfer of photosynthetic carbon from aboveground parts to roots and soil. Soil organic carbon, microbial biomass carbon, particulate organic carbon, mineral-associated organic carbon, and their corresponding 13C-labeled carbon fractions all increased following application of nitrogen reduction combined with biochar, peaking under the TN80%+B treatment. Soil CO2 emissions decreased with declining nitrogen inputs, with the lowest cumulative emissions observed under TN60%+B (1937.31 kg C ha−1). Biochar also suppressed cellobiohydrolase activity and cbh abundance while enhancing α-glucosidase, β-glucosidase, and carbon-fixation gene abundances (cbbL, accA, and aclA). Overall, TN80%+B provides the most favorable balance among outcomes, delivering concurrent benefits of improved fruit quality, stable yield, enhanced soil carbon retention, and reduced CO2 emissions.
W7222970223.title: Effects of Nitrogen Application Rate Reduction Combined with Biochar Amendment on Apple Yield and Quality, Photosynthetic Carbon Allocation, and Soil Carbon Retention

W7222970934.abstract: Melatonin (N-acetyl-5-methoxytryptamine) (MLT) is a naturally occurring hormone produced endogenously, primarily in the suprachiasmatic nucleus. MLT exhibits a plethora of uses particularly in the treatment of sleep disorders (sleep onset and maintenance). However, due to its short biological half-life, MLT cannot maintain effective plasma concentrations for a prolonged period when it is exogenously taken from immediate-release formulations. The present study aims at developing modified release systems capable of gradually releasing MLT, thereby sustaining its pharmacological effect over eight hours. To this end, modified-release tablets were prepared using new polymeric excipients based on polylactic acid (PLA). Both neat PLA and PLA copolymers with polyethylene glycols (PEGs) of varying molecular weights (PLLA-PEG-PLLA_4000, PLLA-PEG-PLLA_6000, and PLLA-PEG-PLLA_8000) were used, along with other excipients. Certain formulations delivered MLT comparatively fast and may therefore be useful for sleep onset problems, others matched the release behaviour of the marketed product Circadin®, and the rest released the hormone in a more prolonged manner.
W7222970934.title: Probing Melatonin’s Release Pattern from Oral Solid Dosage Forms Using Synthetic Biopolymers

W7222973417.abstract: Biochar materials are compelling adsorbents for pollutants in aqueous solution. Most studies focus on experimenting on purpose-made biochar types to reveal removal mechanisms and their influence on adsorption performance. This work is an effort to bridge the gap between such studies and real-world upscaling by making use of widely available commercial biochar and evaluation of removal performance for Pb2+ and Cr3+. The objective is to compare performance achieved by employed biochar samples to constrain beneficial and detrimental characteristics to the removal process. This is done using both differences among biochar samples and sorbed contaminants. Nine commercial biochar samples from Italy, France and Germany have been characterized by means of CHNOS elemental analysis, surface analysis, thermogravimetric analysis and FT-IR spectroscopy, detecting a great degree of variability in terms of physical and chemical properties. Kinetic and isotherm adsorption experiments with contaminant concentrations up to 50 mg/L yield distinct removal performances for different biochar samples and contaminants. Changes in surface functionality - before and after water treatment - have been surveyed through FT-IR spectroscopy. Removal mechanisms are comparable for Pb2+ and Cr3+ and include complexation with oxygen containing functional groups, interaction with π-carbon bonds and ion exchange. Increasingly high contaminant concentrations pointed out further controls on the adsorption process tied to biochar’s pore structure in relation to the contaminant’s nature. Adsorption-desorption isotherms yielded by surface analysis suggest a subdivision in two groups of biochar samples depending on the occurrence of a H4 hysteresis loop. Such a loop is indicative of slit-shaped porosity, while an open one suggests an ink-bottle pore shape. Provided the presence of adequate surface functionality and area, ink bottle pores can hinder removal process efficiency by restricting access to metal complexes and being blocked by multilayer adsorption phenomena. Regardless of such effects, commercial biochar samples achieve performance levels greater or equal to literature counterparts in similar conditions. Upscaling readiness of commercial biochar materials is proven through deep insight into physical-chemical interactions occurring between sorbent and contaminant. A knowledgeable application of biochar technologies for water treatment requires proper standardized characterization and policy support and can additionally foster its sustainable proposition by limiting the need for costly and impactful post-production modifications.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7222973417.title: Removal of Pb2+ and Cr3+ from Aqueous Solution Through Commercial Biochar: Insights from Characterization for Enhanced Performance

W7222975636.abstract: Abstract Temporary plugging and diverting technology is an effective method for enhancing fracture complexity during repeated fracturing operations. PLA-based temporary plugging agents have attracted extensive attention due to their high mechanical strength and environmental friendliness. However, their relatively low softening temperature and poor balance between stiffness and toughness significantly restrict their applicability in deep reservoirs. In this study, a composite biodegradable temporary plugging agent (CB-TPA) with stable interfacial adhesion morphology and excellent physical properties was prepared by a two-step reactive blending with polylactic acid (PLA), polyglycolic acid (PGA), polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT), and a reactive elastomer (ADR). Experimental results indicated that at a PLA/PGA (70:30) to PBAT mass ratio of 3:1, the tensile strength, Vicat softening temperature, and impact toughness reached 64.4 MPa, 110 °C, and 7.7 kJ/m2, respectively. The material had a lower stiffness loss due to the improved compatibility, demonstrating well-balanced heat resistance, toughness, and stiffness. The simulated plugging experiments showed that CB-TPA could effectively withstand pressures up to 20 MPa at 160 °C, which is superior to that of commercial PLA temporary plugging agents. Under aqueous conditions at 160 °C, the weight loss of CB-TPA reached 96.7% within 4 h. The successful development of this composite biodegradable temporary plugging agent provides a new sustainable solution for the exploitation of deep unconventional oil and gas resources.
W7222975636.title: Strong, Tough, and High-Temperature-Resistant Biodegradable Temporary Plugging Agents for Refracturing in Deep Reservoirs by Two-Step Reactive Extrusion

W7222976592.abstract: Abstract Co-pyrolysis of sewage sludge (SS) and sawdust (SD) with basaltic minerals may produce nutrient-enriched biochars for soil amendment and long-term carbon (C) persistence. However, the effects of mineral incorporation on C transformations and the interpretation of conventional stability indices remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we compared SS and SD copyrolyzed with zeolitic basalt (ZB) and metabasalt (MB). The resulting materials, produced at 500 °C, were characterized by proximate and elemental analyses, X-ray diffraction, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and nutrient and carbon-stability assessments. Mineral addition increased biochar yields to 70–73%, whereas SD-derived biochar exhibited the highest fixed C and thermostable fractions. Materials obtained by co-pyrolyzing SD with ZB or MB, and SS with ZB, showed high thermal resistance. Mineral-enriched biochars had higher ash contents and contained silicate-rich phases, modifying their mineralogical composition and nutrient profiles. Co-pyrolysis of SS with basaltic materials increased Ca, Mg, P, and micronutrient contents. Contrasting responses among elemental, thermochemical, and persistence-based indices showed that no single approach adequately evaluates C stability in mineral-enriched biochars. These findings support the potential use of mineral-enriched biochars as soil amendments and show that C stability requires integrated evaluation.
W7222976592.title: Mineral-Enriched Biochars from Co-Pyrolysis of Sewage Sludge, Sawdust, and Basaltic Rocks: Soil Amendment Potential and Carbon Stability

W7222977146.title: Upcycling of cardoon root biomass into polyhydroxyalkanoate nanocarriers for docetaxel delivery

W7222978400.abstract: The development of protein-based bioplastics from renewable agricultural resources provides a promising route towards alternative polymeric materials derived from non-petroleum feedstocks. This study investigated the effect of maleic acid concentration on the structural, morphological, and spectroscopic characteristics of sesame (Sesamum indicum L.) protein bioplastic films. Sesame protein isolate was prepared through alkaline extraction followed by acid precipitation and subsequently modified with 4% and 5% maleic acid to obtain 4MX and 5MX formulations, respectively. The modified protein materials were plasticised with glycerol and processed into films before characterisation by X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. XRD patterns exhibited broad diffraction features characteristic of predominantly disordered protein-based structures. The principal reflection shifted from 2θ = 16.800° for 4MX to 17.800° for 5MX, corresponding to calculated interplanar spacings of 5.2778 and 4.9835 Å, respectively. Thus, increasing maleic acid concentration produced a 1.000° shift in the principal reflection and an approximately 5.57% reduction in calculated d-spacing. SEM examination revealed concentration-dependent differences in surface organisation, including variations in surface texture, interconnected regions and voids. FTIR spectra retained characteristic protein amide absorptions, while the broad O–H/N–H stretching band shifted from 3261.46 cm−1 for 4MX to 3248.38 cm−1 for 5MX, representing a 13.08 cm−1 shift. The combined XRD, SEM and FTIR findings demonstrate that increasing maleic acid concentration from 4% to 5% alters the structural organisation, surface morphology and molecular environment of the sesame-protein matrix. However, the available data do not independently establish covalent esterification, increased crosslink density, or improved functional performance. Further mechanical, barrier, thermal and controlled chemical analyses are required to establish the structure–property relationships of the resulting films.
W7222978400.journal: International Journal of Applied and Natural Sciences
W7222978400.title: Sesame Seed Protein Bioplastic Films Modified with Maleic Acid: Structural, Morphological and Functional-Group Characterizations

W7222983953.abstract: Injectable biodegradable polymers and micronized acellular dermal matrix (mADM) have potentially complementary regenerative properties, but how their combination shapes the host response remains poorly defined. In many systems, polymers provide persistent material-associated stimulation that may sustain macrophage-driven foreign-body responses, whereas mADM provides tissue-derived extracellular matrix (ECM) cues that support cellular infiltration, vascularization, and remodeling, with persistence dependent on processing and host-mediated replacement. This narrative review evaluates whether changes in macrophage population states could help explain potential polymer–mADM synergy. Across the reviewed polymer–ECM hybrid studies, most evidence is indirect, and temporal sampling rarely resolves sequential state changes. No included study establishes temporal coupling as a causal mechanism. We therefore propose a temporal macrophage-switching model in which both components act from implantation and their relative contributions change over time; their spatiotemporal overlap may shape macrophage population trajectories and remodeling outcomes. We further define a functional macrophage polarization window using biological landmarks rather than fixed time points. The model remains a testable hypothesis whose applicability depends on material and tissue context. Validation requires polymer-only, mADM-only, and hybrid comparisons across independent mADM lots, with systematic variation in polymer persistence, mADM processing, component ratio, spatial organization, and degradation/remodeling kinetics.
W7222983953.title: Micronized Acellular Dermal Matrix and Synthetic Polymers: Temporal Macrophage Transition as a Mechanistic Framework

W7222985777.abstract: Biochar has emerged as a highly attractive, sustainable support for enzyme immobilization, with dual benefits: valorization of available lignocellulosic waste and use as a stable, porous matrix for enzyme binding. This study investigated acid-modified sour cherry stone biochar (SCBM) as support for two laccases of different origins: crude laccase (Bjerkandera adusta TMF1 (CL)) and purified commercial laccase (Trametes versicolor (TvL)). The aim was to compare immobilization efficiency, activity retention and Brilliant Green (BG) decolorization in batch and air-lift reactors (ALRs). Immobilization of crude (SCBM-CL) and commercial (SCBM-TvL) laccase was successfully achieved and confirmed by SEM-EDX and FTIR-ATR analyses. Under optimized batch conditions, SCBM-TvL achieved approximately 92% of BG removal within 4 h and maintained high catalytic activity over nine consecutive cycles, whereas SCBM-CL reached almost 66% removal, with a progressive loss of activity upon reuse. In the ALR, using a 25-fold lower biochar-to-solution ratio, SCBM-TvL achieved almost complete BG decolorization within 4 h, while SCBM-CL achieved 57% within the same time. After treatment, BG solution exhibited a phytostimulatory effect, no antimicrobial activity, and 87% COD reduction, indicating reduced toxicity and organic load after enzyme treatment. Furthermore, the BG decolorization achieved by SCBM-TvL in ALRs highlights the economic advantage of this system and supports its potential for further scale-up.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7222985777.title: A Comparative Evaluation of Dye Removal in Batch and Air-Lift Systems by Commercial and Crude Laccase Immobilized on Biochar

W7222987538.abstract: Biochar is widely applied in the amelioration of saline soils; however, few studies have focused on the mechanical properties of biochar-amended saline soils. To evaluate the mechanical properties of biochar-amended saline soil in seasonally frozen regions, specimens with different salt and biochar contents were first subjected to unconfined compressive strength (UCS) tests, and the optimum biochar content was determined. Freeze–thaw cycling, UCS, NMR and SEM tests were then performed at the optimum biochar content to examine the strength attenuation, pore-structure evolution and microstructural damage mechanism of the biochar-amended saline soil. The results indicate that biochar effectiveness depends on both salt and biochar contents. Considering strength enhancement, applicability across different salt contents and material utilization efficiency, 5% biochar was identified as the optimum biochar content in this study. At this content, the peak strength declined continuously as freeze–thaw cycles increased, and the strength loss was generally greater at moderate-to-high salt contents. The maximum peak strength loss ratio reached 90.19% after 12 freeze–thaw cycles. The NMR and SEM results suggest that freeze–thaw cycling promoted the transformation of small pores into medium and large pores, together with crack propagation, aggregate loosening and interparticle separation. Therefore, the strength degradation of saline soil amended with 5% biochar under freeze–thaw cycles was closely associated with pore-structure coarsening and deterioration of microstructural integrity. These findings provide an experimental basis for the low-carbon stabilization of saline soil, freeze–thaw durability evaluation and the design of engineering fill materials in seasonally frozen regions.
W7222987538.title: Mechanical response of biochar-amended saline soil under freeze-thaw conditions

oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7222987592.title: Sulphate removal from synthetic acid mine drainage by iron-impregnated coconut shell biochar: role of iron retention and surface accessibility

W7222988324.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials in landscape architecture has highlighted the potential of polylactic acid/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate (PLA/PBAT)-based wood-plastic composites. However, poor interfacial compatibility between the hydrophilic plant fibers and the hydrophobic polyester matrices, coupled with susceptibility to hydrolytic degradation, limits their outdoor applications. This study presents a synergistic modification strategy for bamboo powder using a silane coupling agent (KH550) and nano-silica (Nano-SiO2), integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accelerated aging experiments to elucidate the enhancement mechanism of "chemical bridging–physical filling. " MD simulations revealed that the modification forms a dense "core-shell" barrier via covalent anchoring and a robust hydrogen-bond network, reducing the interfacial free volume to 14.1 % and lowering the water molecule self-diffusion coefficient from 4.58 × 10–7 to 0.42 × 10–7 cm2 s–1. This microscopic moisture barrier underpins the macroscopic aging resistance. Accelerated UV-condensation aging tests (1000 h) confirmed that the modified composites preserved the polyester backbone, with a weight-average molecular weight retention of 88.4 %, a tensile strength of 84.3 %, and an impact strength of 81.2 %. The surface color change was limited to E = 4.2, markedly outperforming unmodified composites. Additionally, the initial properties were improved: water absorption decreased from 4.25 % to 1.85 %, tensile strength reached 46.5 MPa, and impact strength reached 6.2 kJ m–2, achieving concurrent rigidity and toughness enhancement. These results demonstrate that nano-synergistic modification effectively mitigates weathering-induced degradation in PLA/PBAT composites, offering a practical pathway for their sustainable application in outdoor landscape environments.
W7222988324.title: Modificiran z rastlinskimi vlakni ojačani popolnoma biorazgradljivi lesno-plastični kompozit za trajnostno krajinsko arhitekturo: združljivost vmesnika in mehanizem staranja

W7222993799.title: “Toxic stress” and “substrate perturbation”: The dual fate and sustainable management of plastics in anaerobic digestion systems

W7222994370.abstract: Abstract Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (P3HB) stands out as a microbial biopolymer with biodegradable properties, offering a sustainable alternative to petroleum-based plastic. However, its application is hindered by brittleness and processing challenges, partially attributed to its fully (R)-isotactic stereocenter configuration. The enzymes responsible for P3HB production, polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) synthases, are traditionally considered to be strictly stereospecific, causing P3HB isotacticity. In this study, we developed an in vitro assay to analyze the stereospecificity of this enzyme class. Our investigation of PHA synthases reveals that the enzymes from Allochromatium vinosum and Chromobacterium sp. USM2, despite belonging to different PHA synthase classes and having low sequence identity, share the trait of not strictly adhering to stereospecificity. Notably, they demonstrate the capability of producing stereoirregular P3HB in vitro. Furthermore, we identified two key limitations influencing the production of stereoirregular P3HB in vitro. First, PHA synthases appear to require a high (S)- over (R)-substrate ratio. Second, under (R)-limiting conditions, the resulting stereoirregular P3HB exhibits a lower molar mass compared to its isotactic counterpart. Our findings challenge the assumption of universally strict stereospecificity among the PHA synthases tested and identify factors governing stereoirregular P3HB formation under assay conditions. The developed assay may support future enzyme engineering efforts aimed at tuning P3HB stereochemistry and ultimately polymer properties.
W7222994370.title: Selected PHA Synthases Exhibit Nonstrict Stereospecificity and Produce Stereoirregular Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) In Vitro

W7222995807.abstract: Biochar composites are promising for electromagnetic wave absorption due to their renewability and low cost, but performance optimization remains a challenge. Here, hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 composite nanoparticles, in which the CoFe and CoFe2O4 phases coexist, are grown in situ on lotus-leaf-derived porous carbon via a Kirkendall-type process during heat treatment. The optimized composite (pyrolyzed at 800 °C) exhibits a saturation magnetization of 69.20 emu/g and a coercivity of 482 Oe; a calculated minimum reflection loss (RLmin) of −71.4 dB is obtained at a matching thickness of 2.70 mm, with an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 5.68 GHz at 1.70 mm, covering most of the Ku band. The enhanced microwave absorption performance is attributed to the synergy of dielectric and magnetic losses, polarization relaxations, and improved impedance matching, together with multiple scattering within the hollow structure. In addition, the exchange coupling between the FeCo and CoFe2O4 may contribute to magnetic dissipation, while hollow cavities may promote internal reflections for further energy attenuation. This work provides a biomass-derived route to high-performance biochar-based absorbers competitive with synthetic counterparts.
W7222995807.title: Boosting Microwave Absorption via Hollow CoFe/CoFe2O4 Nanoparticles Anchored on Lotus-Leaf-Derived Biochar

W7222996889.abstract: The depletion of fossil resources and increasing plastic-derived pollution have become major environmental concerns. In this context, biodegradable biopolymers such as polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) have attracted considerable scientific interest. Microalgae and cyanobacteria represent promising photosynthetic microorganisms for sustainable bioplastic production. In this study, ten microalgal species (Parachlorella kessleri, Chlorella vulgaris, Chlorella minutissima, Tetraselmis tetrathele, Chromochloris zofigiensis, Acutodesmus obliquus, Euglena gracilis, Chlorococcum oleofaciens, Botryococcus braunii, and Coelastrella vacuolata) and four cyanobacterial species (Arthrospira platensis, Nostoc muscorum, Chlorogloeopsis fritschii, and Synechocystis sp.) were screened for growth and PHA accumulation. Cultivation was performed under autotrophic conditions, mixotrophic growth with acetate, mixotrophic growth in anaerobic digestion effluent, and nitrogen-depleted conditions. Arthrospira platensis showed the highest PHA content under autotrophic growth, reaching 4.3% w/w. Most species adapted successfully to anaerobic digestion effluent, achieving total nitrogen and phosphorus removal above 90% in most cases, although PHA accumulation remained low (0.6–1.3% w/w). Acetate supplementation and nitrogen limitation markedly enhanced PHA accumulation. Mixotrophic cultivation with acetate yielded up to 10.2% w/w in cyanobacteria, whereas nitrogen starvation increased accumulation further, with Synechocystis sp. reaching 14.4% w/w. Overall, cyanobacteria outperformed green microalgae, supporting their potential for sustainable bioplastic production. These findings provide a basis for species selection and future process optimization.
W7222996889.title: Microalgae and Cyanobacteria Species Valorization Towards Sustainable Bioplastics Production

W7223005727.abstract: Hexavalent chromium (Cr(VI)) is a highly toxic and mobile heavy metal pollutant. Developing efficient, low-cost, and sustainable adsorbents for Cr(VI) removal from wastewater is urgently needed. In this study, wet okara (soybean-processing residue) was used as a biomass precursor to fabricate porous biochar via one-step microwave-assisted KOH/K 2 CO 3 activation. The synergistic activation effect of dual alkalis, together with the rapid volumetric heating provided by microwave treatment, enabled the simultaneous construction of abundant micropores and mesopores. The optimized biochar, denoted as BC-KOH + K 2 CO 3 , exhibited a high specific surface area of 941 m 2 ·g −1 , a total pore volume of 0.44 cm 3 ·g −1 , and a micropore volume of 0.31 cm 3 ·g −1 , indicating the successful formation of a micropore-dominated hierarchical porous structure. Batch adsorption experiments demonstrated that BC-KOH + K 2 CO 3 displayed excellent Cr(VI) removal performance from a 100 mg/L solution under acidic conditions, achieving a maximum adsorption capacity of 250.74 mg·g −1 at pH = 1. The adsorption capacity reached 230.8 mg·g −1 at pH = 2 in the first adsorption cycle and remained at 107.7 mg·g −1 in the fourth adsorption cycle, and showed strong resistance to interference from common coexisting ions. The dual-alkali activation strategy also improved the adsorption performance of biochars derived from other biomass precursors (rice husk and bran), demonstrating preliminary cross-feedstock transferability at the adsorption-performance level. This work provides a rapid, energy-efficient, and generalizable approach for converting agricultural and food-processing wastes into high-performance biochar adsorbents for heavy metal-contaminated wastewater remediation.
