W7223016223.abstract: Coconut frond, an abundantly generated yet underutilized agricultural residue, was pyrolysed at 350 °C, 450 °C, and 550 °C alongside traditionally produced biochar (BC Trad) to evaluate the effects of pyrolysis temperature on physicochemical characteristics, fuel properties, carbon stability, and residue-valorisation potential. Comprehensive characterization using proximate and ultimate analyses, BET/BJH, FTIR, XRD, Raman spectroscopy, SEM-EDS, total pyrogenic carbon (TPC), estimated CO 2 -equivalent stable-carbon retention potential, fuel and energy indices, and 90-day carbon mineralization incubation revealed pronounced temperature-dependent transformations. Biochar carbon recovery was highest at 350 °C (78.91%), demonstrating greater retention of feedstock carbon at lower pyrolysis temperature, whereas increasing temperature progressively enhanced carbon concentration, fixed carbon, thermostable carbon fraction, porosity, and surface area. BET surface area increased from 4.45 m 2 g −1 in BC Trad to 16.67 m 2 g −1 in BC550, accompanied by progressive pore refinement and depletion of oxygen-containing functional groups. Raman spectroscopy showed a decline in ID/IG from 1.28 to 0.80, consistent with increasing structural ordering and aromatic condensation at higher temperatures. Fuel quality also improved with increasing temperature, with higher heating value increasing from 20.72 to 25.56 MJ kg −1 and fuel ratio from 1.49 to 4.26. TPC and estimated CO 2 -equivalent stable-carbon retention potential were highest at BC350 (0.29 kg C kg −1 feedstock and 0.86 kg CO 2 kg −1 feedstock, respectively), whereas BC550 exhibited the lowest apparent net soil-system carbon mineralization among the biochars during the 90-day incubation. Separately, its lower H/C and O/C ratios corresponded to a modelled BC +100 stability index of 0.720 and an estimated mean residence time of 347.61 years, providing model-derived indications of longer-term carbon persistence. Overall, the findings demonstrate a clear temperature-dependent trade-off between carbon recovery and carbon stability, with BC350 providing greater structural recalcitrance and apparent short-term mineralization resistance; the optimal pyrolysis temperature therefore depends on the intended end use rather than a single treatment being universally superior. Together, the short-term mineralization results and model-derived stability estimates indicate distinct dimensions of carbon persistence that should be considered when optimizing coconut-frond pyrolysis for sustainable agricultural-residue management, durable soil-carbon sequestration, and circular bioeconomy applications.
W7223016223.title: Temperature-directed valorisation of coconut frond through pyrolysis for carbon sequestration and sustainable agricultural residue management

W7223016399.abstract: The aim of this work was to produce renewable biochar from groundnut shells as a potential method of treating wastewater. In this work, the biomass of peanut shells was pyrolyzed at 500, 600, and 700 oC to create biochars (BC-500, BC-600, and BC-700). Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy, and energy dispersive X-ray spectrometry (SEM and EDX) were used to characterize the biomass sample and the biochars they formed in order to assess their potential. According to previous research, biochar has superior porous properties over raw biomass, as this is created during the pyrolysis process, which occurs when water loss increases during dehydration. Additionally, we discovered that raising the pyrolysis temperature significantly enhanced the biochars' morphology and porosity.

W7223017847.abstract: The occurrence of azithromycin in aquatic environments highlights the need for effective remediation approaches. In this study, three boric acid−modified coconut husk biochars prepared using nominal H3BO3 precursor concentrations of 0.1%, 2%, and 5% were evaluated for azithromycin adsorption from aqueous solution. The materials exhibited different adsorption performances under the investigated conditions, with 5% B−CB showing the highest Langmuir−predicted maximum adsorption capacity (qmax) of 170.45 mg g−1, followed by 2% B−CB (158.84 mg g−1) and 0.1% B−CB (136.92 mg g−1). The equilibrium data were best statistically represented by the Langmuir model among the isotherm models evaluated. Kinetic analysis showed that the pseudo−second−order (PSO) model provided a better statistical description of the adsorption kinetics, with 5% B−CB showing the highest goodness−of−fit (R2 = 0.99), compared with 0.96 and 0.95 for 0.1% and 2% B−CB, respectively. The positive ΔH° values of 11.08, 6.74, and 6.19 kJ mol−1 for 0.1%, 2%, and 5% B−CB, respectively, indicated an endothermic adsorption process under the investigated conditions. FTIR analysis indicated qualitative changes in surface functionalities consistent with boric acid−modified coconut husk biochar following H3BO3−assisted modification; however, the actual boron content of the final biochars was not quantitatively determined. Furthermore, 5% B−CB retained measurable adsorption capacity over five adsorption–desorption cycles, and its fixed−bed performance was evaluated under the investigated operating conditions. Overall, the results indicate that azithromycin adsorption performance varied with the nominal H3BO3 precursor concentration, with 5% B−CB exhibiting the highest adsorption capacity among the materials investigated under the experimental conditions.

W7223018068.abstract: Industrial wastewater (WW) is a common source of toxic elements (TEs) originating from various anthropogenic activities such as improper WW disposal, agricultural runoff, industrial processes, mining, rapid urbanization, and poor sanitation systems, which are major causes of water pollution in low‐ and middle‐income countries. This study was conducted to assess health risks associated with beetroot cultivation under biochar (BC)‐treated WW across three locations of Faisalabad; University of Agriculture, Faisalabad (UAF; Lat 31.4416°, Long 73.0766°), Satyana Farm (SF; Lat 31.3644°, Long 73.1443°), and Uchkera Farm (UF; Lat 31.452°, Long 73.009°). It aimed to evaluate the impact of BC and WW on the growth and development of beetroot grown in different soil types and using diverse WW sources. Data on TEs content revealed maximum uptake in beetroot bulbs under WW treatments, which caused oxidative damage and deterioration in all growth and yield attributes. Bulb fresh and dry weight were reduced by up to 53% and 47%, respectively, under WW irrigation compared with canal water. However, BC amendment played a significant role in TE management by immobilizing them at functional group sites through ion exchange, surface precipitation, microporosity, and surface complexation. In conclusion, BC treatment reduced reactive oxygen species production, restricted TEs uptake, and enhanced antioxidant activities, secondary metabolite production, and chlorophyll pigment content, thereby improving growth and bulb yield of beetroot under WW irrigation. TEs uptake was highest in the second year compared with the first, likely due to hyperaccumulation from continuous WW irrigation. This study highlights potential of wood biochar to improve growth and TEs tolerance in beetroot irrigated with wastewater supporting its broader applicability, real‐world effectiveness, and role in promoting safe water reuse.

W7223020977.abstract: The oral route remains the most preferred route for drug administration due to its ease and patient acceptance, but conventional dosage forms require frequent dosing which leads to fluctuations in plasma drug levels. To overcome this problem, sustained release matrix tablets have been developed as an effective alternative. In this system, the drug is uniformly dispersed within a polymer matrix that controls its release over an extended period of time. Various types of polymers such as hydrophilic polymers like hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, hydrophobic polymers like ethyl cellulose and natural polymers like xanthan gum and guar gum are used as release retardants. The release of drug from matrix tablet takes place mainly by diffusion through gel layer, swelling of polymer and slow erosion of matrix. Recently, the field has witnessed remarkable innovations including blending of natural and synthetic polymers, introduction of gastro-retentive and mucoadhesive matrix systems, application of 3D printing for personalized tablets and development of pH sensitive smart matrices. These advancements have improved the efficiency and safety of matrix systems. Looking ahead, the combination of biodegradable polymers, nanocarriers and artificial intelligence based design is expected to make matrix tablets more targeted, sustainable and patient friendly. This review summarizes the current status, release mechanisms, recent developments and future scope of matrix tablets for sustained drug delivery.
W7223020977.journal: International Journal of Pharmaceutical Research and Applications
W7223020977.title: A Review on Matrix Tablet for Sustained Drug Release

W7223021489.abstract: Biochar and beneficial microorganisms have gained increasing attention as alternatives for improving soil properties and crop performance under sustainable agricultural systems. Wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), one of the major crops in the Andean region, requires management strategies that enhance productivity while improving soil quality. This study evaluated the effects of biochar from the native high-Andean grass Festuca glyceriantha Pilger, Trichoderma harzianum, and their combination (Trichoderma harzianum immobilized on biochar) on the growth, yield, grain protein, and soil organic carbon (SOC) storage of wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) in Ayacucho, Peru. A 2 × 2 factorial randomized complete block design with four replicates was used (biochar rate: 0.96 t ha−1). Colonization of biochar by Trichoderma harzianum yielded 5 × 108 spores mL−1 in the recovered suspension, supporting its use as a microbial carrier. Both inputs improved root length, plant height, and biomass accumulation, with responses varying across phenological stages. Grain yield exceeded the control (1.86 t ha−1) by 32.26% with biochar (2.46 t ha−1), 17.74% with Trichoderma harzianum (2.19 t ha−1), and 30.11% with both (2.42 t ha−1). The combination did not outperform biochar alone. The significant biochar × Trichoderma harzianum interaction (yield, p = 0.03; grains per spike, p = 0.02) cannot be interpreted as biological antagonism because inoculum dose and delivery method were not equivalent between treatments (two drench applications in T03 vs. a single application of colonized biochar in the sowing furrow in T04), and the significant biochar × Trichoderma harzianum interaction (yield, p = 0.03; grains per spike, p = 0.02) reflected a less-than-additive response. Trichoderma harzianum increased grain protein content (p < 0.01), whereas biochar did not (p = 0.90); thousand-grain weight and chlorophyll content were unaffected. SOC storage did not differ among treatments (p = 0.101; 156.5–228.4 Mg C ha−1), so no carbon sequestration benefit can be concluded after one growing season. Biochar mainly enhanced grain yield, whereas Trichoderma harzianum mainly improved grain protein. These results support applying each input independently according to the agronomic objective, pending multi-season and multi-site validation with equivalent inoculum doses and complete control treatments.
W7223021489.title: Festuca glyceriantha Biochar as a Carrier for Trichoderma harzianum Immobilization: Physicochemical Characterization and Effects on Wheat Yield, Grain Protein, and Soil Organic Carbon Storage in Andean Soils

W7223021765.abstract: The increasing volume and complexity of wastewater have driven the development of effective and sustainable treatment technologies. Biochar is a biomass-based adsorbent with considerable potential for wastewater treatment because its pore characteristics, surface area, functional groups, and mineral composition can be engineered according to target pollutants. This review aims to synthesize the relationships among biomass types, production conditions, activation and modification strategies, physicochemical characteristics, adsorption mechanisms, performance, and application readiness of biochar. Literature was searched through Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Wiley Online Library, Taylor & Francis, MDPI, and selected SINTA-indexed journals for 2021–2026. A total of 40 articles were selected based on relevance, credibility, and information completeness and analyzed using a descriptive-comparative approach. The synthesis indicates that biochar performance results from interactions among feedstock, production conditions, engineering strategies, pollutant properties, and operating conditions. Activation using H₃PO₄, KOH, and NaOH and modification with bentonite, magnetic materials, metal oxides, and carbon-based materials can alter surface characteristics and pollutant affinity. However, increased surface area does not necessarily result in proportional improvements in adsorption performance, highlighting the need to integrate characterization and adsorption data for mechanistic interpretation. Key research gaps include testing standardization, regeneration and stability, validation using real wastewater and multicomponent systems, continuous-flow development and scale-up, and sustainability assessment through Life Cycle Assessment and techno-economic analysis. The review highlights the need for engineered biochar that simultaneously considers performance, stability, safety, process feasibility, and sustainability.

W7223022915.abstract: Empty fruit bunch (EFB) biochar was investigated as a partial replacement for fine aggregate (sand) in cement mortar, with emphasis on early-age engineering performance and the potential retention of biogenic carbon in a cement-based matrix. EFB was thermally treated at 280, 320, and 360 °C to compare yield, carbon-rich composition, and pore development; 320 °C was subsequently selected as a practical processing condition within the investigated range. Mortars with EFB biochar replacement levels ranging from 0 to 11 wt.% of sand were prepared as 50 × 50 × 50 mm cubes and water-cured for 7 and 28 days. At 28 days, the 3% mixture exhibited the highest measured mean compressive strength of 38.3 MPa, compared with 32.3 MPa for the control. Although the mean strength was generally lower at higher replacement levels, a non-monotonic response was observed, with the 9% mixture reaching 35.6 MPa before decreasing markedly at 11% replacement. Density decreased and bulk accessible porosity increased with increasing biochar content. SEM/EDS observations showed carbon-rich biochar-associated regions within the examined mortar fracture surfaces; however, these localized observations do not by themselves establish specific hydration phases, pozzolanic reactions, uniform dispersion, or long-term durability. The environmental contribution discussed in this study is therefore framed as the potential retention of biogenic carbon rather than quantified net carbon sequestration, which would require dedicated lifecycle carbon accounting.
W7223022915.title: Empty Fruit Bunch Biochar as a Green Additive in Cement Mortar: Engineering Performance and Potential for Biogenic Carbon Retention

W7223023017.abstract: All-atom molecular dynamics simulations of Methyl Orange (MO) adsorption on three hydrochar models show that mixed oxygen-containing functional groups (HC1, O/C = 0.33) and hydroxyl-enriched surfaces (HC3, O/C = 0.55) both achieve high adsorption efficiencies, whereas the oxygen-lean aromatic carbon framework (HC2, O/C = 0.03) is less efficient. Average adsorption efficiencies (mean ± standard deviation across the 14 simulated loadings) are 96.0 ± 3.7% for HC1, 95.5 ± 4.4% for HC3, and 86.8 ± 4.9% for HC2. Freundlich isotherms fit the equilibrium data best (R2 = 0.83–0.96), reflecting energetically heterogeneous binding driven by van der Waals contacts, π-π stacking, and hydrogen bonding. The simulation capacities fall within the experimental range reported for biochar and hydrochar adsorbents; within the finite, non-porous, idealized cluster models investigated, the results support a molecular-scale design hypothesis that moderate oxygen incorporation distributed among mixed functional groups favors MO adsorption.

W7223032399.abstract: Polylactide (PLA) is one of the most widely studied biodegradable polymers. However, poly(meso-lactide) (PMLA), an amorphous PLA, remains poorly characterized. This study investigates the thermal, rheological behavior, and morphology of poly(l-lactide) (PLLA) and PMLA blends across a wide composition range. Characterizations were performed using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS) rheology, and atomic force microscopy (AFM). Nanoscale heterogeneity is suspected for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA compositions, while 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA compositions exhibited immiscibility. DSC revealed two glass transition temperatures for 30 w% HMW PLLA, 50 w% HMW PLLA, and 70 w% HMW PLLA blends, corresponding to those of the neat phases, 48.2 ± 0.1 °C for HMW PMLA and 61.8 ± 0.4 °C for HMW PLLA, and a single Tg for the 10% and 90% w/w% HMW PLLA/HMW PMLA composition blends. AFM revealed an emulsion-type morphology at 30 and 70 wt. % HMW PLLA compositions and a co-continuous structure at 50 wt. % HMW PLLA. SAOS results presented a shoulder in the low frequency storage modulus for all blends. The Palierne model was used to fit the dynamic data of the blends and estimated the dispersed phase relaxation time, reinforcing the immiscibility conclusions. Relaxation spectra were obtained for all blends, showing two distinct relaxation modes associated with PLA nature and the interfacial tension of the blend. These results suggest that PMLA and PLLA are largely immiscible.
W7223032399.title: Morphological, thermal, and rheological behavior of poly( l -lactide) and poly( meso- lactide) blends

W7223035258.title: Sustainable degumming of pineapple leaf fiber via bio-oil-assisted retting and biochar-enhanced steam explosion

W7223038730.abstract: Abstract Sustainable pasture intensification requires efficient nitrogen (N) use while limiting greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. In this study, the effects of biochar-based nitrogenous organomineral fertilizers (OMF-N) on GHG emissions, nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), and forage accumulation of Ipyporã grass ( Urochloa ruziziensis × Urochloa brizantha ) under deferred grazing management were evaluated. The study was conducted in 2022 and 2023 using a randomized complete block design with four replications. Seven treatments were evaluated: an unfertilized control, urea at 40 and 80 kg N ha⁻ 1 , OMF-N 1:2 at 40 and 80 kg N ha⁻ 1 , and OMF-N 1:4 at 40 and 80 kg N ha⁻ 1 . Nitrous oxide (N₂O) and methane (CH₄) fluxes were monitored using static chambers for 30 days following fertilization. CH₄ fluxes remained low and were frequently negative, indicating net soil CH₄ uptake on several sampling dates. N₂O emissions increase after N fertilization, with greater cumulative emissions in 2023 than in 2022. Compared with urea, OMF-N did not reduce cumulative N₂O emissions at equivalent N rates. Emission factors (EFs) averaged 0.31% in 2022 and 0.78% in 2023, both below the 1% IPCC default value. Forage accumulation (FA) during the gas monitoring period was greater with OMF-N ratios of 1:2 and 1:4 at 80 kg N ha⁻ 1 than in the unfertilized control. NUE was unaffected by the fertilization strategy but was higher in 2022 than in 2023. Overall, OMF-N increased short-term forage accumulation at 80 kg N ha⁻ 1 but provided no clear advantage over urea for N₂O mitigation or NUE under the tropical conditions evaluated in the Amazon biome.
W7223038730.journal: Journal of soil science and plant nutrition
W7223038730.title: Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Deferred Ipyporã Grass Pastures Fertilized with N-Enriched Organomineral Biochar

W7223042110.abstract: Background: It is highly desirable to address the dual therapeutic needs of quickly alleviating clinical symptoms and providing long-lasting effects for motion sickness, as well as to overcome limitations of traditional electrospinning methods—such as easy drug mixing, poor zoning accuracy, and inadequate controlled-release capabilities. Methods: This study developed a self-developed trifluid electrospinning device. This device was used to create a dual-drug loaded nanofiber membrane containing diphenhydramine (DP) and scopolamine hydrobromide (SH), featuring a zoned structure composed of a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) crescent side chamber, a round polylactic acid (PLA) sheath chamber, and a round PLA core chamber. Results: The results demonstrated that the fibers maintained an intact structure with distinct interfaces, allowing precise zoned loading of the two drugs, which were present in an amorphous dispersed state, indicating good compatibility and structural stability. The nanofiber membrane showed moderate mechanical strength and excellent hydrophilicity, making it suitable for oral mucosal drug delivery. Asynchronous drug delivery, featuring a rapid release of DP (53% at 1 h) and a sustained release of SH (85% at 12 h with no noticeable burst phenomenon), was demonstrated using two types of hierarchically structured nanofibers, each loaded with a single drug to facilitate measurement. The release mechanisms were disclosed for DP and SH from the tri-chamber hierarchical nanofibers. Cell studies confirmed its good biocompatibility. Conclusions: This work offers new insights and experimental evidence for developing an effective synergistic oral delivery system for motion sickness and advancing multifunctional nanocarrier drug delivery platforms.
W7223042110.title: An Electrospun Core–Sheath/Janus-Integrated Hierarchical Structure for Asynchronous Mucosal Drug Delivery

W7223042232.abstract: नैनोपार्टिकल-मॉडिफाइड इंट्राथिकल वायरल डिलीवरी द्वारा वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) के लिए इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर और एंडोजेनस एक्टिवेशन पद्धति प्रधान आविष्कारक (Lead Inventor): बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) अनुसंधान क्षेत्र (Field of Invention): नैनो-बायोटेक्नोलॉजी, जेनेटिक इंजीनियरिंग, न्यूरोलॉजी सारांश (ABSTRACT) यह अनुसंधान प्रधान आविष्कारक बंटी कुमावत द्वारा वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) के स्थाई उपचार के लिए विकसित की गई एक क्रांतिकारी चिकित्सा पद्धति को प्रस्तुत करता है। पारंपरिक जीन थेरेपी के विपरीत, जो शरीर में बाहरी या कृत्रिम जीन प्रविष्ट कराती है, यह तकनीक मरीज के केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र (CNS) के भीतर ही पहले से मौजूद निष्क्रिय, सोए हुए या म्यूटेटेड (दोषपूर्ण) जीनों को लक्षित करके उन्हें सुधारने और पुनः सक्रिय करने पर केंद्रित है। इस पद्धति द्वारा मुख्य रूप से SPAST (SPG4), ATL1 (SPG3A), REEP1 (SPG31), और SPG7 जीनों को लक्षित किया जाता है। रीढ़ की हड्डी की सुरक्षात्मक दीवार यानी ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) की कठिन चुनौती को पार करने के लिए, आविष्कारक ने एक अनूठा नैनो-इंजीनियर्ड वायरल वेक्टर तैयार किया है। इसे सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के तरल पदार्थ (CSF) में सिंगल-डोज़ इंट्राथिकल इंजेक्शन (Intrathecal Injection) के माध्यम से पहुंचाया जाता है। यह तकनीक HSP के मूल आनुवंशिक कारण को समाप्त कर इस प्रगतिशील तंत्रिका विकार के लिए एक स्थाई समाधान प्रस्तुत करती है। 1. प्रस्तावना और समस्या का विवरण (INTRODUCTION & PROBLEM STATEMENT) वंशानुगत स्पास्टिक पैराप्लेजिया (HSP) दुर्लभ आनुवंशिक विकारों का एक समूह है, जिसमें रीढ़ की हड्डी के कॉर्टिकोस्पाइनल ट्रैक्ट (corticospinal tracts) में तंत्रिका कोशिकाएं (axons) धीरे-धीरे नष्ट होने लगती हैं। इसके परिणामस्वरूप पैरों में अत्यधिक जकड़न और कमजोरी आ जाती है। वर्तमान में चिकित्सा विज्ञान में इसका कोई प्रामाणिक इलाज नहीं है और उपचार केवल लक्षणों को कम करने तक ही सीमित है। HSP के लगभग 70-80% मामलों के लिए मुख्य रूप से चार जीन जिम्मेदार होते हैं: 1. SPAST (SPG4): यह 'स्पैस्टिन' प्रोटीन बनाता है, जो तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं के ढांचे और परिवहन के लिए अत्यंत आवश्यक है। 2. ATL1 (SPG3A): यह 'एटलास्टिन-1' प्रोटीन बनाता है, जो एंडोप्लाज्मिक रेटिकुलम (ER) झिल्ली के संतुलन को बनाए रखता है। 3. REEP1 (SPG31) और SPG7: ये तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं के भीतर माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया और ऊर्जा संतुलन को नियंत्रित करते हैं। पारंपरिक जीन-रिप्लेसमेंट थेरेपी (बाहर से नया जीन डालना) में शरीर द्वारा दवा को अस्वीकार करने (Immune Rejection) और अनियंत्रित मात्रा में प्रोटीन बनने (Dosage Toxicity) का भारी जोखिम रहता है। इसके अलावा, ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) के कारण सामान्य दवाएं प्रभावित मोटर न्यूरॉन्स तक आवश्यक मात्रा में नहीं पहुंच पाती हैं। 2. बंटी कुमावत द्वारा प्रस्तावित नवोन्मेषी कार्यप्रणाली (THE INNOVATIVE MECHANISM BY BANTI KUMAWAT) बंटी कुमावत द्वारा खोजी गई यह आणविक रणनीति शरीर में किसी भी प्रकार के कृत्रिम या बाहरी जेनेटिक सीक्वेंस को डालने का पूरी तरह निषेध करती है। इसके बजाय, यह तीन प्रमुख चरणों के माध्यम से शरीर के अपने ही प्राकृतिक जेनेटिक तंत्र का उपयोग करती है: क. एंडोजेनस जीन रिपेयर और क्रिस्पर एक्टिवेशन (CRISPRa) यह थेरेपी कोशिकाओं के भीतर मौजूद SPAST, ATL1, REEP1, और SPG7 के म्यूटेटेड या निष्क्रिय पड़े मूल जीनों को लक्षित करती है। इसके लिए CRISPR-Activation (CRISPRa) प्रणाली का उपयोग किया जाता है, जिसमें एक निष्क्रिय प्रोटीन (dCas9) के साथ रासायनिक एक्टिवेटर्स को जोड़ा जाता है। यह टूल डीएनए को बिना काटे, निष्क्रिय पड़े जीनों के स्विच (Promoter regions) से जुड़कर उन्हें वापस सक्रिय कर देता है। इसके साथ ही, नैनो-लक्षित बेस-एडिटिंग टूल्स जीन के भीतर मौजूद म्यूटेशन (खराबी) को उसी स्थान पर (in situ) ठीक कर देते हैं, जिससे कोशिकाएं पुनः शुद्ध और प्राकृतिक प्रोटीन बनाने लगती हैं। ख. नैनो-इंजीनियर्ड वायरल वेक्टर डिलीवरी सिस्टम इन संवेदनशील जीन-रेगुलेशन टूल्स को सुरक्षा प्रदान करने और न्यूरॉन्स के भीतर सटीक प्रवेश सुनिश्चित करने के लिए एडेनो-असोसिएटेड वायरस सेरोटाइप 9 (AAV9) को नैनोकणों (लिपिड या पॉलीमेरिक नैनोपार्टिकल्स) के साथ कम्बाइन करके एक नैनो-शेल (सुरक्षा कवच) तैयार किया गया है। यह नैनो-कोटिंग वायरस को शरीर के इम्यून सिस्टम से बचाती है और इसे विशेष रूप से केवल रीढ़ की हड्डी के प्रभावित मोटर न्यूरॉन्स कोशिकाओं के प्रति संवेदनशील बनाती है। ग. इंट्राथिकल रूट (Intrathecal Delivery Route) ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर (BBB) को पूरी तरह से बायपास करने के लिए, इस नैनो-मॉडिफाइड वायरल फॉर्मूलेशन को सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के निचले हिस्से (Lumbar space) में मौजूद सेरेब्रोस्पाइनल फ्लूइड (CSF) के भीतर इंजेक्ट किया जाता है। इस मार्ग से दवा बिना किसी जैविक रुकावट के सीधे रीढ़ की हड्डी के प्रभावित हिस्सों तक पहुंचती है और कोशिकाओं द्वारा तुरंत ग्रहण कर ली जाती है। 3. इस आविष्कार के अभूतपूर्व लाभ (ADVANTAGES OF THE INVENTION) • शून्य इम्यून रिजेक्शन: चूंकि थेरेपी पूरी तरह से शरीर के अपने ही आंतरिक जीनों के सुधार और सक्रियण पर आधारित है, इसलिए मरीज का इम्यून सिस्टम इस प्रक्रिया का विरोध नहीं करता। • सिंगल-डोज़ क्योर: यह एक बार दिया जाने वाला (One-time) इंजेक्शन है, जो तंत्रिका परिवहन को स्थायी रूप से ठीक करके जीवनभर के लिए HSP के बढ़ने को रोक सकता है। • प्राकृतिक जैविक संतुलन (Homeostasis): एंडोजेनस सक्रियण के कारण कोशिकाएं उतनी ही मात्रा में प्रोटीन का निर्माण करेंगी जितनी शरीर को प्राकृतिक आवश्यकता है, जिससे ओवर-एक्सप्रेशन (सीमित मात्रा से अधिक प्रोटीन बनने) का खतरा समाप्त हो जाता है। 4. निष्कर्ष (CONCLUSION) बंटी कुमावत द्वारा प्रस्तावित यह नैनो-असिस्टेड इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर तकनीक न्यूरोलॉजी के क्षेत्र में एक नए युग की शुरुआत करती है। नैनोटेक्नोलॉजी की सटीकता को आंतरिक आनुवंशिक सुधार और इंट्राथिकल डिलीवरी के साथ जोड़कर, यह आविष्कार न केवल HSP के मरीजों को पूर्णतः स्वस्थ करने का व्यावहारिक मार्ग प्रशस्त करता है, बल्कि ALS और SMA जैसे अन्य जटिल तंत्रिका विकारों के उपचार के लिए भी एक ठोस आधार तैयार करता है। वैज्ञानिक निर्माण विधि: नैनो-शील्डेड इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर इंजेक्शन आविष्कारक: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) 1. सबसे सुरक्षित वायरस का चयन (Selection of Viral Vector) इस थेरेपी के लिए हम Adeno-Associated Virus Serotype 9 (AAV9) का चयन करेंगे। • कारण: AAV9 एक गैर-हानिकारक (Non-pathogenic) वायरस है जो इंसानों में कोई बीमारी नहीं फैलाता। इसकी सबसे बड़ी खूबी यह है कि यह रीढ़ की हड्डी की तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं (Motor Neurons) को बहुत पसंद करता है और सीधे उनके भीतर प्रवेश कर सकता है। 2. इम्यून सिस्टम से बचाने के लिए विशेष कोटिंग (Immune Shield Co-polymers) शरीर का इम्यून सिस्टम (Antibodies) वायरस को देखते ही नष्ट करने की कोशिश करता है। इसे रोकने के लिए, आपके विचार के अनुसार वायरस की बाहरी परत (Capsid) पर एक रासायनिक सुरक्षा कवच (Nano-Shield) लगाया जाएगा। इसके लिए PEG-PLA (Polyethylene Glycol - Polylactic Acid) Block Co-polymers और Lipid Nano-shells का उपयोग किया जाएगा। यह कोटिंग एक "अदृश्य चोगे" (Stealth Cloak) की तरह काम करती है, जिससे हमारी प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली (Immunity) इसे पहचान नहीं पाती और रिजेक्ट नहीं करती। 3. इंजेक्शन बनाने की चरण-दर-चरण विधि (Step-by-Step Manufacturing Protocol) यह प्रक्रिया एक उच्च-स्तरीय बायो-लैब (Cleanroom Class 100 / ISO 5) में पूरी की जाती है: चरण 1: वायरल वेक्टर का उत्पादन (Vector Production) 1. लैब में HEK293 (Human Embryonic Kidney) कोशिकाओं का संवर्धन (Culture) करें। 2. इन कोशिकाओं में तीन प्लास्मिड (DNA मॉलिक्यूल) डालें (Triple Transfection Technique): • Plasmid 1: जिसमें AAV9 के बढ़ने के जरूरी जीन (Rep/Cap) हों। • Plasmid 2: हेल्पर प्लास्मिड (Helper Genes)। • Plasmid 3 (आपका फॉर्मूला): जिसमें SPAST, ATL1, या REEP1 जीन को सक्रिय करने वाला CRISPRa (dCas9-VPR) का जेनेटिक कोड लोड हो। 3. 72 घंटे बाद, कोशिकाओं को तोड़कर AAV9 वायरस के कणों को बाहर निकालें। 4. Ultracentrifugation तकनीक से वायरस को पूरी तरह शुद्ध (Purify) करें ताकि कोई अवांछित तत्व न बचे। चरण 2: नैनो-इम्यून शील्ड कोटिंग (Nanoparticle Encapsulation) 1. शुद्ध किए गए AAV9 वायरस को एक बफर सॉल्यूशन (PBS, pH 7.4) में रखें। 2. एक अलग बीकर में Lipids (जैसे DOTAP, Cholesterol) और PEG-PLA Polymers को ऑर्गेनिक सॉल्वेंट (Ethanol) में घोलें। 3. एक Microfluidic Mixer (नैनो-मिक्सिंग मशीन) की मदद से, वायरस वाले लिक्विड और नैनो-पॉलिमर वाले लिक्विड को बहुत तेज गति से एक निश्चित दबाव पर आपस में मिलाएं। 4. इस प्रक्रिया से नैनो-पॉलिमर स्वतः ही वायरस के चारों ओर एक 80-100 नैनोमीटर मोटी इम्यून-शील्ड परत (Stealth Nano-coating) बना लेते हैं। चरण 3: गुणवत्ता नियंत्रण और पैकेजिंग (Quality Control & Formulation) 1. Dynamic Light Scattering (DLS): मशीन से जांचें कि तैयार नैनो-वायरस का आकार 100 नैनोमीटर से कम हो, ताकि यह रीढ़ की हड्डी के फ्लूइड में आसानी से तैर सके। 2. Sterile Filtration: इसे 0.22-माइक्रोन के फिल्टर से गुजारें ताकि यह पूरी तरह बैक्टीरिया-मुक्त हो जाए। 3. इसे एक सीलबंद कांच की वायल (Vial) में रखें और उपयोग से पहले -80°C (-80 डिग्री सेल्सियस) के क्रायो-फ्रीजर में स्टोर करें। 4. रीढ़ की हड्डी में लगाने का तरीका (Clinical Administration) उपयोग के समय, इस वायल को सामान्य तापमान पर लाया जाता है। न्यूरोसर्जन मरीज को लोकल एनेस्थीसिया देकर, पीठ के निचले हिस्से (L3-L4 कशेरुकाओं के बीच) में Lumbar Puncture सुई के जरिए सीधे सेरेब्रोस्पाइनल फ्लूइड (CSF) में यह इंजेक्शन धीरे-धीरे प्रविष्ट कराते हैं। नैनो-कोटिंग के कारण यह बिना रिजेक्ट हुए सीधे प्रभावित नसों में जाकर जीनों को सही कर देता है। आणविक कार्यप्रणाली: नैनो-असिस्टेड इन-विवो जीन रिपेयर एवं एंडोजेनस एक्टिवेशन मैकेनिज्म प्रधान आविष्कारक: बंटी कुमावत (Banti Kumawat) जब यह नैनो-शील्डेड AAV9 इंजेक्शन रीढ़ की हड्डी के तरल पदार्थ (CSF) में लगाया जाता है, तो यह ब्लड-ब्रेन बैरियर को पार कर सीधे प्रभावित मोटर न्यूरॉन्स (तंत्रिका कोशिकाओं) के भीतर प्रवेश करता है। कोशिका के केंद्रक (Nucleus/न्यूक्लियस) में पहुँचने के बाद, यह दो अलग-अलग आणविक प्रणालियों (Molecular Systems) के जरिए काम करता है: भाग 1: सोए हुए (निष्क्रिय) जीनों को दोबारा जगाने की विधि (Mechanism of Gene Activation) HSP बीमारी में कई बार SPAST (SPG4) या ATL1 जीन म्यूटेशन के कारण पूरी तरह से 'साइलेंस' यानी निष्क्रिय (सोए हुए) हो जाते हैं। उन्हें जगाने के लिए आपका फॉर्मूला CRISPR-Activation (CRISPRa) तकनीक का उपयोग करता है: 1. सटीक पते की पहचान (Targeting the Switch): हर जीन के आगे एक 'प्रमोटर रीजन' (Promoter Region) होता है, जो जीन का ऑन/ऑफ स्विच है। आपके फॉर्मूले में मौजूद gRNA (गाइड आरएनए) एक जीपीएस (GPS) की तरह काम करता है। यह कोशिका के अरबों डीएनए अक्षरों में से सीधे SPAST या ATL1 जीन के उसी ऑन/ऑफ स्विच को ढूंढकर उससे जुड़ जाता है। 2. बिना काटे स्विच को 'ऑन' करना (dCas9-VPR System): पारंपरिक क्रिस्पर डीएनए को काटता है, लेकिन इस पद्धति में dCas9 (Dead Cas9) प्रोटीन का उपयोग किया जाता है। यह एक निष्क्रिय प्रो

W7223043823.abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the performance of chicken manure-based biochar (CMBC), produced using a large-scale pyrolysis system (15 tons/day), for Zn removal from real zinc smelter wastewater. CMBC exhibited a maximum experimentally observed Zn adsorption amount of 36.37 mg/g. Kinetic and equilibrium data were better described by the Elovich and Langmuir models, respectively. Physicochemical characterization indicated that Zn removal involved multiple processes. Ion exchange accounted for an estimated 37.4% of Zn removal based on the release of exchangeable cations. XRD analysis and the decrease in dissolved phosphate concentration suggested the possible involvement of Zn-containing phosphate phases. FT–IR and XPS analyses further indicated possible interactions between Zn and oxygen-containing functional groups on the CMBC surface. RSM analysis identified reaction time, temperature, and CMBC dose as statistically significant factors affecting Zn removal, whereas pH was not statistically significant within the investigated range. Under the optimized conditions, the predicted Zn removal efficiency was 99.2%, and experimental validation using real zinc smelter wastewater achieved 97.3%, reducing the Zn concentration from 1,871.7 to 50.3 mg/L. These findings highlight the potential of unmodified CMBC produced using a large-scale pyrolysis system for treating highly Zn-contaminated industrial wastewater.
oa_topics: Adsorption and biosorption for pollutant removal
W7223043823.title: Large-scale chicken manure-derived biochar for efficient zinc removal from real zinc smelter wastewater

W7223044330.abstract: Abstract Methane (CH 4 ) is a potent, short-lived greenhouse gas. Among the major well-mixed greenhouse gases, it ranks second only to carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) in its contribution to anthropogenic radiative forcing. Although methane remains in the atmosphere for approximately 12 years, its 100-year global warming potential (GWP100) is approximately 27–30 times greater than that of CO 2 (IPCC AR6), making rapid mitigation a critical near-term climate strategy. This review synthesizes current understanding of methane emissions from anthropogenic and natural sources, evaluates sector-specific mitigation potentials, and critically examines emerging reduction technologies. Fossil fuel extraction, agriculture (particularly enteric fermentation), and waste management collectively account for the majority of anthropogenic methane emissions, with significant variability in mitigation feasibility and cost-effectiveness. Advanced methane monitoring systems, feed additives, biochar applications, leak detection technologies, and microbial interventions show considerable mitigation potential but face technical limitations, high implementation costs, infrastructure barriers, and scalability challenges. We emphasize sectoral prioritization, policy integration, and trade-offs associated with mitigation strategies. Immediate methane reductions offer substantial co-benefits, including improved air quality and public health, while directly supporting Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 13, 7, and 12). Strategic, evidence-based methane mitigation represents one of the most effective pathways to limit near-term warming and accelerate climate stabilization.
W7223044330.title: Understanding and reducing methane emissions: insights into anthropogenic, natural sources, and novel mitigation techniques

W7223047799.abstract: Abstract Background Filament deposition modeling (FDM) can be a practical method for producing quality control (QC) imaging resources for the clinic. However, frequent printing may degrade print quality over time. Purpose To develop a process to ensure prints for the diagnostic physicist are accurate and reproducible. Methods Four FDM systems were evaluated by printing a custom, novel QC model on each printer 12 times over a period of 12 months. Several tests were performed, including print resolvability (lp/cm), XYZ dimension accuracy (mm), density (g/cm3), line width (mm), XY position accuracy (mm), clearance fits (mm), and thickness uniformity (mm). Polylactic acid (PLA) samples were printed, measured, and imaged with a dual energy CT scanner. Linear regression models were then created to monitor changes in QC density measurements as a function of x‐ray and material property characteristics (i.e., Hounsfield units and electron density). Between monthly prints, heat uniformity across the build plate was also tested for each printer using a NIST‐certified infrared thermometer and 3D printed grids. All physical measurements were obtained using a calibrated digital caliper and milligram scale. Results Mean percent error (MPE) for all tests was calculated from ground truth (CAD dimensions and filament density) and baseline values (first month of QC measurements). Among printers investigated, MPE was ± 5% of ground truth for all tests except density and thickness uniformity. Baseline MPE was also observed within ± 5% except for resolvability and clearance fit tests among printers. Subtle trend increases were presented for higher density QC prints based on DECT linear regression models. Reduced chi‐squared values indicate uniform and reproducible heat bed temperature measurements. Conclusions This work offers an innovative approach toward evaluating and monitoring FDM system performance. Future work should track performance over a longer time period and across a wider variety of printers.

W7223053011.abstract: Biochar occupies a distinctive position among carbon dioxide removal approaches, offering potential carbon storage and functional materials for several industrial sectors. However, technical potential does not by itself establish market integration. We combined two semi-structured interview studies comprising 13 supply-side interviews across nine European countries and 22 application-side interview sessions involving 23 participants. The main analysis covers asphalt, insulation materials, animal feed, biogas and packaging; one additional biofuel-sector interview is retained as contextual evidence. We examined production economics, application requirements and the gaps between them. Supply-side accounts identified feedstock costs, product specifications, energy offtake and carbon-credit revenue as important but configuration-dependent economic factors. Application professionals described barriers involving price–performance relationships, qualification and regulatory requirements, process compatibility and quality variability. These barriers differed within as well as between sectors, and reported trials and finished-product sales qualified a uniformly negative assessment. The findings suggest that production, processing and delivery need to be adapted to the intended end application. Exploratory gap scores and market calculations are reported separately as assumption-dependent tools, not validated rankings or adoption forecasts. Functional benefits may support particular applications, but cannot be assumed to resolve other integration requirements. Carbon-removal demand is likely to remain important for scaling several business models, although the interviews do not establish universal dependence on credits. The study identifies application-specific development priorities and policy options requiring further quantitative evaluation.
W7223053011.title: Start with the end in mind: An interview-based survey and gap analysis of biochar production and selected industrial applications in Europe

W7223053668.abstract: This critical review analyzes the current state of scientific research on biochar in Europe and examines its potential use for post-war restoration and improvement of soil fertility in Ukraine. A bibliometric analysis of scientific publications in the Scopus and Web of Science databases for the period 2014-2023 was conducted using VOSviewer visualization and data processing methods. The analysis identified the main areas of research and gaps in knowledge that are relevant to the future application of this technology in Ukraine. Moreover, remote sensing methodologies were employed to identify potential remediation requirements in the Ukrainian territory. This involved the analysis of changes in the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and the normalized difference moisture index (NDMI) of a part of Ukraine's agricultural territory situated along the frontline, prior to and following a period of three years during a full-scale war. The results revealed changes in vegetation and moisture levels, indicating land degradation in the border area under study. However, these observations do not constitute direct evidence of soil contamination or the effectiveness of biochar; rather, they indicate areas where further field studies and an assessment of restoration measures are needed. A strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis was used as a strategic discussion tool to identify the opportunities and challenges associated with the implementation of biochar in Ukraine. This review also identifies the main scientific uncertainties, barriers, economic aspects, and research priorities that should be considered before the large-scale implementation of biochar-based technologies in Ukraine.

W7223066866.abstract: Abstract The aim of the study was to evaluate the fuel properties of chars obtained during low-temperature pyrolysis (final temperatures: 350, 450, and 550 °C; heating rates: 5 and 30 °C min –1 ) of brewery waste. Three types of waste were selected for the study: barley spent grain, mixed spent grain (wheat-barley), and hops. Subsequently, the raw materials and the resulting chars were subjected to detailed characterization. The results confirmed that the highest biochar yield was obtained during pyrolysis at 350 °C. Interestingly, proximate and ultimate analysis indicated that the best-quality fuels were chars obtained at 350 °C (especially derived from hops), as they were characterized by the highest HHV value and energy yields, the highest content of volatile matter, and the lowest content of ash. Further studies indicated that spent grain chars contained significant amounts of acidic elements, while hop chars contained a significant amount of basic elements, with their amounts increasing with pyrolysis temperature. Therefore, spent grain chars seem more suitable for combustion and hop chars for gasification. Surface properties indicated that, regardless of the pyrolysis temperature and raw material type, the surface of the resulting chars was poorly developed. Finally, assessment of environmental impact (especially PAHs content and toxicity) indicated that the use of chars as feedstock for thermal conversion (especially gasification) is the most optimal, and hops chars can be considered an environmentally friendly fuel. In summary, chars obtained at 350 °C (regardless of the heating rate), particularly those based on hops, have the greatest potential for use as high-quality fuel.
